2.40.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
sucandre patite rājan rājendrāṇāṃ śiromaṇau /
tatputraḥ puṣkarākṣastu rāmaṃ yoddhumathāgataḥ //
2.40.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
सुचन्द्रे पतिते राजन् राजेन्द्राणां शिरोमणौ ।
तत्पुत्रः पुष्कराक्षस्तु रामं योद्धुमथागतः ॥
2.40.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / When Sucandra, the crest-jewel of the foremost of kings, had fallen, O king, / his son Puṣkarākṣa came forward to fight Rāma.

2.40.s:
sa rathastho mahāvīryaḥ sarvaśastrāstrakovidaḥ /
abhivīkṣya raṇetyugraṃ rāmaṃ kālātakopamam //
2.40.d:
स रथस्थो महावीर्यः सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रकोविदः ।
अभिवीक्ष्य रणेत्युग्रं रामं कालातकोपमम् ॥
2.40.m: Mounted on his chariot, endowed with great valour and skilled in all weapons and missiles, / beholding Rāma terribly fierce in battle like the god of Death,

2.40.s:
cakāra śarajālaṃ ca bhārgavendrasya sarvataḥ /
muhūrttaṃ jāmadagnyo 'pi bāṇaiḥ saṃjhadito 'bhavat //
2.40.d:
चकार शरजालं च भार्गवेन्द्रस्य सर्वतः ।
मुहूर्त्तं जामदग्न्यो ऽपि बाणैः संझदितो ऽभवत् ॥
2.40.m: he created a web of arrows around the foremost Bhārgava on all sides. / For a moment Jāmadagnya was covered with arrows.

2.40.s:
tato niṣkamya sahasā bhārgavendro mahābalaḥ /
śarabandhānmahārāja samudaikṣata sarvataḥ //
2.40.d:
ततो निष्कम्य सहसा भार्गवेन्द्रो महाबलः ।
शरबन्धान्महाराज समुदैक्षत सर्वतः ॥
2.40.m: Then, having broken out quickly from the cage of arrows, O great king, / the mighty Bhārgava looked in every direction.

2.40.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ puṣkārākṣaṃ tu sucandratanayaṃ tadā /
krodhamāhārayāmāsa didhakṣanniva pāvakaḥ //
2.40.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं पुष्काराक्षं तु सुचन्द्रतनयं तदा ।
क्रोधमाहारयामास दिधक्षन्निव पावकः ॥
2.40.m: Seeing Puṣkarākṣa, the son of Sucandra, / he gave way to anger like a fire eager to burn.

2.40.s:
sa krodhena samāviṣṭo vāruṇaṃ samavāsṛjat /
tato meghāḥ samutpannā garjanto bhairavānnavān //
2.40.d:
स क्रोधेन समाविष्टो वारुणं समवासृजत् ।
ततो मेघाः समुत्पन्ना गर्जन्तो भैरवान्नवान् ॥
2.40.m: Filled with anger, he loosed the missile of Varuṇa; / then clouds arose, roaring with fearful sounds.

2.40.s:
vavṛṣurjaladhārābhiḥ plāvayanto dharāṃ nṛpa /
puṣkarākṣo mahāvīryo vāyavyāstrumavāsṛjat //
2.40.d:
ववृषुर्जलधाराभिः प्लावयन्तो धरां नृप ।
पुष्कराक्षो महावीर्यो वायव्यास्त्रुमवासृजत् ॥
2.40.m: They rained down torrents of water, inundating the earth, O king. / The mighty Puṣkarākṣa then loosed the missile of Vāyu.

2.40.s:
tena te 'darśanaṃ nītāḥ sadya eva balāhakāḥ /
atha rāmo bhṛśaṃ kruddho brāhmaṃ tatrābhisaṃdadhe //
2.40.d:
तेन ते ऽदर्शनं नीताः सद्य एव बलाहकाः ।
अथ रामो भृशं क्रुद्धो ब्राह्मं तत्राभिसंदधे ॥
2.40.m: By that, those clouds were instantly made to disappear. / Then Rāma, fiercely enraged, fitted the missile of Brahmā.

2.40.s:
puṣkarākṣo 'pi tenaiva vicakarṣa mahābalaḥ /
brāhma so 'pyāhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā daṇḍāhata ivāragaḥ //
2.40.d:
पुष्कराक्षो ऽपि तेनैव विचकर्ष महाबलः ।
ब्राह्म सो ऽप्याहितं दृष्ट्वा दण्डाहत इवारगः ॥
2.40.m: The mighty Puṣkarākṣa also drew [his bow] with that same [missile]. / Seeing that Brahmā's missile had been warded off, [Rāma,] like a serpent struck with a stick,

2.40.s:
ghoraṃ paraśumādāya niḥśvasaṃstamadhāvata /
rāmasyādhāvatastatra puṣkarākṣo dhanurdharaḥ //
2.40.d:
घोरं परशुमादाय निःश्वसंस्तमधावत ।
रामस्याधावतस्तत्र पुष्कराक्षो धनुर्धरः ॥
2.40.m: took up his terrible battle-axe and rushed at him, hissing with fury. / As Rāma rushed forward, the archer Puṣkarākṣa

2.40.s:
saṃdadhe pañcaviśikhāndīptāsyānuragāniva /
ekaikena ca bāṇena hṛdi śīrṣe bhujadvaye //
2.40.d:
संदधे पञ्चविशिखान्दीप्तास्यानुरगानिव ।
एकैकेन च बाणेन हृदि शीर्षे भुजद्वये ॥
2.40.m: fitted five sharp arrows like fiery-mouthed serpents; / and piercing him successively with one arrow each in the chest, the head, both arms,

2.40.s:
śikhāyāṃ ca kramādbhittvā tastaṃbha bhṛśa māturam /
sa caivaṃ pīḍīto rāmaḥ puṣkarākṣeṇa saṃyuge //
2.40.d:
शिखायां च क्रमाद्भित्त्वा तस्तंभ भृश मातुरम् ।
स चैवं पीडीतो रामः पुष्कराक्षेण संयुगे ॥
2.40.m: and the crest, he stopped [Rāma], who was sorely distressed. / And thus tormented in battle by Puṣkarākṣa,

2.40.s:
kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā bhṛśaṃ dhāvanparaśuṃ mūrdhnyapatayāt /
śikhāmārabhya pādāntaṃ puthkarākṣaṃ dvidhākarot //
2.40.d:
क्षणं स्थित्वा भृशं धावन्परशुं मूर्ध्न्यपतयात् ।
शिखामारभ्य पादान्तं पुथ्कराक्षं द्विधाकरोत् ॥
2.40.m: Rāma paused for a moment, then ran forward with fury and brought down his battle-axe upon [Puṣkarākṣa's] head, / splitting Puṣkarākṣa into two, from his crest down to his feet.

2.40.s:
patite śakale bhūmau tatkālaṃ paśyatā nṛṇām /
āścaryaṃ sumāhajjātaṃ divi caiva divau kasām //
2.40.d:
पतिते शकले भूमौ तत्कालं पश्यता नृणाम् ।
आश्चर्यं सुमाहज्जातं दिवि चैव दिवौ कसाम् ॥
2.40.m: When the two halves fell to the ground, as men looked on at that moment, / a very great wonder arose [among them], and among the sky-dwellers in heaven.

2.40.s:
vidārya rāmastaṃ krodhātpuṣkarākṣa mahābalam /
tatsainyamadahatkruddhaḥ pāvako vipinaṃ yathā //
2.40.d:
विदार्य रामस्तं क्रोधात्पुष्कराक्ष महाबलम् ।
तत्सैन्यमदहत्क्रुद्धः पावको विपिनं यथा ॥
2.40.m: Having cleaven mighty Puṣkarākṣa in anger, / Rāma, enraged, burned his army as a fire burns a forest.

2.40.s:
yato yato dhāvati bhārgavendro mano 'nilaujāḥ praharanparaśvadham /
tatastato vājirathebhamānavā nikṛttagātrāḥ śataśo nipetuḥ //
2.40.d:
यतो यतो धावति भार्गवेन्द्रो मनो ऽनिलौजाः प्रहरन्परश्वधम् ।
ततस्ततो वाजिरथेभमानवा निकृत्तगात्राः शतशो निपेतुः ॥
2.40.m:
Wherever the best of the Bhārgavas rushed, possessing the swiftness of mind and wind, striking with his battle-axe,
there horses, chariots, elephants, and men fell by the hundreds, their limbs severed.

2.40.s:
rāmeṇa tatrā tibalena saṃgare nihanyamānāstu paraśvadhena /
hā tāta mātastviti jalpamāṃnā bhasmībabhūvuḥ suvicūrṇitāstadā //
2.40.d:
रामेण तत्रा तिबलेन संगरे निहन्यमानास्तु परश्वधेन ।
हा तात मातस्त्विति जल्पमांना भस्मीबभूवुः सुविचूर्णितास्तदा ॥
2.40.m: Slain there in battle with the battle-axe by Rāma of exceedingly great strength, / crying out, "Alas, father! Mother!", they were then thoroughly crushed into ashes.

2.40.s:
muhūrttamātreṇa ca bhārgaveṇa tatpuṣkarākṣasya balaṃ samagram /
anekarājanyakulaṃ hateśvaraṃ itaṃ navākṣauhiṇikaṃ bhṛśāturam //
2.40.d:
मुहूर्त्तमात्रेण च भार्गवेण तत्पुष्कराक्षस्य बलं समग्रम् ।
अनेकराजन्यकुलं हतेश्वरं इतं नवाक्षौहिणिकं भृशातुरम् ॥
2.40.m: And in merely an instant, the entire army of Puṣkarākṣa, / consisting of nine akṣauhiṇīs, its kings slain, its lords killed, was brought by the Bhārgava to deep distress.

2.40.s:
patite puṣkarākṣe tu kārttavīryārjunaḥ svayam /
ājagāma mahāvīryaḥ suvarṇarathamāsthitaḥ //
2.40.d:
पतिते पुष्कराक्षे तु कार्त्तवीर्यार्जुनः स्वयम् ।
आजगाम महावीर्यः सुवर्णरथमास्थितः ॥
2.40.m: When Puṣkarākṣa had fallen, Kārttavīryārjuna himself, / endowed with great valor, arrived mounted upon a golden chariot,

2.40.s:
nānāśastrasamākīrṇaṃ nānāratnaparicchadam /
daśanalvapramāṇaṃ ca śatavājiyutaṃ nṛpaḥ //
2.40.d:
नानाशस्त्रसमाकीर्णं नानारत्नपरिच्छदम् ।
दशनल्वप्रमाणं च शतवाजियुतं नृपः ॥
2.40.m: strewn with various weapons, furnished with various jewels, / measuring ten nalvas, and yoked with a hundred horses, O king.

2.40.s:
yute bāhusahasreṇa nānāyudhadhareṇa ca /
babhau svarlokamārokṣyandehati sukṛtī yathā //
2.40.d:
युते बाहुसहस्रेण नानायुधधरेण च ।
बभौ स्वर्लोकमारोक्ष्यन्देहति सुकृती यथा ॥
2.40.m: Endowed with a thousand arms bearing various weapons, / he shone like a meritorious soul ascending to heaven having abandoned his body.

2.40.s:
putrāstasya mahāvīryāḥ śataṃ yuddhaviśāradāḥ /
senāḥ saṃvyūhya saṃtasthuḥ saṃgrāme piturājñayā //
2.40.d:
पुत्रास्तस्य महावीर्याः शतं युद्धविशारदाः ।
सेनाः संव्यूह्य संतस्थुः संग्रामे पितुराज्ञया ॥
2.40.m: His one hundred sons, of great valor and skilled in battle, / drew up the forces in array and stood in the battle at their father's command.

2.40.s:
kārttavīryastu balavānrāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā raṇājire /
kālāntakayamaprakhyaṃ yoddhuṃ samupacakrame //
2.40.d:
कार्त्तवीर्यस्तु बलवान्रामं दृष्ट्वा रणाजिरे ।
कालान्तकयमप्रख्यं योद्धुं समुपचक्रमे ॥
2.40.m: The mighty Kārttavīrya, having seen Rāma on the battlefield, / resembling Yama the ender of Time, advanced to fight.

2.40.s:
dakṣe pañcaśataṃ bāṇānvāme pañcaśataṃ dhanuḥ /
jagrā ha bhārgavendrasya samare jetumudyataḥ //
2.40.d:
दक्षे पञ्चशतं बाणान्वामे पञ्चशतं धनुः ।
जग्रा ह भार्गवेन्द्रस्य समरे जेतुमुद्यतः ॥
2.40.m: Taking five hundred arrows in his right [hands] and five hundred bows in his left, / he undertook to conquer the chief of the Bhārgavas in battle.

2.40.s:
bāṇavarṣaṃ cakārātha rāmasyopari bhūpate /
yathā balāhako vīra parvatopari varṣati //
2.40.d:
बाणवर्षं चकाराथ रामस्योपरि भूपते ।
यथा बलाहको वीर पर्वतोपरि वर्षति ॥
2.40.m: Then, O king, he poured a shower of arrows upon Rāma, / just as a cloud, O hero, rains upon a mountain.

2.40.s:
bāṇavarṣeṇa nenājau satkṛto bhṛgunandanaḥ /
jagrāha svaghanurdivyaṃ bāṇavarṣaṃ tathākarot //
2.40.d:
बाणवर्षेण नेनाजौ सत्कृतो भृगुनन्दनः ।
जग्राह स्वघनुर्दिव्यं बाणवर्षं तथाकरोत् ॥
2.40.m: Welcomed in battle with that shower of arrows, the delight of Bhṛgu / grasped his own divine bow and similarly poured a shower of arrows.

2.40.s:
tāvubhauraṇasaṃdṛptau tadā bhārgavahaihayau /
cakraturyaddhamatulaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam //
2.40.d:
तावुभौरणसंदृप्तौ तदा भार्गवहैहयौ ।
चक्रतुर्यद्धमतुलं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम् ॥
2.40.m: Then both the Bhārgava and the Haihaya, proud in battle, / fought an incomparable and tumultuous battle that made the hair stand on end.

2.40.s:
brahmāstraṃ ca sabhūpālaḥ saṃdadhe raṇamūrddhani /
vadhāya bhārgavendrasya sarvaśastrāstradhṛgabalī //
2.40.d:
ब्रह्मास्त्रं च सभूपालः संदधे रणमूर्द्धनि ।
वधाय भार्गवेन्द्रस्य सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रधृगबली ॥
2.40.m: The mighty king, who wielded all weapons and missiles, / fixed the brahmāstra at the head of the battle for the slaughter of the chief of the Bhārgavas.

2.40.s:
rāmo 'pi vāryupaspṛśya brahmaṃ brāhmaya saṃdadhe /
tato vyomni sadā sakte dve cāpya stre narādhipa //
2.40.d:
रामो ऽपि वार्युपस्पृश्य ब्रह्मं ब्राह्मय संदधे ।
ततो व्योम्नि सदा सक्ते द्वे चाप्य स्त्रे नराधिप ॥
2.40.m: Rāma also, having touched water, fixed the brahmāstra against the brahmāstra. / Then, O lord of men, both missiles remained locked in the sky,

2.40.s:
vavṛdhāte jagatprānte tejasā jvalanārkavat /
trayo lokāḥ sapātālā dṛṣṭvā tanmahadadbhutam //
2.40.d:
ववृधाते जगत्प्रान्ते तेजसा ज्वलनार्कवत् ।
त्रयो लोकाः सपाताला दृष्ट्वा तन्महदद्भुतम् ॥
2.40.m: and swelled at the ends of the universe with brilliance like blazing suns. / Seeing that great marvel, the three worlds together with the netherworld,

2.40.s:
jvaladastrayugaṃ taptā menire 'syopasaṃyamam /
rāmastadā vīkṣya jagatpraṇāśaṃ jagannivāsoktamathāsmarattadā //
2.40.d:
ज्वलदस्त्रयुगं तप्ता मेनिरे ऽस्योपसंयमम् ।
रामस्तदा वीक्ष्य जगत्प्रणाशं जगन्निवासोक्तमथास्मरत्तदा ॥
2.40.m: scorched by the pair of blazing missiles, considered it their dissolution. / Seeing then the destruction of the world, Rāma remembered what had been spoken by the Abode of the Universe:

2.40.s:
rakṣā vidheyādya mayāsya saṃyamo nivāraṇīyaḥ paramāṃśadhāriṇā /
iti vyavasya prabhurugratejā netradvayenātha tadastrayugamam //
2.40.d:
रक्षा विधेयाद्य मयास्य संयमो निवारणीयः परमांशधारिणा ।
इति व्यवस्य प्रभुरुग्रतेजा नेत्रद्वयेनाथ तदस्त्रयुगमम् ॥
2.40.m: "Protection must be offered by me today; its destruction must be averted by [me] bearing the supreme portion." / Deciding thus, the lord of terrible majesty then, with his pair of eyes,

2.40.s:
pītvātirāmaṃ jagadākalayya tasthau kṣaṇaṃ dhyānagato mahātmā /
dhyānaprabhāveṇa tatastu tasya brahmāstrayugmaṃ vigataprabhāvam //
2.40.d:
पीत्वातिरामं जगदाकलय्य तस्थौ क्षणं ध्यानगतो महात्मा ।
ध्यानप्रभावेण ततस्तु तस्य ब्रह्मास्त्रयुग्मं विगतप्रभावम् ॥
2.40.m: drank in that pair of missiles, and, embracing the universe, the great-souled one stood for a moment absorbed in meditation. / Then, by the power of his meditation, the pair of brahmāstras lost their splendor

2.40.s:
papāta bhūmau sahasātha tatkṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsvāsthyamupājagāma /
sa jāmadagnyo mahātāṃ mahīyānsraṣṭuṃ tathā pālayituṃ nihantum //
2.40.d:
पपात भूमौ सहसाथ तत्क्षणं सर्वं जगत्स्वास्थ्यमुपाजगाम ।
स जामदग्न्यो महातां महीयान्स्रष्टुं तथा पालयितुं निहन्तुम् ॥
2.40.m: and suddenly fell to the earth that instant, and the entire world attained peace. / That Jāmadagnya, greater than the great, is competent to create, to preserve, and to destroy;

2.40.s:
vibhustathāpīha nijaṃprabhāvaṃ gopāyituṃ lokavidhiṃ cakāra /
dhanurddharaḥ śūratamo mahasvānsadagraṇīḥ saṃsadi tathyavaktā //
2.40.d:
विभुस्तथापीह निजंप्रभावं गोपायितुं लोकविधिं चकार ।
धनुर्द्धरः शूरतमो महस्वान्सदग्रणीः संसदि तथ्यवक्ता ॥
2.40.m: all-pervading though he is, in order to conceal his own power he observed worldly conduct here. / An archer, the bravest of heroes, glorious, foremost of the virtuous, a speaker of truth in the assembly,

2.40.s:
kalākalāpeṣu kṛtaprayatno vidyāsu śāstreṣu budho vidhijñaḥ /
evaṃ nṛloke prathayansvabhāvaṃ sarvāṇi kalyāni karoti nityam //
2.40.d:
कलाकलापेषु कृतप्रयत्नो विद्यासु शास्त्रेषु बुधो विधिज्ञः ।
एवं नृलोके प्रथयन्स्वभावं सर्वाणि कल्यानि करोति नित्यम् ॥
2.40.m: proficient in the whole range of arts, wise in the branches of knowledge and scriptures, knower of rules— / manifesting such a nature in the world of men, he always accomplishes all auspicious deeds.

2.40.s:
sarve tu lokā vijitāstu tena rāmeṇa rājanyaniṣūdanena /
evaṃ sa rāmaḥ prathitaprabhāvaḥ praśāmayitvā tu tadastrayugmam //
2.40.d:
सर्वे तु लोका विजितास्तु तेन रामेण राजन्यनिषूदनेन ।
एवं स रामः प्रथितप्रभावः प्रशामयित्वा तु तदस्त्रयुग्मम् ॥
2.40.m: Indeed, all the worlds were conquered by that Rāma, the destroyer of kṣatriyas. / Thus that Rāma of renowned power, having appeased that pair of missiles,

2.40.s:
punaḥ pravṛtto nidhanaṃ prakartuṃ raṇāgaṇe haihayavaṃśaketoḥ /
tuṇīrataḥ patriyugaṃ gṛhītvā puṅkhe nidhāyātha dhanurjyakāyām //
2.40.d:
पुनः प्रवृत्तो निधनं प्रकर्तुं रणागणे हैहयवंशकेतोः ।
तुणीरतः पत्रियुगं गृहीत्वा पुङ्खे निधायाथ धनुर्ज्यकायाम् ॥
2.40.m: proceeded once again to bring about the death of the banner of the Haihaya race on the battleground. / Taking a pair of feathered arrows from his quiver and placing them at the notch on his bowstring,

2.40.s:
ālakṣya lakṣyaṃ nṛpakarṇayugmaṃ cakartta cūḍāmaṇihartukāmaḥ /
sa kṛttakarṇo nṛpatirmahātmā vinirjitāśeṣajagatpravīraḥ //
2.40.d:
आलक्ष्य लक्ष्यं नृपकर्णयुग्मं चकर्त्त चूडामणिहर्तुकामः ।
स कृत्तकर्णो नृपतिर्महात्मा विनिर्जिताशेषजगत्प्रवीरः ॥
2.40.m: aiming at the target, the king's pair of ears, he sliced them off, desiring to seize his crest-jewel. / That great-souled monarch, who had conquered all the heroes of the universe, with his ears severed,

2.40.s:
mene nijaṃ vīryamiha praṇaṣṭaṃ rāmeṇa bhūmīśatiraskṛtātmā /
kṣaṇaṃ dharādhīśatanurvivarṇā gatānubhāvā nṛpaterbabhūva //
2.40.d:
मेने निजं वीर्यमिह प्रणष्टं रामेण भूमीशतिरस्कृतात्मा ।
क्षणं धराधीशतनुर्विवर्णा गतानुभावा नृपतेर्बभूव ॥
2.40.m: felt that his own valor was lost here, his soul humiliated by the king of the earth [Rāma]. / For a moment, the body of the ruler of the earth became pale, the king stripped of his majesty,

2.40.s:
lekhyeva saccitrakaraprayuktā sudīnacittasya vilakṣyate 'ga /
tataḥ sa rājā nijavīryavaibhavaṃ samastalokādhikatāṃ prayātam //
2.40.d:
लेख्येव सच्चित्रकरप्रयुक्ता सुदीनचित्तस्य विलक्ष्यते ऽग ।
ततः स राजा निजवीर्यवैभवं समस्तलोकाधिकतां प्रयातम् ॥
2.40.m: appearing like a figure painted by a skilled artist, O mountain, with an exceedingly despondent mind. / Then that king, reflecting upon the majesty of his own valor which surpassed all the worlds,

2.40.s:
vicintya paulastyajayādilabdhaṃ śocannivāsītsa jayābhikāṅkṣīṃ /
dadhyau punarmīlitalocano nṛpau dattaṃ tamātreyakulapradīpam //
2.40.d:
विचिन्त्य पौलस्त्यजयादिलब्धं शोचन्निवासीत्स जयाभिकाङ्क्षीं ।
दध्यौ पुनर्मीलितलोचनो नृपौ दत्तं तमात्रेयकुलप्रदीपम् ॥
2.40.m: obtained by his victory over the son of Pulastya and others, longing for victory, was as if in mourning. / With closed eyes, the king meditated again upon Datta, the illuminator of the race of Atri,

2.40.s:
yasya prabhāvānugṛhīta ojasā tiraścakārā khilalokapālakān /
yadāsya hṛdyeṣa mahānubhāvo dattaḥ prayāto na hi darśanaṃ tadā //
2.40.d:
यस्य प्रभावानुगृहीत ओजसा तिरश्चकारा खिललोकपालकान् ।
यदास्य हृद्येष महानुभावो दत्तः प्रयातो न हि दर्शनं तदा ॥
2.40.m: favored by whose power he had formerly eclipsed all the guardians of the world with his vigor. / When this high-minded Datta did not appear in his heart,

2.40.s:
khinno 'timātraṃ dharaṇīpatistadā punaḥ punardhyānapathaṃ jagāma /
sa dhyāyamāno 'pi na cājagāma datto manogocaramasya rājan //
2.40.d:
खिन्नो ऽतिमात्रं धरणीपतिस्तदा पुनः पुनर्ध्यानपथं जगाम ।
स ध्यायमानो ऽपि न चाजगाम दत्तो मनोगोचरमस्य राजन् ॥
2.40.m: the ruler of the earth, exceedingly afflicted, entered the path of meditation again and again. / Yet even though meditated upon, Datta did not come into the range of his mind, O king.

2.40.s:
tapasvino dāntatamasya sādhoranāgaso duṣkṛtikāriṇo vibhuḥ /
evaṃ yadātrestanayo mahātmā dṛṣṭo na ca dhyānapathe nṛpeṇa //
2.40.d:
तपस्विनो दान्ततमस्य साधोरनागसो दुष्कृतिकारिणो विभुः ।
एवं यदात्रेस्तनयो महात्मा दृष्टो न च ध्यानपथे नृपेण ॥
2.40.m: For an ascetic, most restrained, virtuous, and blameless [he was], whereas the lord [Kārttavīrya] was a perpetrator of evil deeds. / When the great-souled son of Atri was thus not seen by the king in the path of meditation,

2.40.s:
tadātiduḥ khena vidūyamānaḥ śokena mohena yuto babhūva /
taṃ śokamagnaṃ nṛpatiṃ mahātmā rāmo jagādākhilacittadarśī //
2.40.d:
तदातिदुः खेन विदूयमानः शोकेन मोहेन युतो बभूव ।
तं शोकमग्नं नृपतिं महात्मा रामो जगादाखिलचित्तदर्शी ॥
2.40.m: he was then tormented by immense pain and overcome with grief and delusion. / To that king plunged in grief, the great-souled Rāma, who perceives the minds of all, spoke:

2.40.s:
mā śokabhāvaṃ nṛpate prayāhi naivānuśocanti mahānubhāvāḥ /
yaste varāyābhavamādisarge sa eva cāhaṃ taṃva sādanāya //
2.40.d:
मा शोकभावं नृपते प्रयाहि नैवानुशोचन्ति महानुभावाः ।
यस्ते वरायाभवमादिसर्गे स एव चाहं तंव सादनाय ॥
2.40.m: "Do not enter into a state of grief, O king; the magnanimous do not lament. / I who appeared in the primary creation to grant you a boon am that very one come for your destruction.

2.40.s:
samāgatastvaṃ bhavadhīracittaḥ saṃgrāmakāle na viṣādacarcā /
sarvo hi lokaḥ svakṛtaṃ bhunakti śubhāśubhaṃ daivakṛtaṃ vipāke //
2.40.d:
समागतस्त्वं भवधीरचित्तः संग्रामकाले न विषादचर्चा ।
सर्वो हि लोकः स्वकृतं भुनक्ति शुभाशुभं दैवकृतं विपाके ॥
2.40.m: You have arrived here; be firm in mind. At the time of battle, there should be no discussion of dejection. / For all creatures enjoy the fruits of their own actions, good and bad, brought about by destiny in their fruition.

2.40.s:
anyonako 'pyasya śubhāśubhasya viparyayaṃ kartumalaṃ nareśa /
yatte supuṇyaṃ bahujanmasaṃcitaṃ teneha dattasya varārhapātram //
2.40.d:
अन्योनको ऽप्यस्य शुभाशुभस्य विपर्ययं कर्तुमलं नरेश ।
यत्ते सुपुण्यं बहुजन्मसंचितं तेनेह दत्तस्य वरार्हपात्रम् ॥
2.40.m: No one else is capable of reversing this good and bad, O lord of men. / Because of the great merit accumulated by you over many births, you became here a worthy recipient of Datta's boon;

2.40.s:
jāto bhavānadya tu duṣkṛtasya phalaṃ prabhuṅkṣva tvamihārjitasya /
gururvimatyāpakṛtastvayā me yatastataḥ karṇanikṛntanaṃ te //
2.40.d:
जातो भवानद्य तु दुष्कृतस्य फलं प्रभुङ्क्ष्व त्वमिहार्जितस्य ।
गुरुर्विमत्यापकृतस्त्वया मे यतस्ततः कर्णनिकृन्तनं ते ॥
2.40.m: today, however, enjoy the fruit of the evil deed accrued by you here. / Because my preceptor was harmed by you through foolishness, your ears were sliced off

2.40.s:
kṛtaṃ mayā paśya harantamojasā cūḍāmaṇiṃ māmapatdṛtya te yaśaḥ /
ityevamuktvā sa bhṛgurmahātmā niyojya bāṇaṃ ca vikṛṣya cāpam //
2.40.d:
कृतं मया पश्य हरन्तमोजसा चूडामणिं मामपत्दृत्य ते यशः ।
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स भृगुर्महात्मा नियोज्य बाणं च विकृष्य चापम् ॥
2.40.m: by me. Behold me stripping away your fame by taking your crest-jewel with my might!" / Having spoken thus, that great-souled Bhṛgu, fixing an arrow and drawing his bow,

2.40.s:
cikṣepa rājñaḥ sa tu lāghavena cchittvā maṇiṃ rāmamamupājagāma /
tadvīkṣya karmāsya muneḥ sutasya sa cārjuno haihayavaṃśadharttā //
2.40.d:
चिक्षेप राज्ञः स तु लाघवेन च्छित्त्वा मणिं रामममुपाजगाम ।
तद्वीक्ष्य कर्मास्य मुनेः सुतस्य स चार्जुनो हैहयवंशधर्त्ता ॥
2.40.m: shot it with dexterity; and having cut off the jewel of the king, it returned to Rāma. / Beholding that deed of the sage's son, Arjuna, the supporter of the Haihaya race,

2.40.s:
samudyato 'bhūtpunarapyudāyudhastaṃ hantumājau dvijamātmaśatrum /
śūlaśaktigadācakrakhaḍhgapaṭṭiśatomaraiḥ //
2.40.d:
समुद्यतो ऽभूत्पुनरप्युदायुधस्तं हन्तुमाजौ द्विजमात्मशत्रुम् ।
शूलशक्तिगदाचक्रखढ्गपट्टिशतोमरैः ॥
2.40.m: stood ready once again with weapons raised to kill that twice-born enemy in battle, / with tridents, spears, maces, discs, swords, paṭṭiśas, and javelins,

2.40.s:
nānāpraharaṇaiścānyairājaghāna dvijātmajam /
sa rāmo lāghavenaiva saṃprakṣiptānyanena ca //
2.40.d:
नानाप्रहरणैश्चान्यैराजघान द्विजात्मजम् ।
स रामो लाघवेनैव संप्रक्षिप्तान्यनेन च ॥
2.40.m: and struck the son of the twice-born with various other weapons. / But Rāma, with great agility, cut down in mid-air with his swift arrows

2.40.s:
śūlādīni cakarttāśu madhya eva nijāśugaiḥ /
sa rājā vāryupaspṛśya sasarjāgneyamuttamam //
2.40.d:
शूलादीनि चकर्त्ताशु मध्य एव निजाशुगैः ।
स राजा वार्युपस्पृश्य ससर्जाग्नेयमुत्तमम् ॥
2.40.m: the tridents and other weapons hurled by him. / The king, having touched water, discharged the supreme fiery missile.

2.40.s:
astraṃ rāmo vāruṇena śamayāmāsa satvaram /
gāndharvaṃ vidadhe rājā vāyavyenāhanadvibhum //
2.40.d:
अस्त्रं रामो वारुणेन शमयामास सत्वरम् ।
गान्धर्वं विदधे राजा वायव्येनाहनद्विभुम् ॥
2.40.m: Rāma quickly pacified that missile with a water missile. / The king discharged the gāndharva weapon, and struck the lord with the vāyavya weapon.

2.40.s:
nāgāstraṃ gāruḍenāpi rāmaściccheda bhūpate /
dattena dattaṃ yacchūlamavyarthaṃ mantrapūrvakam //
2.40.d:
नागास्त्रं गारुडेनापि रामश्चिच्छेद भूपते ।
दत्तेन दत्तं यच्छूलमव्यर्थं मन्त्रपूर्वकम् ॥
2.40.m: Rāma also cut down the serpentine missile with the Gāruḍa missile, O king. / Then the trident, given by Datta with mantras, which was infallible,

2.40.s:
jagrāha samare rājā bhārgavasya vadhāya ca /
tacchūlaṃ śatasūryābhamanivāryaṃ surāsuraiḥ //
2.40.d:
जग्राह समरे राजा भार्गवस्य वधाय च ।
तच्छूलं शतसूर्याभमनिवार्यं सुरासुरैः ॥
2.40.m: The king seized in battle for the slaying of the Bhārgava. / That trident, radiant as a hundred suns and irresistible even to gods and asuras,

2.40.s:
cikṣepa rāmamuddiśya samagreṇa balena saḥ /
mūrdhni tadbhārgavasyātha nipapāta mahīpate //
2.40.d:
चिक्षेप राममुद्दिश्य समग्रेण बलेन सः ।
मूर्ध्नि तद्भार्गवस्याथ निपपात महीपते ॥
2.40.m: He hurled aiming at Rāma with all his might. / Then it fell, O king, upon the head of that Bhārgava.

2.40.s:
tena śūlaprahāreṇa vyathito bhārgavastadā /
mūrcchāmavāpa rājendra papāta ca hariṃ smaran //
2.40.d:
तेन शूलप्रहारेण व्यथितो भार्गवस्तदा ।
मूर्च्छामवाप राजेन्द्र पपात च हरिं स्मरन् ॥
2.40.m: Agonized then by that blow of the trident, the Bhārgava / fell into a faint, O king of kings, and dropped down remembering Hari.

2.40.s:
patite bhārgave tatra sarve devā bhayākulāḥ /
samājagmuḥ puraskṛtya brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān //
2.40.d:
पतिते भार्गवे तत्र सर्वे देवा भयाकुलाः ।
समाजग्मुः पुरस्कृत्य ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरान् ॥
2.40.m: When the Bhārgava had fallen there, all the gods, overcome with fear, / assembled, placing Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara at their head.

2.40.s:
śaṅkarastu mahājñānī sākṣānmṛtyuñjayaḥ prabhuḥ /
bhārgavaṃ jīvayāmāsa saṃjīvanyā sa vidyayā //
2.40.d:
शङ्करस्तु महाज्ञानी साक्षान्मृत्युञ्जयः प्रभुः ।
भार्गवं जीवयामास संजीवन्या स विद्यया ॥
2.40.m: Then Śaṅkara, the lord possessing great knowledge and the visible conqueror of death, / revived the Bhārgava with the saṃjīvanī lore.

2.40.s:
rāmastu cetanāṃ prāpya dadarśa purataḥ surān /
praṇanāma ca rājendra bhaktyā brahmādikāṃstu tān //
2.40.d:
रामस्तु चेतनां प्राप्य ददर्श पुरतः सुरान् ।
प्रणनाम च राजेन्द्र भक्त्या ब्रह्मादिकांस्तु तान् ॥
2.40.m: Having regained consciousness, Rāma beheld the gods before him, / and he bowed down in devotion, O best of kings, to those [gods] beginning with Brahmā.

2.40.s:
te stutā bhārgavendreṇa sadyo 'darśanamāgatāḥ /
sa rāmo vāryuspṛśya jajāpa kavacaṃ tu tat //
2.40.d:
ते स्तुता भार्गवेन्द्रेण सद्यो ऽदर्शनमागताः ।
स रामो वार्युस्पृश्य जजाप कवचं तु तत् ॥
2.40.m: Praised by the chief of Bhārgavas, they instantly vanished from sight. / Touching water, that Rāma then chanted that armor [mantra].

2.40.s:
utthitaśca susaṃrabdho nirdahanniva cakṣuṣā /
smṛtvā pāśupataṃ cāstraṃ śivadattaṃ sa bhārgavaḥ //
2.40.d:
उत्थितश्च सुसंरब्धो निर्दहन्निव चक्षुषा ।
स्मृत्वा पाशुपतं चास्त्रं शिवदत्तं स भार्गवः ॥
2.40.m: He stood up highly enraged, burning as it were with his eyes; / remembering the Pāśupata missile given by Śiva, that Bhārgava,

2.40.s:
sadyaḥ saṃhṛtavāṃstattu kārttavīryaṃ mahābalam /
sa rājā dattabhaktastu viṣṇoścakraṃ sudarśanam /
praviṣṭo bhasmasājjātaṃ śarīraṃ bāhunandana //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite kārttavīryavadho nāma catvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 40//
2.40.d:
सद्यः संहृतवांस्तत्तु कार्त्तवीर्यं महाबलम् ।
स राजा दत्तभक्तस्तु विष्णोश्चक्रं सुदर्शनम् ।
प्रविष्टो भस्मसाज्जातं शरीरं बाहुनन्दन ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते कार्त्तवीर्यवधो नाम चत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 40॥
2.40.m:
Instantly destroyed that mighty Kārttavīrya with it. / That king, devoted to Datta, entered the Sudarśana cakra of Viṣṇu, / [and his] body was turned to ashes, O son of Bāhu.

Thus ends the fortieth chapter, named 'The Slaying of Kārttavīrya', in the account of the Bhārgava, in the third Upoddhātapāda, in the middle section proclaimed by Vāyu, in the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa. // 40

2.41.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
dṛṣṭvā piturvadhaṃ ghoraṃ tatputrāste śataṃ tvarā /
vārayāmāsuratyugraṃ bhārgavaṃ svabaleḥ pṛthak //
2.41.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
दृष्ट्वा पितुर्वधं घोरं तत्पुत्रास्ते शतं त्वरा ।
वारयामासुरत्युग्रं भार्गवं स्वबलेः पृथक् ॥
2.41.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Seeing the terrible slaying of their father, his hundred sons in haste / individually checked the extremely fierce Bhārgava with their own forces.

2.41.s:
ekaikākṣaihiṇīyuktāḥ sarve te yuddhadurmadāḥ /
saṃgrāmaṃ tumulaṃ cakruḥ saṃrabdhāstu piturvadhāt //
2.41.d:
एकैकाक्षैहिणीयुक्ताः सर्वे ते युद्धदुर्मदाः ।
संग्रामं तुमुलं चक्रुः संरब्धास्तु पितुर्वधात् ॥
2.41.m: Accompanied each by an akṣauhiṇī, all of them maddened with war, / infuriated by the death of their father, waged a tumultuous battle.

2.41.s:
rāmastu dṛṣṭvā tatputrāñchūrānraṇaviśāradān /
paraśvadhaṃ samādāya yuyudhe taiśca saṃgare //
2.41.d:
रामस्तु दृष्ट्वा तत्पुत्राञ्छूरान्रणविशारदान् ।
परश्वधं समादाय युयुधे तैश्च संगरे ॥
2.41.m: Beholding his sons, valiant and skilled in battle, / Rāma took up his battle-axe and fought with them in combat.

2.41.s:
tāṃ senāṃ bhagavānrāmaḥ śatākṣauhiṇisaṃmitām /
nijaghāna tvarāyukto muhurttadvayamātrataḥ //
2.41.d:
तां सेनां भगवान्रामः शताक्षौहिणिसंमिताम् ।
निजघान त्वरायुक्तो मुहुर्त्तद्वयमात्रतः ॥
2.41.m: The blessed Rāma swiftly struck down that army, / measured at a hundred akṣauhiṇīs, in merely two muhūrtas.

2.41.s:
niḥśeṣitaṃ svasainyaṃ tu kuṭhāreṇaiva līlayā /
dṛṣṭvā rāmeṇa tesarve yuyudhurvīryasaṃmatāḥ //
2.41.d:
निःशेषितं स्वसैन्यं तु कुठारेणैव लीलया ।
दृष्ट्वा रामेण तेसर्वे युयुधुर्वीर्यसंमताः ॥
2.41.m: Seeing their own army completely annihilated / with his battle-axe as if in sport by Rāma, all of them fought, proud of their prowess.

2.41.s:
nānāvidhāni divyāni praharanto mahojasaḥ /
parito maṇḍalaṃ cakrurbhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ //
2.41.d:
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि प्रहरन्तो महोजसः ।
परितो मण्डलं चक्रुर्भार्गवस्य महात्मनः ॥
2.41.m: Striking with various divine weapons, those of great splendor / formed a circle around the great-souled Bhārgava.

2.41.s:
atha rāmo 'pi balavāṃsteṣāṃ maṇḍalamadhyagaḥ /
vireje bhagavānsākṣādyathā nābhistu cakragā //
2.41.d:
अथ रामो ऽपि बलवांस्तेषां मण्डलमध्यगः ।
विरेजे भगवान्साक्षाद्यथा नाभिस्तु चक्रगा ॥
2.41.m: Then the powerful Rāma too, standing in the middle of their circle, / shone like the lord himself, like the hub of a wheel.

2.41.s:
nṛtyannivācau virarāja rāmaḥ śataṃ punaste parito bhramantaḥ /
rejuśca gopī gaṇamadhyasaṃsthaḥ kṛṣṇo yathā tāḥ parito bhramantyaḥ //
2.41.d:
नृत्यन्निवाचौ विरराज रामः शतं पुनस्ते परितो भ्रमन्तः ।
रेजुश्च गोपी गणमध्यसंस्थः कृष्णो यथा ताः परितो भ्रमन्त्यः ॥
2.41.m: Rāma shone in battle as if dancing; moreover, those hundred, revolving around him, / shone as the cowherd women revolving around Kṛṣṇa when he stood in their midst.

2.41.s:
tadā tu sarve druhiṇapradhānāḥ samāgatāḥ svasvavimānasaṃsthāḥ /
samākirannandanamālyavarṣaiḥ samantato rāmamahīnavīryam //
2.41.d:
तदा तु सर्वे द्रुहिणप्रधानाः समागताः स्वस्वविमानसंस्थाः ।
समाकिरन्नन्दनमाल्यवर्षैः समन्ततो राममहीनवीर्यम् ॥
2.41.m: Then indeed all [the gods] headed by Druhiṇa, mounted upon their respective aerial chariots, / showered from all sides rains of garlands from the Nandana [grove] upon Rāma of unflagging valor.

2.41.s:
yaḥ śastrapādādudatiṣṭhata dhvanir huṃkāragarbho divamaspṛśansa vai /
tauryatrikasyeva śarakṣatāni bhāntīva yadvannakhadantapātāḥ //
2.41.d:
यः शस्त्रपादादुदतिष्ठत ध्वनिर् हुंकारगर्भो दिवमस्पृशन्स वै ।
तौर्यत्रिकस्येव शरक्षतानि भान्तीव यद्वन्नखदन्तपाताः ॥
2.41.m: The sound that arose from the fall of weapons, filled with roarings, touched heaven; / the wounds from arrows shone like marks of nails and teeth, as if in a dramatic performance of music, song, and dance.

2.41.s:
krandanti śastraiḥ kṣatavikṣatāṅgā gāyanti yadvatkila gītavijñāḥ /
evaṃ pravṛttaṃ nṛpayuddhamaṇḍalaṃ paśyanti devā bhṛśavismitākṣaḥ //
2.41.d:
क्रन्दन्ति शस्त्रैः क्षतविक्षताङ्गा गायन्ति यद्वत्किल गीतविज्ञाः ।
एवं प्रवृत्तं नृपयुद्धमण्डलं पश्यन्ति देवा भृशविस्मिताक्षः ॥
2.41.m: Those whose limbs were wounded and torn by weapons cried out, truly like experts in music singing; / the gods, with eyes full of astonishment, watched the battle circle of the kings thus underway.

2.41.s:
tatastu rāmo 'vanipālaputrāñjighāṃsurājau vividhāstrapūgaiḥ /
pṛthakcakārātiba lāṃstu maṇḍaladvicchidya paṅktiṃ prabhurāttacāpaḥ //
2.41.d:
ततस्तु रामो ऽवनिपालपुत्राञ्जिघांसुराजौ विविधास्त्रपूगैः ।
पृथक्चकारातिब लांस्तु मण्डलद्विच्छिद्य पङ्क्तिं प्रभुरात्तचापः ॥
2.41.m: Then Rāma, desirous of slaying the sons of the king in battle with masses of diverse weapons, / the lord having taken up his bow, broke their line and separated the exceedingly powerful ones from the circle.

2.41.s:
ekaikaśastānnijaghāna vīrāñchataṃ tadā pañca tataḥ palāyitāḥ /
śūro vṛṣāsyo vṛṣaśūrasenau jayadhvajaścāpi vibhinnadhairyāḥ //
2.41.d:
एकैकशस्तान्निजघान वीराञ्छतं तदा पञ्च ततः पलायिताः ।
शूरो वृषास्यो वृषशूरसेनौ जयध्वजश्चापि विभिन्नधैर्याः ॥
2.41.m: One by one he struck down those valiant hundred; then five fled: / Śūra, Vṛṣāsya, Vṛṣa, Śūrasena, / and Jayadhvaja, their courage shattered.

2.41.s:
mahābhayenātha parītacitā himādripādāntarakānanaṃ ca /
pṛthaggatāste suparīpsavo nṛpā na ko 'pi kāṃsviddadṛśe bhṛśārttaḥ //
2.41.d:
महाभयेनाथ परीतचिता हिमाद्रिपादान्तरकाननं च ।
पृथग्गतास्ते सुपरीप्सवो नृपा न को ऽपि कांस्विद्ददृशे भृशार्त्तः ॥
2.41.m: Their minds seized with great fear, into the interior forests at the foot of the Himālaya / those kings went separately, longing to save their lives; sorely afflicted, none of them saw anyone else.

2.41.s:
rāmo 'pi hatvā nṛpacakramājau rājñaḥ sahāyarthamupāgataṃ ca /
samanvito 'sāvakṛtavraṇena sasnau mudāgatya ca narmadāyām //
2.41.d:
रामो ऽपि हत्वा नृपचक्रमाजौ राज्ञः सहायर्थमुपागतं च ।
समन्वितो ऽसावकृतव्रणेन सस्नौ मुदागत्य च नर्मदायाम् ॥
2.41.m: Rāma too, having slain in battle the circle of kings who had arrived to aid the king, / accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa, went in joy and bathed in the Narmadā.

2.41.s:
srātvā nityakriyāṃ kṛtvā saṃpūjya vṛṣabhadhvajam /
pratasthe draṣṭumurvīśa śivaṃ kailāsavāsinam //
2.41.d:
स्रात्वा नित्यक्रियां कृत्वा संपूज्य वृषभध्वजम् ।
प्रतस्थे द्रष्टुमुर्वीश शिवं कैलासवासिनम् ॥
2.41.m: Having bathed, performed his daily rites, and worshipped the bull-bannered [god], / he set out, O lord of the earth, to see Śiva, who dwells on Kailāsa,

2.41.s:
gurupatnīmumāṃ cāpi sutau skandavināyakau /
manoyāyī mahātmāsāvakṛtavraṇasaṃyutaḥ //
2.41.d:
गुरुपत्नीमुमां चापि सुतौ स्कन्दविनायकौ ।
मनोयायी महात्मासावकृतव्रणसंयुतः ॥
2.41.m: And the guru's wife, Umā, and their two sons, Skanda and Vināyaka. / That great-souled one, traveling with the speed of thought together with Akṛtavraṇa,

2.41.s:
kṛtakāryo mudā yuktaḥ kailāsaṃ prāpya tatkṣaṇam /
dadarśa tatra nagarīṃ mahatīmalakābhidham //
2.41.d:
कृतकार्यो मुदा युक्तः कैलासं प्राप्य तत्क्षणम् ।
ददर्श तत्र नगरीं महतीमलकाभिधम् ॥
2.41.m: Having accomplished his task and filled with joy, reached Kailāsa that very moment, / and there beheld the great city named Alakā,

2.41.s:
nānāmaṇigaṇākīrṇabhavanairupaśobhitām /
nānārupadharairyakṣaiḥ śobhitāṃ citrabhūṣaṇaiḥ //
2.41.d:
नानामणिगणाकीर्णभवनैरुपशोभिताम् ।
नानारुपधरैर्यक्षैः शोभितां चित्रभूषणैः ॥
2.41.m: Adorned with mansions crowded with various collections of gems, / beautified by Yakṣas bearing diverse forms and wearing variegated ornaments,

2.41.s:
nānāvṛkṣasamākīṇairvanaiścopavanairyutām /
dīrghikābhiḥ sudīrghābhistaḍāgaiścopaśobhitām //
2.41.d:
नानावृक्षसमाकीणैर्वनैश्चोपवनैर्युताम् ।
दीर्घिकाभिः सुदीर्घाभिस्तडागैश्चोपशोभिताम् ॥
2.41.m: Provided with groves and gardens filled with diverse trees, / and adorned with very long oblong lakes and ponds,

2.41.s:
sarvato 'pyāvṛtāṃ bāhye sītayālakanandayā /
tatra devāṅganāsnānamuktakuṅkumapiñjaram //
2.41.d:
सर्वतो ऽप्यावृतां बाह्ये सीतयालकनन्दया ।
तत्र देवाङ्गनास्नानमुक्तकुङ्कुमपिञ्जरम् ॥
2.41.m: Surrounded on the outside on all sides by the cool Alakanandā, / which was yellow with saffron left from the bathing of celestial women there,

2.41.s:
tṛṣāvira hitāścāṃbhaḥ pibanti kariṇo mudā /
yatra saṃgītasaṃnādā śrūyante tatratatra ha //
2.41.d:
तृषाविर हिताश्चांभः पिबन्ति करिणो मुदा ।
यत्र संगीतसंनादा श्रूयन्ते तत्रतत्र ह ॥
2.41.m: And where elephants, freed from thirst, drank water joyfully, / where the resonances of music were heard here and there,

2.41.s:
gandharvairapsarobhiśca satataṃ sahakāribhiḥ /
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhārgavo rājanmudā paramayā yutaḥ //
2.41.d:
गन्धर्वैरप्सरोभिश्च सततं सहकारिभिः ।
तां दृष्ट्वा भार्गवो राजन्मुदा परमया युतः ॥
2.41.m: Accompanied constantly by Gandharvas and Apsarases. / Beholding it, the Bhārgava, O king, filled with supreme joy,

2.41.s:
yayau tadūrdhvaṃ śikharaṃ yatra śevaparaṃ gṛham /
tato dadarśa rājendra snigdhacchāyaṃ mahāvaṭam //
2.41.d:
ययौ तदूर्ध्वं शिखरं यत्र शेवपरं गृहम् ।
ततो ददर्श राजेन्द्र स्निग्धच्छायं महावटम् ॥
2.41.m: Ascended to the peak above it, where the supreme abode of Śiva was. / Then he beheld, O king of kings, a great banyan tree of pleasant shade;

2.41.s:
tasyādhastādvarāvāsaṃ susevyaṃ siddhasaṃyutam /
dadarṃśa tatra prākāraṃ śatayojanamaṇḍalam //
2.41.d:
तस्याधस्ताद्वरावासं सुसेव्यं सिद्धसंयुतम् ।
ददर्ंश तत्र प्राकारं शतयोजनमण्डलम् ॥
2.41.m: Beneath it was an excellent dwelling, easy to resort to, accompanied by Siddhas. / He beheld there an enclosure a hundred yojanas in circumference,

2.41.s:
nānāratnācitaṃ ramyaṃ caturdvāraṃ gaṇāvṛtam /
nandīśvaraṃ mahākālaṃ raktākṣaṃ vikaṭodaram //
2.41.d:
नानारत्नाचितं रम्यं चतुर्द्वारं गणावृतम् ।
नन्दीश्वरं महाकालं रक्ताक्षं विकटोदरम् ॥
2.41.m: Charming, studded with various gems, having four gates, and surrounded by the gaṇas: / Nandīśvara, Mahākāla, Raktākṣa, Vikaṭodara,

2.41.s:
piṅgalākṣaṃ viśālākṣaṃ virūpākṣaṃ ghaṭodaram /
mandāraṃ bhairavaṃ bāṇaṃ ruruṃ bhairavameva ca //
2.41.d:
पिङ्गलाक्षं विशालाक्षं विरूपाक्षं घटोदरम् ।
मन्दारं भैरवं बाणं रुरुं भैरवमेव च ॥
2.41.m: Piṅgalākṣa, Viśālākṣa, Virūpākṣa, Ghaṭodara, / Mandāra, Bhairava, Bāṇa, Ruru, and Bhairava,

2.41.s:
vīrakaṃ vīrabhadraṃ ca caṇḍaṃ bhṛṅgiṃ riṭiṃ mukham /
siddhendranātharudrāṃśca vidyādharamahoragān //
2.41.d:
वीरकं वीरभद्रं च चण्डं भृङ्गिं रिटिं मुखम् ।
सिद्धेन्द्रनाथरुद्रांश्च विद्याधरमहोरगान् ॥
2.41.m: Vīraka, Vīrabhadra, Caṇḍa, Bhṛṅgin, and Riṭi at the head, / chiefs of Siddhas, Nāthas, and Rudras, Vidyādharas and great serpents,

2.41.s:
bhūtapretapiśācāṃśca kūṣmāṇḍānbrahmarākṣasān /
vetālāndānavendrāṃśca yogīndrāṃśca jaṭādharān //
2.41.d:
भूतप्रेतपिशाचांश्च कूष्माण्डान्ब्रह्मराक्षसान् ।
वेतालान्दानवेन्द्रांश्च योगीन्द्रांश्च जटाधरान् ॥
2.41.m: Bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, brahmarākṣasas, / vetālas, chiefs of Dānavas, and foremost yogins with matted locks,

2.41.s:
yakṣakiṃpuruṣāṃścaiva ḍākinīyo ginīstathā /
dṛṣṭvā nandyā5yā tatra praviṣṭo 'ntarmudānvitaḥ //
2.41.d:
यक्षकिंपुरुषांश्चैव डाकिनीयो गिनीस्तथा ।
दृष्ट्वा नन्द्या5या तत्र प्रविष्टो ऽन्तर्मुदान्वितः ॥
2.41.m: Yakṣas, Kiṃpuruṣas, and likewise ḍākinīs and yoginīs. / Having seen [them], with the permission of Nandin he entered inside with joy;

2.41.s:
dadarśa tatra bhuvanairāvṛtaṃ śivamandiram /
caturyojanavistīrṇaṃ tatra prāgdvārasaṃsthitau //
2.41.d:
ददर्श तत्र भुवनैरावृतं शिवमन्दिरम् ।
चतुर्योजनविस्तीर्णं तत्र प्राग्द्वारसंस्थितौ ॥
2.41.m: He beheld there Śiva's temple surrounded by worlds, / four yojanas in extent; there at the eastern gate stood

2.41.s:
dṛṣṭvā vāme kārttikeya dakṣa caiva vināyakam /
nanāma bhārgavastau dvau śivatulyaparākramau //
2.41.d:
दृष्ट्वा वामे कार्त्तिकेय दक्ष चैव विनायकम् ।
ननाम भार्गवस्तौ द्वौ शिवतुल्यपराक्रमौ ॥
2.41.m: Seeing Kārttikeya on the left and Vināyaka on the right, / the Bhārgava bowed to those two whose prowess equaled Śiva's.

2.41.s:
pārṣadapravarāstatra kṣetrapālāśca saṃsthitāḥ /
ratnasiṃhāsanasthāśca ratnabhūṣamabhūṣitāḥ //
2.41.d:
पार्षदप्रवरास्तत्र क्षेत्रपालाश्च संस्थिताः ।
रत्नसिंहासनस्थाश्च रत्नभूषमभूषिताः ॥
2.41.m: The foremost attendants and Kṣetrapālas stood there, / seated upon jewel-studded thrones and adorned with jewel ornaments.

2.41.s:
bhārgavaṃ praviśantaṃ tu hyapṛcchañśivamandiram /
vināyako mahārāja kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭhetyuvāca ha //
2.41.d:
भार्गवं प्रविशन्तं तु ह्यपृच्छञ्शिवमन्दिरम् ।
विनायको महाराज क्षणं तिष्ठेत्युवाच ह ॥
2.41.m: As the Bhārgava was entering Śiva's abode, they asked him, / and Vināyaka said, 'O great king, wait a moment!

2.41.s:
nidrito hyumayā yukto mahādevo 'dhuneti ca /
īśvarājñāṃ gṛhītvāhamatrāgatyakṣaṇāntare //
2.41.d:
निद्रितो ह्युमया युक्तो महादेवो ऽधुनेति च ।
ईश्वराज्ञां गृहीत्वाहमत्रागत्यक्षणान्तरे ॥
2.41.m: Mahādeva is now asleep, accompanied by Umā. / Having received the Lord's command, I will return here in a moment,

2.41.s:
tvayā sārddhaṃ pravekṣyāmi bhrātastiṣṭhātra sāṃpratam /
vināyakacaścaivaṃ śrutvā bhārgavanandanaḥ //
2.41.d:
त्वया सार्द्धं प्रवेक्ष्यामि भ्रातस्तिष्ठात्र सांप्रतम् ।
विनायकचश्चैवं श्रुत्वा भार्गवनन्दनः ॥
2.41.m: and then I will enter together with you. Brother, stay here for now.' / Hearing Vināyaka speak thus, the son of the Bhṛgus,

2.41.s:
pravaktumupacakrāma gaṇeśaṃ tvarayānvitaḥ /
rāma uvāca
gatvā hyantaḥpuraṃ bhrātaḥ praṇamya jagadīśvarau //
2.41.d:
प्रवक्तुमुपचक्राम गणेशं त्वरयान्वितः ।
राम उवाच
गत्वा ह्यन्तःपुरं भ्रातः प्रणम्य जगदीश्वरौ ॥
2.41.m: hastening, began to address Gaṇeśa. / Rāma said: / 'Brother, having gone to the inner apartments and bowed to the two sovereigns of the universe,

2.41.s:
pārvatīśaṅkarau sadyo yāsyāmi nijamandiram /
kārttavīryaḥ sucandraśca saputrabalabāndhavaḥ //
2.41.d:
पार्वतीशङ्करौ सद्यो यास्यामि निजमन्दिरम् ।
कार्त्तवीर्यः सुचन्द्रश्च सपुत्रबलबान्धवः ॥
2.41.m: to Pārvatī and Śaṅkara, I will immediately go to my own abode. / Kārttavīrya and Sucandra, together with their sons, armies, and kinsmen,

2.41.s:
anye sahasraśo bhūpāḥ kāṃbojāḥ paṅlavāḥ śākāḥ /
kānyakubjāḥ kośaleśā māyāvanto mahābalāḥ //
2.41.d:
अन्ये सहस्रशो भूपाः कांबोजाः पङ्लवाः शाकाः ।
कान्यकुब्जाः कोशलेशा मायावन्तो महाबलाः ॥
2.41.m: and thousands of other kings—Kāmbojas, Pahlavas, Śakas, / Kānyakubjas, and rulers of Kośala, full of deceit and possessed of great might—

2.41.s:
nihatāḥ samare sarve mayā śaṃbhuprasādataḥ /
tamimaṃ praṇipatyaiva yāsyāmi svagṛhaṃ prati //
2.41.d:
निहताः समरे सर्वे मया शंभुप्रसादतः ।
तमिमं प्रणिपत्यैव यास्यामि स्वगृहं प्रति ॥
2.41.m: have all been slain in battle by me through the grace of Śambhu. / Having bowed down to him, I shall depart for my own home.'

2.41.s:
ityuktvā bhārgavastatra tasthau gaṇapateḥ puraḥ /
provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ bhārgave sa gaṇādhipaḥ //
2.41.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भार्गवस्तत्र तस्थौ गणपतेः पुरः ।
प्रोवाच मधुरं वाक्यं भार्गवे स गणाधिपः ॥
2.41.m: Having spoken thus, the Bhārgava stood there before the lord of the gaṇas. / That leader of the gaṇas spoke sweet words to the Bhārgava.

2.41.s:
vināyaka uvāca
jñaṇaṃ tiṣṭa mahābhāga darśanaṃ te bhaviṣyati /
adya viśveśvaro bhrātarbhavānyā saha varttate //
2.41.d:
विनायक उवाच
ज्ञणं तिष्ट महाभाग दर्शनं ते भविष्यति ।
अद्य विश्वेश्वरो भ्रातर्भवान्या सह वर्त्तते ॥
2.41.m: Vināyaka said: / 'Wait a moment, O fortunate one, and you will have your audience. / Today the Lord of the Universe, O brother, is with Bhavānī.

2.41.s:
strīpuṃsoryukta yostāta sahaikāsanasaṃsthayoḥ /
karoti sukhabhaṅgaṃ yo narakaṃ sa vrajeddhruvam //
2.41.d:
स्त्रीपुंसोर्युक्त योस्तात सहैकासनसंस्थयोः ।
करोति सुखभङ्गं यो नरकं स व्रजेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
2.41.m: A man who disrupts the pleasure of a man and a woman united together, / seated on the same couch, surely goes to hell.

2.41.s:
viśeṣatastu pitaraṃ guruṃ vā bhūpatiṃ dvijaḥ /
ra7syaṃ samupāsinaṃ na paśyediti niścayaḥ //
2.41.d:
विशेषतस्तु पितरं गुरुं वा भूपतिं द्विजः ।
र7स्यं समुपासिनं न पश्येदिति निश्चयः ॥
2.41.m: Especially a twice-born should never look upon his father, his teacher, or a king / sitting in secret; such is the settled rule.

2.41.s:
kāmato 'kāmato vāpi paśyedyaḥ suratonmukham /
strīvicchedo bhavettasya dhruvaṃ saprasu janmasu //
2.41.d:
कामतो ऽकामतो वापि पश्येद्यः सुरतोन्मुखम् ।
स्त्रीविच्छेदो भवेत्तस्य ध्रुवं सप्रसु जन्मसु ॥
2.41.m: Whoever, intentionally or unintentionally, looks upon [them] intent upon sexual union, / will certainly suffer separation from his wife for seven births.

2.41.s:
śroṇiṃ vakṣaḥ sthalaṃ vaktraṃ yaḥ paśyati parastriyaḥ /
māturvāpi bhaginyā vā duhituḥ sa narādhamaḥ //
2.41.d:
श्रोणिं वक्षः स्थलं वक्त्रं यः पश्यति परस्त्रियः ।
मातुर्वापि भगिन्या वा दुहितुः स नराधमः ॥
2.41.m: He who looks upon the hips, breasts, or face of another man's woman, / or of his mother, his sister, or his daughter, is the lowest of men.'

2.41.s:
bhārgava uvāca
aho śrutamapūrvaṃ kiṃ vacanaṃ tava vaktrataḥ /
brāntyā vinirgataṃ vāpi hāsyārthamathavoditam //
2.41.d:
भार्गव उवाच
अहो श्रुतमपूर्वं किं वचनं तव वक्त्रतः ।
ब्रान्त्या विनिर्गतं वापि हास्यार्थमथवोदितम् ॥
2.41.m: The Bhārgava said: / 'Ah, what unprecedented words have been heard from your mouth! / Did they come forth through delusion, or were they spoken in jest?

2.41.s:
kāmināṃ savikārāṇāmetacchāstranidarśanam /
nirvikārāsya ca śiśorna doṣaḥ kaścideva hi //
2.41.d:
कामिनां सविकाराणामेतच्छास्त्रनिदर्शनम् ।
निर्विकारास्य च शिशोर्न दोषः कश्चिदेव हि ॥
2.41.m: This teaching of the scriptures is for passionate men subject to change; / but for a child who is free from passion, there is no fault whatsoever.

2.41.s:
yāsyāmyantaḥ puraṃ bhrātastava kiṃ tiṣṭha bālaka /
yathādṛṣṭaṃ kariṣyāmi tatra yatsamayocitam //
2.41.d:
यास्याम्यन्तः पुरं भ्रातस्तव किं तिष्ठ बालक ।
यथादृष्टं करिष्यामि तत्र यत्समयोचितम् ॥
2.41.m: I will enter the inner apartments, brother; what is that to you? Stay [here], boy! / Whatever is appropriate to the occasion there, that I will do as I see fit.

2.41.s:
tatraiva mātā tātaśca tvayā nāma nirūpitau /
jagatāṃ pitarau tau ca pārvatīparameśvarau //
2.41.d:
तत्रैव माता तातश्च त्वया नाम निरूपितौ ।
जगतां पितरौ तौ च पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ॥
2.41.m: Indeed, it was you who designated them mother and father; / and those two, Pārvatī and the Supreme Lord, are the parents of all the worlds.'

2.41.s:
ityuktvā bhārgavo rājannantargantuṃ samudyataḥ /
vināyakastadotthāya vārayāmāsa satvaram //
2.41.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भार्गवो राजन्नन्तर्गन्तुं समुद्यतः ।
विनायकस्तदोत्थाय वारयामास सत्वरम् ॥
2.41.m: Having spoken thus, O King, the Bhārgava prepared to enter within. / Then Vināyaka rose and swiftly barred his way.

2.41.s:
vāgyuddhaṃ ca tayorāsīnmitho hastavikarṣaṇam /
dṛṣṭvā sakandastu saṃbhrānto bodhayāmāsa tau tadā //
2.41.d:
वाग्युद्धं च तयोरासीन्मिथो हस्तविकर्षणम् ।
दृष्ट्वा सकन्दस्तु संभ्रान्तो बोधयामास तौ तदा ॥
2.41.m: A war of words ensued between the two, and they dragged each other by the hand. / Seeing this, Skanda became agitated and then tried to dissuade them.

2.41.s:
bāhubhyāṃ dvau samudgṛhya pṛthagutsāritau tathā /
atha kruddho gaṇeśāya bhārgavaḥ paravīrahā /
paraśvadhaṃ samādāya saprakṣeptuṃ samudyataḥ //
2.41.d:
बाहुभ्यां द्वौ समुद्गृह्य पृथगुत्सारितौ तथा ।
अथ क्रुद्धो गणेशाय भार्गवः परवीरहा ।
परश्वधं समादाय सप्रक्षेप्तुं समुद्यतः ॥
2.41.m: Seizing both with his two arms, he pushed them apart. / Then the Bhārgava, slayer of enemy heroes, grew enraged at Gaṇeśa, / and taking up his battle-axe, he prepared to hurl it.

2.41.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā gajānano bhṛguvaraṃ krodhātkṣipantaṃ tvarā svātmārthaṃ paraśuṃ tadā nijakareṇoddhṛtya vegena tu /
bhūrlokaṃ bhuvaḥ svarapi tasyordhvaṃ maharvaijanaṃ lokaṃ cāpi tapo 'tha satyamaparaṃ vaikuṇṭhamapyānayat //
2.41.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा गजाननो भृगुवरं क्रोधात्क्षिपन्तं त्वरा स्वात्मार्थं परशुं तदा निजकरेणोद्धृत्य वेगेन तु ।
भूर्लोकं भुवः स्वरपि तस्योर्ध्वं महर्वैजनं लोकं चापि तपो ऽथ सत्यमपरं वैकुण्ठमप्यानयत् ॥
2.41.m: Seeing the best of the Bhṛgus about to hurl the battle-axe in fury, the Elephant-Faced One swiftly lifted him with his own trunk for his own protection, and with great speed / brought him to the world of the earth, the midspace, heaven, and above that to Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka, and then to Satyaloka, and even to Vaikuṇṭha.

2.41.s:
tasyordhvaṃ ca vidarśayanbhṛguvaraṃ golokamīśātmajo niṣpātyādharalokasaptaka mapītthaṃ darśayāmāsa ca /
uddhṛtyātha tato hi garbhasalile prakṣaptamātraṃ tvarā bhītaṃ prāṇaparipsumānayadatho tatraiva yatrāsthitaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite ekacatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 41//
2.41.d:
तस्योर्ध्वं च विदर्शयन्भृगुवरं गोलोकमीशात्मजो निष्पात्याधरलोकसप्तक मपीत्थं दर्शयामास च ।
उद्धृत्याथ ततो हि गर्भसलिले प्रक्षप्तमात्रं त्वरा भीतं प्राणपरिप्सुमानयदथो तत्रैव यत्रास्थितः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते एकचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 41॥
2.41.m:
And showing the best of the Bhṛgus the Goloka above that, the Lord's son hurled him down and likewise showed him the seven lower worlds; / and then, having lifted him up, as soon as he plunged him into the waters of the Cosmic Womb, he swiftly brought back the terrified man, who was longing to preserve his life, to the very place where he had stood.

Thus ends the forty-first chapter in the story of the Bhārgava in the Upoddhātapāda, the third [part], in the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.42.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
evaṃ saṃbhrāmito rāmo gaṇādhīśena bhūpate /
harṣaśokasamāviṣṭo vicintyātmaparābhavam //
2.42.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एवं संभ्रामितो रामो गणाधीशेन भूपते ।
हर्षशोकसमाविष्टो विचिन्त्यात्मपराभवम् ॥
2.42.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having been thus spun around by the lord of the gaṇas, O king, / Rāma was filled with joy and sorrow, reflecting upon his own humiliation.

2.42.s:
gaṇeśaṃ cābhito vīkṣya nirvikāramavasthitam /
krodhāviṣṭo bhṛśaṃ bhūtvā prākṣipatsvaparaśvadham //
2.42.d:
गणेशं चाभितो वीक्ष्य निर्विकारमवस्थितम् ।
क्रोधाविष्टो भृशं भूत्वा प्राक्षिपत्स्वपरश्वधम् ॥
2.42.m: Seeing Gaṇeśa standing nearby, unaffected, / he was seized with violent rage and hurled his battle-axe.

2.42.s:
gaṇeśastvabhivīkṣyātha pitrā dattaṃ paraśvadham /
amoghaṃ karttukāmastu vāme taṃ daśane 'grahīt //
2.42.d:
गणेशस्त्वभिवीक्ष्याथ पित्रा दत्तं परश्वधम् ।
अमोघं कर्त्तुकामस्तु वामे तं दशने ऽग्रहीत् ॥
2.42.m: Gaṇeśa, seeing the battle-axe given by his father, / and wishing to make it not in vain, caught it with his left tusk.

2.42.s:
sa tu dantaḥ kuṭhāreṇa vicchinno bhūtale 'patat /
bhuvi śoṇitasaṃdigdho vajrāhata ivācalaḥ //
2.42.d:
स तु दन्तः कुठारेण विच्छिन्नो भूतले ऽपतत् ।
भुवि शोणितसंदिग्धो वज्राहत इवाचलः ॥
2.42.m: That tusk, severed by the axe, fell upon the surface of the earth, / smeared with blood upon the ground, like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

2.42.s:
dantapātena vidvastā sābdhidvīpadharā dharā /
cakaṃpe pṛthivīpāla lokāstrāsamupāgatāḥ //
2.42.d:
दन्तपातेन विद्वस्ता साब्धिद्वीपधरा धरा ।
चकंपे पृथिवीपाल लोकास्त्रासमुपागताः ॥
2.42.m: Shattered by the fall of the tusk, the earth with its oceans and continents / trembled, O protector of the earth, and the worlds fell into terror.

2.42.s:
hāhākāro mahānāsī ddevānāṃ divi paśyatām /
kārttikeyādayastatra cukruśurbhṛśamāturāḥ //
2.42.d:
हाहाकारो महानासी द्देवानां दिवि पश्यताम् ।
कार्त्तिकेयादयस्तत्र चुक्रुशुर्भृशमातुराः ॥
2.42.m: A great cry of grief arose among the gods who were watching in heaven; / Kārttikeya and the others who were there cried out in deep distress.

2.42.s:
atha kolāhalaṃ śrutvā dantapātadhvaniṃ tathā /
pārvatīśaṅkarau tatra samājagmaturīśvarau //
2.42.d:
अथ कोलाहलं श्रुत्वा दन्तपातध्वनिं तथा ।
पार्वतीशङ्करौ तत्र समाजग्मतुरीश्वरौ ॥
2.42.m: Then, hearing the commotion and the sound of the falling tusk, / the two sovereigns, Pārvatī and Śaṅkara, arrived there.

2.42.s:
herambaṃ purato dṛṣṭvā vakratuṇḍaikadantinam /
papraccha skandaṃ pārvatī kimetaditi kāraṇam //
2.42.d:
हेरम्बं पुरतो दृष्ट्वा वक्रतुण्डैकदन्तिनम् ।
पप्रच्छ स्कन्दं पार्वती किमेतदिति कारणम् ॥
2.42.m: Seeing Heramba before her with his curved trunk and single tusk, / Pārvatī asked Skanda, 'What is the cause of this?'

2.42.s:
sa tu pṛṣṭastadā mātrā senānīḥ sarvamāditaḥ /
vṛttāntaṃ kathayāmāsa mātre rāmasya śṛṇvataḥ //
2.42.d:
स तु पृष्टस्तदा मात्रा सेनानीः सर्वमादितः ।
वृत्तान्तं कथयामास मात्रे रामस्य शृण्वतः ॥
2.42.m: Questioned then by his mother, the commander of the army related the whole / affair from the beginning to his mother, while Rāma was listening.

2.42.s:
sā śrutvodantamakhilaṃ jagatāṃ jananī nṛpa /
uvāca śaṅkaraṃ ruṣṭā pārvatī prāṇanāyakam //
2.42.d:
सा श्रुत्वोदन्तमखिलं जगतां जननी नृप ।
उवाच शङ्करं रुष्टा पार्वती प्राणनायकम् ॥
2.42.m: Having heard the whole account, O king, Pārvatī, the mother of the worlds, / was enraged and spoke to Śaṅkara, the lord of her life.

2.42.s:
pārvatyuvāca
ayaṃ te bhārgavaḥ śaṃbho śiṣyaḥ putraḥ samo 'bhavat /
tvattolabdhvā paraṃ tejo varma trailokyajidvibho //
2.42.d:
पार्वत्युवाच
अयं ते भार्गवः शंभो शिष्यः पुत्रः समो ऽभवत् ।
त्वत्तोलब्ध्वा परं तेजो वर्म त्रैलोक्यजिद्विभो ॥
2.42.m: Pārvatī said: / 'This Bhārgava, O Śambhu, was your disciple, equal to a son. / Having received from you supreme splendor and armor that conquers the three worlds, O omnipresent one,

2.42.s:
kārttavīryārjunaṃ saṃkhye jitavānūrjitaṃ nṛpam /
svakāryaṃ sādhayitvā tu prādāttubhyaṃ ca dakṣiṇām //
2.42.d:
कार्त्तवीर्यार्जुनं संख्ये जितवानूर्जितं नृपम् ।
स्वकार्यं साधयित्वा तु प्रादात्तुभ्यं च दक्षिणाम् ॥
2.42.m: he defeated the mighty king Kārttavīryārjuna in battle. / Having accomplished his own purpose, he has offered you his fee of honor,

2.42.s:
yatte sutasya daśana kuṭhāreṇa nyapātayat /
anenaiva kṛtārthastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ //
2.42.d:
यत्ते सुतस्य दशन कुठारेण न्यपातयत् ।
अनेनैव कृतार्थस्त्वं भविष्यसि न संशयः ॥
2.42.m: in that he struck down your son's tusk with an axe! / By this alone you will have attained your goal, there is no doubt!

2.42.s:
tvamimaṃ bhārgavaṃ śambho rakṣāntevāsisattamam /
tava kāryāṇi sarvāṇi sādhayiṣyati sadguroḥ //
2.42.d:
त्वमिमं भार्गवं शम्भो रक्षान्तेवासिसत्तमम् ।
तव कार्याणि सर्वाणि साधयिष्यति सद्गुरोः ॥
2.42.m: Protect this Bhārgava, O Śambhu, this best of your disciples! / He will accomplish all the deeds of you, his true teacher!

2.42.s:
aha naivātra tiṣṭhāmi yattvayā vimatā vibho /
putrābhyāṃ sahitā yāsye pituḥ svasya niketanam //
2.42.d:
अह नैवात्र तिष्ठामि यत्त्वया विमता विभो ।
पुत्राभ्यां सहिता यास्ये पितुः स्वस्य निकेतनम् ॥
2.42.m: I shall not stay here at all, since I have been disrespected by you, O Lord! / Accompanied by my two sons, I will go to my father's house.

2.42.s:
saṃto bhujiṣyātanayaṃ satkurvantyātmaputravat /
bhavatā tu kṛtonaiva satkāro vacasāpi hi //
2.42.d:
संतो भुजिष्यातनयं सत्कुर्वन्त्यात्मपुत्रवत् ।
भवता तु कृतोनैव सत्कारो वचसापि हि ॥
2.42.m: Virtuous men honor even the son of a maidservant as their own son; / but by you, no honor was shown even with words

2.42.s:
ātmanastanayasyāsya tato yāsyāmi duḥkhitā /
vasiṣṭha uvāca
etacchrutvā tu vacanaṃ pārvatyā bhagavānbhavaḥ //
2.42.d:
आत्मनस्तनयस्यास्य ततो यास्यामि दुःखिता ।
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं पार्वत्या भगवान्भवः ॥
2.42.m: to your own son; therefore, aggrieved, I shall depart.' / Vasiṣṭha said: / Having heard these words of Pārvatī, the blessed Bhava

2.42.s:
novāca kiñcidvacanaṃ sādhu vāsādhu bhūpate /
sasmāra manasā kṛṣṇaṃ praṇatakleśanāśanam //
2.42.d:
नोवाच किञ्चिद्वचनं साधु वासाधु भूपते ।
सस्मार मनसा कृष्णं प्रणतक्लेशनाशनम् ॥
2.42.m: did not say anything, whether good or bad, O king; / he remembered in his mind Kṛṣṇa, who destroys the affliction of those who bow before him.

2.42.s:
golokanāthaṃ gopīśaṃ nānānunayakovidam /
smṛtamātro 'tha bhagavān keśavaḥ praṇatārttihā /
ājagāma dayāsiṃdhurbhaktavaśyo 'khileśvaraḥ //
2.42.d:
गोलोकनाथं गोपीशं नानानुनयकोविदम् ।
स्मृतमात्रो ऽथ भगवान् केशवः प्रणतार्त्तिहा ।
आजगाम दयासिंधुर्भक्तवश्यो ऽखिलेश्वरः ॥
2.42.m: The lord of Goloka, the master of the cowherd maidens, skilled in various conciliations. / As soon as he was remembered, the blessed Keśava, who removes the distress of the surrendered, / an ocean of compassion, obedient to his devotees, the lord of all, arrived.

2.42.s:
meghaśyāmo viśadavadano ratnakeyūrahāro vidyudvāsā makarasadṛśe kuṇḍale saṃdadhānaḥ /
barhāpīḍaṃ maṇigaṇayutaṃ bibhradīṣatsmitāsyo gopīnātho gaditasuyaśāḥ kaustubhodbhāsivakṣāḥ //
2.42.d:
मेघश्यामो विशदवदनो रत्नकेयूरहारो विद्युद्वासा मकरसदृशे कुण्डले संदधानः ।
बर्हापीडं मणिगणयुतं बिभ्रदीषत्स्मितास्यो गोपीनाथो गदितसुयशाः कौस्तुभोद्भासिवक्षाः ॥
2.42.m:
Dark as a rain-cloud, with a bright countenance, wearing armlets of jewels and necklaces, clad in garments like lightning, bearing earrings shaped like makaras,
adorned with a crest of peacock feathers set with clusters of gems, his face slightly smiling, the lord of the cowherdesses whose fair fame is widely sung, his chest resplendent with the Kaustubha gem,

2.42.s: rādhayā sahitaḥ śrīmān śrīdāmnā cāparājitaḥ //
2.42.d: राधया सहितः श्रीमान् श्रीदाम्ना चापराजितः ॥
2.42.m: accompanied by Rādhā, glorious, along with Śrīdāman, invincible,

2.42.s:
muṣṇaṃstejāṃsi sarveṣāṃ svarucā jñānavāridhiḥ /
athainamāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā śivaḥ saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ //
2.42.d:
मुष्णंस्तेजांसि सर्वेषां स्वरुचा ज्ञानवारिधिः ।
अथैनमागतं दृष्ट्वा शिवः संहृष्टमानसः ॥
2.42.m:
stealing away the splendor of all by his own luster, an ocean of wisdom.
Then, seeing that he had arrived, Śiva was rejoiced in his heart.

2.42.s:
praṇipatya yathānyāyaṃ pūjayāmāsa cāgatam /
praveśyābhyantare veśmarādhayā sahitaṃ vibhum //
2.42.d:
प्रणिपत्य यथान्यायं पूजयामास चागतम् ।
प्रवेश्याभ्यन्तरे वेश्मराधया सहितं विभुम् ॥
2.42.m:
Having bowed down in the proper manner, he paid honor to the arrived [one];
having led the lord into the interior of his dwelling along with Rādhā,

2.42.s:
ratnasiṃhāsane namye sadāraṃ sa nyaveśayat /
tha tatra gatā devī pārvatī tanayānvitā //
2.42.d:
रत्नसिंहासने नम्ये सदारं स न्यवेशयत् ।
थ तत्र गता देवी पार्वती तनयान्विता ॥
2.42.m:
he seated him, along with his consort, upon an exquisite throne of gems.
Then the goddess Pārvatī went there, accompanied by her two sons.

2.42.s:
nanāma caraṇānprabhvoḥ putrābhyāṃ sahitā mudā /
tha rāmo 'pi tatraiva gatvā namitakandharaḥ //
2.42.d:
ननाम चरणान्प्रभ्वोः पुत्राभ्यां सहिता मुदा ।
थ रामो ऽपि तत्रैव गत्वा नमितकन्धरः ॥
2.42.m:
She joyfully bowed to the feet of the two lords together with her sons.
Then Rāma too, having gone to that very place with lowered head,

2.42.s:
pārvatyāścaraṇopānte papātākulamānasaḥ /
sā yadā nābhyanandattaṃ bhārgavaṃ praṇataṃ puraḥ //
2.42.d:
पार्वत्याश्चरणोपान्ते पपाताकुलमानसः ।
सा यदा नाभ्यनन्दत्तं भार्गवं प्रणतं पुरः ॥
2.42.m:
fell down near Pārvatī's feet with a distressed mind.
When she did not welcome that Bhārgava bowed before her,

2.42.s: tadovāca jagannāthaḥ pārvatīṃ prīṇayangirā //
2.42.d: तदोवाच जगन्नाथः पार्वतीं प्रीणयन्गिरा ॥
2.42.m: the Lord of the Universe spoke, pleasing Pārvatī with his words:

2.42.s:
śrīkṛṣma uvāca
ayi naganaṃ dini ninditacandramukhi tvamimaṃ jamadagnisutam /
naya nijahastasarojasamarpitamstakamaṅkamanantaguṇe //
2.42.d:
श्रीकृष्म उवाच
अयि नगनं दिनि निन्दितचन्द्रमुखि त्वमिमं जमदग्निसुतम् ।
नय निजहस्तसरोजसमर्पितम्स्तकमङ्कमनन्तगुणे ॥
2.42.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O daughter of the mountain, whose face outshines the moon, take this son of Jamadagni
into your lap, his head offered by your own lotus hands, O goddess of endless virtues!

2.42.s:
bhavabhayahāriṇi śaṃbhuvihāriṇi kalmaṣanāśini kuṃbhigate /
tava caraṇe patitaṃ satataṃ kṛtakilbiṣamapyava dehi varam //
2.42.d:
भवभयहारिणि शंभुविहारिणि कल्मषनाशिनि कुंभिगते ।
तव चरणे पतितं सततं कृतकिल्बिषमप्यव देहि वरम् ॥
2.42.m:
O remover of worldly fear, delighting with Śambhu, destroyer of impurities, having breasts like water jars!
Protect him who has fallen perpetually at your feet, even if he has committed an offense; grant him a boon!

2.42.s:
śruṇu devi mahābhāge vedoktaṃ vacanaṃ mama /
yacchrutvā harṣitā nūnaṃ bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ /
vināyakaste tanayo mahātmā mahatāṃ mahān //
2.42.d:
श्रुणु देवि महाभागे वेदोक्तं वचनं मम ।
यच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षिता नूनं भविष्यसि न संशयः ।
विनायकस्ते तनयो महात्मा महतां महान् ॥
2.42.m:
Hear, O noble goddess, my words declared in the Vedas,
hearing which you will surely be delighted, without doubt.
Vināyaka is your son, high-souled, greatest among the great,

2.42.s:
yaṃ kāmaḥ krodha udvego bhayaṃ nāviśate kadā /
vedasmṛtipurāṇeṣu saṃhitāsu ca bhāmini //
2.42.d:
यं कामः क्रोध उद्वेगो भयं नाविशते कदा ।
वेदस्मृतिपुराणेषु संहितासु च भामिनि ॥
2.42.m:
whom desire, wrath, anxiety, and fear never penetrate.
In the Vedas, the Smṛtis, the Purāṇas, and the Saṃhitās, O passionate lady,

2.42.s:
nāmānyasyopadiṣṭāni supuṇyāni mahātmabhiḥ /
yāni tāni pravakṣyāmi nikhilāghaharāṇi ca //
2.42.d:
नामान्यस्योपदिष्टानि सुपुण्यानि महात्मभिः ।
यानि तानि प्रवक्ष्यामि निखिलाघहराणि च ॥
2.42.m:
his names are taught by the great-souled, very sacred,
which destroy all sins, and these I shall declare to you.

2.42.s:
pramathānāṃ gaṇā ye ca nānārūpā mahābalāḥ /
teṣāmīśastvayaṃ yasmādgaṇeśastena kīrttitaḥ //
2.42.d:
प्रमथानां गणा ये च नानारूपा महाबलाः ।
तेषामीशस्त्वयं यस्माद्गणेशस्तेन कीर्त्तितः ॥
2.42.m:
Because he is the lord of the Pramatha hosts, diverse in form and immensely strong,
he is therefore celebrated as Gaṇeśa.

2.42.s:
bhūtāni ca bhaviṣyāṇi varttamānāni yāni ca /
brahmāṇḍānyakhilānyeva yasmiṃllaṃbodaraḥ sa tu //
2.42.d:
भूतानि च भविष्याणि वर्त्तमानानि यानि च ।
ब्रह्माण्डान्यखिलान्येव यस्मिंल्लंबोदरः स तु ॥
2.42.m:
Since all the cosmic eggs—past, present,
and future—reside in him, he is Lambodara ('Big-bellied').

2.42.s:
yaḥ sthiro devayogena cchinnaṃ saṃyojitaṃ punaḥ /
gajasya śirasā devitena prokto gajānanaḥ //
2.42.d:
यः स्थिरो देवयोगेन च्छिन्नं संयोजितं पुनः ।
गजस्य शिरसा देवितेन प्रोक्तो गजाननः ॥
2.42.m:
Because his severed [head] was made firm and joined once more
with the head of an elephant by divine power, O goddess, he is called Gajānana ('Elephant-faced').

2.42.s:
caturthyāmuditaścandro darbhiṇā śapta āturaḥ /
anena vidhṛto bhāle bhālacandrastataḥ smṛtaḥ //
2.42.d:
चतुर्थ्यामुदितश्चन्द्रो दर्भिणा शप्त आतुरः ।
अनेन विधृतो भाले भालचन्द्रस्ततः स्मृतः ॥
2.42.m:
The moon, risen on the fourth day, cursed by Darbhin, fell into distress;
placed upon his forehead by him, he is therefore remembered as Bhālacandra ('Moon-crested').

2.42.s:
śaptaḥ purā saptabhistu munibhiḥ saṃkṣayaṃ gataḥ /
jātavedā dīpito 'bhūdyenāsauśūrpakarmakaḥ //
2.42.d:
शप्तः पुरा सप्तभिस्तु मुनिभिः संक्षयं गतः ।
जातवेदा दीपितो ऽभूद्येनासौशूर्पकर्मकः ॥
2.42.m:
Formerly cursed by the seven sages, Agni had met with destruction;
he was rekindled by him, wherefore he is Śūrpakarṇa ('Winnowing-fan-eared').

2.42.s:
purā devāsure yuddhe pūjito diviṣadgaṇaiḥ /
vighnaṃ nivārayāmāsa vighnanāśastataḥ smṛtaḥ //
2.42.d:
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे पूजितो दिविषद्गणैः ।
विघ्नं निवारयामास विघ्ननाशस्ततः स्मृतः ॥
2.42.m:
Formerly, in the war between gods and Asuras, worshiped by the hosts of celestials,
he warded off obstacles; therefore he is remembered as Vighnanāśa ('Destroyer of Obstacles').

2.42.s:
adyāyaṃ devi rāmeṇa kuṭhāreṇa nipātya ca /
daśanaṃ daivato bhadre hyekadantaḥ kṛto 'munā //
2.42.d:
अद्यायं देवि रामेण कुठारेण निपात्य च ।
दशनं दैवतो भद्रे ह्येकदन्तः कृतो ऽमुना ॥
2.42.m:
Today, O goddess, a tusk was felled by Rāma with his axe,
and by fate, O auspicious one, he was made Ekadanta ('Single-tusked') by him.

2.42.s:
bhaviṣyatyatha paryāye brahmaṇo haravallabhe /
vakrībhaviṣyattuṇḍatvādvakratuṇḍaḥ smṛto budhaiḥ //
2.42.d:
भविष्यत्यथ पर्याये ब्रह्मणो हरवल्लभे ।
वक्रीभविष्यत्तुण्डत्वाद्वक्रतुण्डः स्मृतो बुधैः ॥
2.42.m:
Then in the future epoch of Brahmā, O beloved of Hara,
because his trunk will become curved, he is remembered by the wise as Vakratuṇḍa ('Curved-trunked').

2.42.s:
evaṃ tavāsya putrasya saṃti nāmāni pārvati /
smaraṇātpāpahārīṇi trikālānugatānyapi //
2.42.d:
एवं तवास्य पुत्रस्य संति नामानि पार्वति ।
स्मरणात्पापहारीणि त्रिकालानुगतान्यपि ॥
2.42.m:
Thus are the names of this son of yours, O Pārvatī,
which remove sin merely by recollection and pertain to the three times.

2.42.s:
asmāttrayodaśīkalpātpūrvasmindaśamībhave /
mayāsmai tu varo dattaḥ sargadevāgrapūjane //
2.42.d:
अस्मात्त्रयोदशीकल्पात्पूर्वस्मिन्दशमीभवे ।
मयास्मै तु वरो दत्तः सर्गदेवाग्रपूजने ॥
2.42.m:
In the tenth birth prior to this thirteenth kalpa,
a boon was granted by me to him for his worship before the gods at the beginning of creation:

2.42.s:
jātakarmādisaṃskāre garbhādhānādike 'pi ca /
yātrāyāṃ ca vaṇijyādau yuddhe devārcane śubhe //
2.42.d:
जातकर्मादिसंस्कारे गर्भाधानादिके ऽपि च ।
यात्रायां च वणिज्यादौ युद्धे देवार्चने शुभे ॥
2.42.m:
In rites such as birth ceremonies, conception and the rest,
in journey, trade, and such, in war, in auspicious worship of the gods,

2.42.s:
saṃkaṣṭe kāmyasiddhyarthaṃ pūjayedyo gajānanam /
tasya sarvāṇi kāryāṇi siddhyantyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
2.42.d:
संकष्टे काम्यसिद्ध्यर्थं पूजयेद्यो गजाननम् ।
तस्य सर्वाणि कार्याणि सिद्ध्यन्त्येव न संशयः ॥
2.42.m:
and in times of distress, whoever worships Gajānana for the attainment of his desires,
all his undertakings surely succeed; there is no doubt.

2.42.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityuktaṃ tu samākarṇya kṛṣṇena sumahātmanā /
pārvatī jagatāṃ nāthā vismitāsīcchubhānanā //
2.42.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्युक्तं तु समाकर्ण्य कृष्णेन सुमहात्मना ।
पार्वती जगतां नाथा विस्मितासीच्छुभानना ॥
2.42.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having heard this spoken by the great-souled Kṛṣṇa,
Pārvatī, the mistress of the worlds, of auspicious face, was amazed.

2.42.s:
yadā naivottaraṃ prādātpārvatī śivasannidhau /
tadā rādhābravīddevīṃ śivarūpā sanātanī //
2.42.d:
यदा नैवोत्तरं प्रादात्पार्वती शिवसन्निधौ ।
तदा राधाब्रवीद्देवीं शिवरूपा सनातनी ॥
2.42.m:
When Pārvatī gave no reply at all in the presence of Śiva,
then the eternal Rādhā, whose nature is identical with Śiva, spoke to the goddess.

2.42.s:
śrīrādhovāca /
prakṛtiḥ puruṣaścobhāvanyonyāśrayavigrahau /
dvidhā bhinnau prakāśete prapañce 'smin yathā tathā //
2.42.d:
श्रीराधोवाच ।
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चोभावन्योन्याश्रयविग्रहौ ।
द्विधा भिन्नौ प्रकाशेते प्रपञ्चे ऽस्मिन् यथा तथा ॥

2.42.s:
tvaṃ cāhamāvayordevi bhedo naivāsti kaścana /
viṣṇustvamahamevāsmi śivo dviguṇatāṃ gataḥ //
2.42.d:
त्वं चाहमावयोर्देवि भेदो नैवास्ति कश्चन ।
विष्णुस्त्वमहमेवास्मि शिवो द्विगुणतां गतः ॥
2.42.m:
You and I, O goddess—there is no difference between us at all;
you are Viṣṇu, I am indeed Śiva doubled in nature.

2.42.s:
śivasya hṛdaye viṣṇurbhavatyā rūpamāsthitaḥ /
mama rūpaṃ samāsthāya viṣṇośca hṛdaye śivaḥ //
2.42.d:
शिवस्य हृदये विष्णुर्भवत्या रूपमास्थितः ।
मम रूपं समास्थाय विष्णोश्च हृदये शिवः ॥
2.42.m:
In the heart of Śiva is Viṣṇu, having assumed your form;
and in the heart of Viṣṇu is Śiva, having assumed my form.

2.42.s:
eṣa rāmo mahābhāge vaiṣṇavaḥ śaivatāṃ gataḥ /
gaṇeśo 'yaṃ śivaḥ sākṣādvaiṣṇavatvaṃ samāsthitaḥ //
2.42.d:
एष रामो महाभागे वैष्णवः शैवतां गतः ।
गणेशो ऽयं शिवः साक्षाद्वैष्णवत्वं समास्थितः ॥
2.42.m:
This Rāma, O noble lady, is a Vaiṣṇava who has become a Śaiva;
this Gaṇeśa is Śiva directly, who has assumed the state of a Vaiṣṇava.

2.42.s:
etayorovayoḥ prabhavoścāpi bhedo na dṛśyate /
evāmuktvā tu sā rādhā kroḍe kṛtvā gajānanam //
2.42.d:
एतयोरोवयोः प्रभवोश्चापि भेदो न दृश्यते ।
एवामुक्त्वा तु सा राधा क्रोडे कृत्वा गजाननम् ॥
2.42.m:
No difference is seen between these two, nor between the two of us, nor between the two lords.
Having spoken thus, Rādhā took Gajānana onto her lap,

2.42.s:
mūrdhnyupāghrāya pasparśa svahastena kapolake /
spṛṣṭamātre kapole tu kṣataṃ pūrttimudāgatam //
2.42.d:
मूर्ध्न्युपाघ्राय पस्पर्श स्वहस्तेन कपोलके ।
स्पृष्टमात्रे कपोले तु क्षतं पूर्त्तिमुदागतम् ॥
2.42.m:
smelled him on the head, and touched his cheek with her own hand.
As soon as the cheek was touched, the wound attained healing.

2.42.s:
pārvatī muprasannābhūdanunītātha rādhayā /
pādayoḥ patitaṃ rāmamutthāpya nijapāṇinā //
2.42.d:
पार्वती मुप्रसन्नाभूदनुनीताथ राधया ।
पादयोः पतितं राममुत्थाप्य निजपाणिना ॥
2.42.m:
Pārvatī became exceedingly well pleased, being persuaded by Rādhā;
lifting up with her own hand Rāma who was fallen at her feet,

2.42.s:
kroḍīcakāra suprītā mūrdhnyu pāghrāya pārvatī /
evaṃ tayostu satkāraṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmagaṇeśayoḥ //
2.42.d:
क्रोडीचकार सुप्रीता मूर्ध्न्यु पाघ्राय पार्वती ।
एवं तयोस्तु सत्कारं दृष्ट्वा रामगणेशयोः ॥
2.42.m:
Pārvatī joyfully embraced him on her lap and smelled his head.
Seeing such hospitable treatment given to Rāma and Gaṇeśa,

2.42.s:
kṛṣṇaḥ skandamupākṛṣya svāṅke premṇā nyaveśayat /
atha śaṃbhurapi prītaḥ śrīdāmānam pasthitam //
2.42.d:
कृष्णः स्कन्दमुपाकृष्य स्वाङ्के प्रेम्णा न्यवेशयत् ।
अथ शंभुरपि प्रीतः श्रीदामानम् पस्थितम् ॥
2.42.m:
Kṛṣṇa pulled Skanda close and lovingly placed him on his lap.
Then Śambhu too, well-pleased, took Śrīdāman who was standing near,

2.42.s:
svotsaṃge sthāpayāmāsa premṇā matkṛtya mānadaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite dvicatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 42//
2.42.d:
स्वोत्संगे स्थापयामास प्रेम्णा मत्कृत्य मानदः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते द्विचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 42॥
2.42.m:
and placed him on his lap with affection, honoring him respectfully.

Thus ends the forty-second chapter in the account of Bhārgava, in the third section, the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa spoken by Vāyu. // 42

2.43.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
evaṃ susnigdhacitteṣu teṣu tiṣṭhatsu bhūpate /
bhavānyutsaṃgato rāmaḥ samutthāya kṛtājaliḥ //
2.43.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
एवं सुस्निग्धचित्तेषु तेषु तिष्ठत्सु भूपते ।
भवान्युत्संगतो रामः समुत्थाय कृताजलिः ॥
2.43.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
While they remained with very tender minds in this way, O king,
Rāma, having arisen from the lap of Bhavānī with folded palms,

2.43.s:
tuṣṭāva prayato bhūtvā nirviśeṣa viśeṣavat /
advayaṃ dvaitamāpannaṃ nirguṇaṃ saguṇātmakam //
2.43.d:
तुष्टाव प्रयतो भूत्वा निर्विशेष विशेषवत् ।
अद्वयं द्वैतमापन्नं निर्गुणं सगुणात्मकम् ॥
2.43.m:
composed in mind, praised her who is without distinction yet possesses distinction,
non-dual yet entered into duality, devoid of qualities yet consisting of qualities:

2.43.s:
rāma uvāca
prakṛtivikṛtijātaṃ viśvametadvidhātuṃ mama kiyadanubhātaṃ vaibhavaṃ tatpramātum /
aviditatanunāmābhīṣṭavastvekadhāmābhavadatha bhava bhāmā pātu māṃ pūrṇakāmā //
2.43.d:
राम उवाच
प्रकृतिविकृतिजातं विश्वमेतद्विधातुं मम कियदनुभातं वैभवं तत्प्रमातुम् ।
अविदिततनुनामाभीष्टवस्त्वेकधामाभवदथ भव भामा पातु मां पूर्णकामा ॥
2.43.m:
Rāma said:
To ordain this universe born of Prakṛti and its transformations, how much of my insight has shone to measure that majesty?
May the consort of Bhava, the single abode of desired reality whose form and names are unknown, whose desires are fulfilled, protect me!

2.43.s:
prakaṭitaguṇābhānaṃ kālasaṃkhyāvidhānaṃ sakalabhavanidānaṃ kīrtyate yatpradhānam /
tadiha nikhilatātaḥ saṃbabhūvokṣapātaḥ kṛtakṛtakanipātaḥ pātu māmadya mātaḥ //
2.43.d:
प्रकटितगुणाभानं कालसंख्याविधानं सकलभवनिदानं कीर्त्यते यत्प्रधानम् ।
तदिह निखिलतातः संबभूवोक्षपातः कृतकृतकनिपातः पातु मामद्य मातः ॥
2.43.m:
That which is praised as Pradhāna, the cause of all existence, displaying the manifestation of the guṇas, ordaining the count of time—
from which the father of all became the showerer [of seed], throwing down the created and uncreated: may that Mother protect me today!

2.43.s:
danujakulavināśīlekhapātāvināśī prathamakulavikāśī sarvavidyāprakāśī /
prasabharacitakāśī bhaktadattākhilāśīravatu vijitapāśī māṃsadā ṣaṇmukhāśī //
2.43.d:
दनुजकुलविनाशीलेखपाताविनाशी प्रथमकुलविकाशी सर्वविद्याप्रकाशी ।
प्रसभरचितकाशी भक्तदत्ताखिलाशीरवतु विजितपाशी मांसदा षण्मुखाशी ॥
2.43.m:
Destroyer of the demon race, imperishable protectress of the gods, displayer of the primary race, illuminator of all wisdom,
forcefully creating luster, bestowing all blessings upon her devotees, conqueror of the fettered: may the mother of the six-faced one protect me always!

2.43.s:
haranikaṭa nivāsī kṛṣṇasevāvilāsī praṇatajanavibhāsī gopakanyāprahāsī /
harakṛtabahumāno gopikeśaikatāno viditabahuvidhāno jāyatāṃ kīrtihā nau //
2.43.d:
हरनिकट निवासी कृष्णसेवाविलासी प्रणतजनविभासी गोपकन्याप्रहासी ।
हरकृतबहुमानो गोपिकेशैकतानो विदितबहुविधानो जायतां कीर्तिहा नौ ॥
2.43.m:
Abiding near Hara, taking pleasure in the service of Kṛṣṇa, illuminating those who bow to her, smiling upon the cowherd maidens,
highly honored by Hara, single-minded toward the lord of the cowherdesses, knowing manifold rites: may she be the destroyer of ill fame for us two!

2.43.s:
prabhuniyatamānā yo nunnabhaktāntarāyo tdṛtaduritanikāyo jñānadātāparāyoḥ /
sakalaguṇagariṣṭho rādhikāṅkeniviṣṭo mama kṛtamaparādhaṃ kṣantumarhatvagādham //
2.43.d:
प्रभुनियतमाना यो नुन्नभक्तान्तरायो त्दृतदुरितनिकायो ज्ञानदातापरायोः ।
सकलगुणगरिष्ठो राधिकाङ्केनिविष्टो मम कृतमपराधं क्षन्तुमर्हत्वगाधम् ॥
2.43.m: He who possesses measured and constant majesty, who removes the obstacles of his devotees, who bears away heaps of sins, who bestows knowledge, who is beyond comprehension, / who is highest in all virtues, seated on the lap of Rādhikā—may he deign to forgive my deep offense.

2.43.s:
yā rādhā jagadudbhavasthitilayeṣvārādhyate vā janaiḥ śabdaṃ bodhayatīśavaktraṃvigalatpremāmṛtāsvādanam /
rāseśī rasikeśvarī ramaṇatdṛnniṣṭhānijānandinī netrī sā paripātu māmavanataṃ rādheti ya kīrtyate //
2.43.d:
या राधा जगदुद्भवस्थितिलयेष्वाराध्यते वा जनैः शब्दं बोधयतीशवक्त्रंविगलत्प्रेमामृतास्वादनम् ।
रासेशी रसिकेश्वरी रमणत्दृन्निष्ठानिजानन्दिनी नेत्री सा परिपातु मामवनतं राधेति य कीर्त्यते ॥
2.43.m: She, Rādhā, who is worshipped by people during the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe, who makes understood the word, the tasting of the nectar of love flowing from the Lord’s mouth, / queen of the rāsa, sovereign of the lovers, devoted to gazing at her beloved, rejoicing in her own self, the leader—may that one celebrated as ‘Rādhā’ protect me who am bowed down.

2.43.s: yasyā garbhasamudbhavo hyativirāḍyasyāṃśabhūto virāṭ yannābhyaṃburuhodbhavena vidhinaikāntopadiṣṭena vai sṛṣṭaṃ sarvamidaṃ carācaramayaṃ viśvaṃ ca yadromasu brahmāṇḍāni vibhānti tasya jananī śaśvatprasannāstu sā //
2.43.d: यस्या गर्भसमुद्भवो ह्यतिविराड्यस्यांशभूतो विराट् यन्नाभ्यंबुरुहोद्भवेन विधिनैकान्तोपदिष्टेन वै सृष्टं सर्वमिदं चराचरमयं विश्वं च यद्रोमसु ब्रह्माण्डानि विभान्ति तस्य जननी शश्वत्प्रसन्नास्तु सा ॥
2.43.m: From whose womb the supreme Virāṭ indeed arose, of whom the Virāṭ is a portion; and by Brahmā, who sprang from his navel-lotus and was instructed in solitude, / this entire universe composed of moving and unmoving beings was created; and on whose bodily hairs cosmic eggs shine forth—may his mother always be pleased!

2.43.s:
pāyādyaḥ sa carācarasya jagato vyāpī vibhuḥ saccidānandābdhiḥ prakaṭasthito vilasati premāndhayā rādhayā /
kṛṣṇaḥ pūrṇatamo mamopari dayāklinnāntaraḥ stātsadā yenāhaṃ sukṛtī bhavāmi ca bhavāmyānandalīnāntaraḥ //
2.43.d:
पायाद्यः स चराचरस्य जगतो व्यापी विभुः सच्चिदानन्दाब्धिः प्रकटस्थितो विलसति प्रेमान्धया राधया ।
कृष्णः पूर्णतमो ममोपरि दयाक्लिन्नान्तरः स्तात्सदा येनाहं सुकृती भवामि च भवाम्यानन्दलीनान्तरः ॥
2.43.m: May he who is the all-pervading, almighty ocean of existence, consciousness, and bliss, who manifestly abides and sports with Rādhā blinded by love, protect [me]! / May Kṛṣṇa, the most complete, his heart ever moistened with compassion toward me, [be pleased], so that I become virtuous and my heart becomes merged in bliss.

2.43.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
stutvaivaṃ jāmadagnyastu virarāma ha tatparam /
vijñātākhilatattvārtho hṛṣṭaromā kṛtārthavat //
2.43.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
स्तुत्वैवं जामदग्न्यस्तु विरराम ह तत्परम् ।
विज्ञाताखिलतत्त्वार्थो हृष्टरोमा कृतार्थवत् ॥
2.43.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having thus praised [them], the son of Jamadagni then fell silent, / having understood the reality of all truths, his hair standing on end, feeling fulfilled.

2.43.s:
athovāca prasannātmā kṛṣṇaḥ kamalalocanaḥ /
bhārgavaṃ praṇataṃ bhaktyā kṛpāpātraṃ purasthitam //
2.43.d:
अथोवाच प्रसन्नात्मा कृष्णः कमललोचनः ।
भार्गवं प्रणतं भक्त्या कृपापात्रं पुरस्थितम् ॥
2.43.m: Then lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, his heart pleased, / spoke to the Bhārgava, who stood before him, bowed down in devotion and worthy of grace.

2.43.s:
kṛṣma uvāca
siddho 'si bhārgavendra tvaṃ prasādānmama saṃpratam /
adya prabhṛti vatsāsmiṃlloke śreṣṭhatamo bhava //
2.43.d:
कृष्म उवाच
सिद्धो ऽसि भार्गवेन्द्र त्वं प्रसादान्मम संप्रतम् ।
अद्य प्रभृति वत्सास्मिंल्लोके श्रेष्ठतमो भव ॥
2.43.m: Kṛṣṇa said: / O best of Bhārgavas, you have attained perfection now by my grace. / From this day forward, my child, become the greatest in this world.

2.43.s:
tubhyaṃ varo mayā dattaḥ purā viṣṇupadāśrame /
tatsarvaṃ kramato bhāvyaṃ samā bahvīstvayā vibho //
2.43.d:
तुभ्यं वरो मया दत्तः पुरा विष्णुपदाश्रमे ।
तत्सर्वं क्रमतो भाव्यं समा बह्वीस्त्वया विभो ॥
2.43.m: A boon was given to you by me previously in the hermitage of Viṣṇupada; / all of that must come to pass in due order for many years through you, O mighty one.

2.43.s:
dayā vidheyā dīneṣu śreya uttamamicchatā /
yogaśca sādanīyo vai śatrūṇāṃ nigrahastathā //
2.43.d:
दया विधेया दीनेषु श्रेय उत्तममिच्छता ।
योगश्च सादनीयो वै शत्रूणां निग्रहस्तथा ॥
2.43.m: Compassion should be shown to the wretched by one desiring the highest good; / yoga should indeed be practiced, and likewise the restraint of enemies.

2.43.s:
tvatsamo nāsti loke 'smiṃstejasā ca balena ca /
jñānena yaśasā vāpi sarvaśreṣṭhatamo bhavān //
2.43.d:
त्वत्समो नास्ति लोके ऽस्मिंस्तेजसा च बलेन च ।
ज्ञानेन यशसा वापि सर्वश्रेष्ठतमो भवान् ॥
2.43.m: There is no one equal to you in this world in splendor or strength; / in knowledge or fame, you shall be the foremost of all.

2.43.s:
atha svagṛhamāsādya pitroḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ kuru /
tapaścara yathākālaṃ tena siddhiḥ karasthitā //
2.43.d:
अथ स्वगृहमासाद्य पित्रोः शुश्रूषणं कुरु ।
तपश्चर यथाकालं तेन सिद्धिः करस्थिता ॥
2.43.m: Now, having reached your home, serve your parents; / practice asceticism at the proper time; through that, perfection will rest in your hand.

2.43.s:
rādhotsaṃgātsamutthāpya gaṇeśaṃ rādhikeśvaraḥ /
āliṅgya gāḍhaṃ rāseṇa maitrīṃ tasya cakāra ha //
2.43.d:
राधोत्संगात्समुत्थाप्य गणेशं राधिकेश्वरः ।
आलिङ्ग्य गाढं रासेण मैत्रीं तस्य चकार ह ॥
2.43.m: Raising Gaṇeśa from the lap of Rādhā, the Lord of Rādhikā / embraced him closely and, with delight, established friendship between him [and Rāma].

2.43.s:
athobhāvapi saṃprītau tadā rāmagaṇeśvarau /
kṛṣṇājñayā mahābhāgau babhūvaturarindama //
2.43.d:
अथोभावपि संप्रीतौ तदा रामगणेश्वरौ ।
कृष्णाज्ञया महाभागौ बभूवतुररिन्दम ॥
2.43.m: Then both of them, Rāma and the lord of the gaṇas, were well pleased, / and by Kṛṣṇa's command, O tamer of foes, those highly fortunate ones became [friends].

2.43.s:
etasminnantare devī rādhā kṛṣṇapriyā satī /
ubhābhyāṃ ca varaṃ prādātprasannāsyā mudānvitā //
2.43.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवी राधा कृष्णप्रिया सती ।
उभाभ्यां च वरं प्रादात्प्रसन्नास्या मुदान्विता ॥
2.43.m: In the meantime, the virtuous goddess Rādhā, beloved of Kṛṣṇa, / her face cheerful and filled with joy, granted a boon to both of them.

2.43.s:
rādhovāca /
sarvasya jagato vandyau durādharṣauṃ priyāvahau /
madbhaktau ca viśeṣeṇa bhavantau bhavatāṃ sutau //
2.43.d:
राधोवाच ।
सर्वस्य जगतो वन्द्यौ दुराधर्षौं प्रियावहौ ।
मद्भक्तौ च विशेषेण भवन्तौ भवतां सुतौ ॥
2.43.m: Rādhā said: / May both of you, my sons, be worthy of worship by the whole world, invincible, bringers of joy, / and especially devoted to me.

2.43.s:
bhavatornāma cauccārya yatkāryaṃ yaḥ samārabhet /
siddhiṃ prayātu tatasarvaṃ matprasādāddhi tasya tu //
2.43.d:
भवतोर्नाम चौच्चार्य यत्कार्यं यः समारभेत् ।
सिद्धिं प्रयातु ततसर्वं मत्प्रसादाद्धि तस्य तु ॥
2.43.m: And whatever undertaking anyone begins having uttered your two names, / may all of that attain success indeed by my grace!

2.43.s:
athovāca jaganmātā bhavānī bhavavallabhā /
vatsa rāma prasannāhaṃ tubhyaṃ kaṃ pradade varam /
taṃ prabrūhi mahābhāga bhayaṃ tyaktvā sudūrataḥ /
rāma uvāca
janmānta rasahasreṣu yeṣuyeṣu vrajāmyaham //
2.43.d:
अथोवाच जगन्माता भवानी भववल्लभा ।
वत्स राम प्रसन्नाहं तुभ्यं कं प्रददे वरम् ।
तं प्रब्रूहि महाभाग भयं त्यक्त्वा सुदूरतः ।
राम उवाच
जन्मान्त रसहस्रेषु येषुयेषु व्रजाम्यहम् ॥
2.43.m: Then Bhavānī, mother of the universe and beloved of Bhava, said: / “Child Rāma, I am pleased; what boon shall I grant you? / State it, O highly fortunate one, casting fear far away.” / Rāma said: / “In whichever thousands of other births I may wander,

2.43.s:
kṛṣṇayorbhavayorbhakto bhaviṣyāmīti dehi me /
abhedena ca paśyāmi kṛṣṇau cāpi bhavau tathā //
2.43.d:
कृष्णयोर्भवयोर्भक्तो भविष्यामीति देहि मे ।
अभेदेन च पश्यामि कृष्णौ चापि भवौ तथा ॥
2.43.m: grant me this: that I shall be a devotee of Kṛṣṇa and Bhava, / and that I may see Kṛṣṇa and Bhava without distinction!”

2.43.s:
pārvatyuvāca
evamastu mahābhāga bhakto 'si bhavakṛṣṇayoḥ /
cirañjīvī bhavāśu tvaṃ prasādānmama suvrata //
2.43.d:
पार्वत्युवाच
एवमस्तु महाभाग भक्तो ऽसि भवकृष्णयोः ।
चिरञ्जीवी भवाशु त्वं प्रसादान्मम सुव्रत ॥
2.43.m: Pārvatī said: / So be it, O highly fortunate one! You are a devotee of Bhava and Kṛṣṇa. / May you soon become long-lived by my grace, O you of good vows!

2.43.s:
athovāca dharādhīśaḥ prasannastamumāpatiḥ /
praṇataṃ bhārgavendraṃ tu varārhaṃ jagadīśvaraḥ //
2.43.d:
अथोवाच धराधीशः प्रसन्नस्तमुमापतिः ।
प्रणतं भार्गवेन्द्रं तु वरार्हं जगदीश्वरः ॥
2.43.m: Then the lord of the earth, the husband of Umā, Lord of the Universe, pleased, / spoke to that foremost Bhārgava, bowed down and worthy of boons.

2.43.s:
śiva uvāca
rāmabhakto 'si me vatsa yaste datto varo mayā /
sa bhaviṣyati kārtsyena satyamuktaṃ na cānyathā //
2.43.d:
शिव उवाच
रामभक्तो ऽसि मे वत्स यस्ते दत्तो वरो मया ।
स भविष्यति कार्त्स्येन सत्यमुक्तं न चान्यथा ॥
2.43.m: Śiva said: / O child, you are devoted to Rāma; the boon that was granted to you by me / will be completely fulfilled; it is spoken truthfully, not otherwise.

2.43.s:
adyaprabhṛti loke 'smin bhavato balavattaraḥ /
na ko 'pi bhavatādvatsa tejasvī ca bhavatparaḥ //
2.43.d:
अद्यप्रभृति लोके ऽस्मिन् भवतो बलवत्तरः ।
न को ऽपि भवताद्वत्स तेजस्वी च भवत्परः ॥
2.43.m: From this day forward in this world, let there be no one / stronger than you, O child, and no one more splendid than you.

2.43.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
atha kṛṣṇo 'pyanujñāpya śivaṃ ca naganandinīm /
golokaṃ prayayau yuktaḥ śrīdāmnā cāpi rādhayā //
2.43.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
अथ कृष्णो ऽप्यनुज्ञाप्य शिवं च नगनन्दिनीम् ।
गोलोकं प्रययौ युक्तः श्रीदाम्ना चापि राधया ॥
2.43.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Then Kṛṣṇa also, taking leave of Śiva and the daughter of the mountain, / departed for Goloka accompanied by Śrīdāman and Rādhā.

2.43.s:
atha rāmo 'pi dharmātmā bhavānīṃ ca bhavaṃ tathā /
saṃpūjya cābhivādyātha pradakṣiṇamupā kramīt //
2.43.d:
अथ रामो ऽपि धर्मात्मा भवानीं च भवं तथा ।
संपूज्य चाभिवाद्याथ प्रदक्षिणमुपा क्रमीत् ॥
2.43.m: Then the righteous Rāma, having worshipped / Bhavānī and Bhava and bowed to them, performed circumambulation.

2.43.s:
gaṇeśaṃ kārttikeyaṃ ca natvāpṛcchya ca bhūpate /
