akṛtavraṇasaṃyukto niścakrāma gṛhāntarāt //
2.43.d:
गणेशं कार्त्तिकेयं च नत्वापृच्छ्य च भूपते ।
अकृतव्रणसंयुक्तो निश्चक्राम गृहान्तरात् ॥
2.43.m: Having bowed to and taken leave of Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya, O king, / accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa, he went out from the interior of the house.

2.43.s:
niṣkramyamāṇo rāmastu nandīśvaramukhairgaṇaiḥ /
namaskṛto yayau rājansvagṛhaṃ parayā mudā //
iti śrī brahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamābhāge tṛtīya
upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite tricatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 43//
2.43.d:
निष्क्रम्यमाणो रामस्तु नन्दीश्वरमुखैर्गणैः ।
नमस्कृतो ययौ राजन्स्वगृहं परया मुदा ॥
इति श्री ब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमाभागे तृतीय
उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते त्रिचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 43॥
2.43.m:
Departing, Rāma was saluted by the gaṇas / led by Nandīśvara, O king, and went to his own home with supreme joy.

Thus ends the forty-third chapter, on the deeds of the Bhārgava, in the Upoddhātapāda, the third [part], in the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu. // 43

2.44.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
rājannevaṃ bhṛgurvidvānpaśyañjanapadānbahūn /
samājagāma dharmātmākṛtavraṇasamanvitaḥ //
2.44.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
राजन्नेवं भृगुर्विद्वान्पश्यञ्जनपदान्बहून् ।
समाजगाम धर्मात्माकृतव्रणसमन्वितः ॥
2.44.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / O king, thus the wise Bhṛgu, viewing many regions, / the righteous one, arrived accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa.

2.44.s:
nililyuḥ kṣattriyāḥ sarve yatra tatra nirīkṣya tam /
vrajantaṃ bhārgavaṃ mārge prāṇarakṣaṇatatparāḥ //
2.44.d:
निलिल्युः क्षत्त्रियाः सर्वे यत्र तत्र निरीक्ष्य तम् ।
व्रजन्तं भार्गवं मार्गे प्राणरक्षणतत्पराः ॥
2.44.m: All the kṣatriyas hid here and there upon seeing him, / the Bhārgava walking on the road, intent upon saving their lives.

2.44.s:
athāsasāda rājendra rāmaḥ svapiturāśramam /
śāntasattvasamākīrṇaṃ vedadhtraninināditam //
2.44.d:
अथाससाद राजेन्द्र रामः स्वपितुराश्रमम् ।
शान्तसत्त्वसमाकीर्णं वेदध्त्रनिनिनादितम् ॥
2.44.m: Then, O king of kings, Rāma reached his father’s hermitage, / crowded with peaceful living beings, resounding with the deep chanting of the Veda,

2.44.s:
yatra siṃhā mṛgā gāvo nāgamārjjāramūṣakāḥ /
samaṃ ca ranti saṃhṛṣṭā bhayaṃ tyaktvā sudūrataḥ //
2.44.d:
यत्र सिंहा मृगा गावो नागमार्ज्जारमूषकाः ।
समं च रन्ति संहृष्टा भयं त्यक्त्वा सुदूरतः ॥
2.44.m: where lions, deer, cows, elephants, cats, and mice / roam together delighted, having cast fear far away,

2.44.s:
yatra dhūmaṃ samīkṣyaiva hyagnihotrasamudbhavam /
unnadanti mayūrāśca nṛtyanti ca mahīpane //
2.44.d:
यत्र धूमं समीक्ष्यैव ह्यग्निहोत्रसमुद्भवम् ।
उन्नदन्ति मयूराश्च नृत्यन्ति च महीपने ॥
2.44.m: where, seeing the smoke rising from the agnihotra fire, / peacocks call out and dance, O ruler of the earth,

2.44.s:
yatra sāyantane kāle sūryasyābhimukhaṃ dvijaiḥ /
jalāñjalīnprakṣipadbhiḥ kriyate bhūrcalāvilā //
2.44.d:
यत्र सायन्तने काले सूर्यस्याभिमुखं द्विजैः ।
जलाञ्जलीन्प्रक्षिपद्भिः क्रियते भूर्चलाविला ॥
2.44.m: where at evening time, as the twice-born cast cupfuls of water with folded hands / toward the sun, the ground is made moist and muddy,

2.44.s:
yatrāntevāsibhirnityaṃ vedāḥ śāstrāṇi saṃhitāḥ /
abhyasyante mudā yuktairbrahmacaryavrate sthitaiḥ //
2.44.d:
यत्रान्तेवासिभिर्नित्यं वेदाः शास्त्राणि संहिताः ।
अभ्यस्यन्ते मुदा युक्तैर्ब्रह्मचर्यव्रते स्थितैः ॥
2.44.m: where the Vedas, śāstras, and saṃhitās are constantly / practiced by disciples filled with joy, established in the vow of brahmacarya.

2.44.s:
atha rāmaḥ prasannātmā paśyannāśramasaṃpadam /
praviveśa śanai rājannakṛtavraṇasaṃyutaḥ //
2.44.d:
अथ रामः प्रसन्नात्मा पश्यन्नाश्रमसंपदम् ।
प्रविवेश शनै राजन्नकृतव्रणसंयुतः ॥
2.44.m: Then Rāma, pleased in mind, beholding the splendor of the hermitage, / entered slowly, O king, accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa.

2.44.s:
jayaśabdaṃ namaḥśabdaṃ proccaradbhirdvijātmajaiḥ /
dvijaiśca satkṛto rāmaḥ paraṃ harṣamupāgataḥ //
2.44.d:
जयशब्दं नमःशब्दं प्रोच्चरद्भिर्द्विजात्मजैः ।
द्विजैश्च सत्कृतो रामः परं हर्षमुपागतः ॥
2.44.m: Honored with shouts of “Victory!” and “Salutations!” / uttered by the sons of twice-born and the twice-born themselves, Rāma experienced supreme joy.

2.44.s:
āśramābhyantare tatra saṃpraviśya nijaṃ gṛham /
dadarśa pitaraṃ rāmo jamadagniṃ taponidhim //
2.44.d:
आश्रमाभ्यन्तरे तत्र संप्रविश्य निजं गृहम् ।
ददर्श पितरं रामो जमदग्निं तपोनिधिम् ॥
2.44.m: Entering there into the interior of the hermitage, into his own home, / Rāma saw his father, Jamadagni, a treasury of asceticism,

2.44.s:
sākṣādbhṛgumivāsīnaṃ nigrahānugrahakṣamam /
papāta caraṇopānte hyaṣṭāṅgāliṅgitāvaniḥ //
2.44.d:
साक्षाद्भृगुमिवासीनं निग्रहानुग्रहक्षमम् ।
पपात चरणोपान्ते ह्यष्टाङ्गालिङ्गितावनिः ॥
2.44.m: seated like Bhṛgu in person, capable of punishing and showing grace; / he fell at the proximity of his feet, touching the ground with the eight limbs [of his body].

2.44.s:
rāmo 'haṃ tavā dāso 'smi proccaranniti bhūpate /
jagrāha caraṇau cāpi vidhivatsajjanāgraṇīḥ //
2.44.d:
रामो ऽहं तवा दासो ऽस्मि प्रोच्चरन्निति भूपते ।
जग्राह चरणौ चापि विधिवत्सज्जनाग्रणीः ॥
2.44.m: Saying aloud, “I am Rāma, your servant,” O king, / the foremost of virtuous men clasped his feet in accordance with rule.

2.44.s:
atha mātuśca caraṇavabhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ /
uvāca praṇato vākyaṃ tayoḥ saṃharṣakāraṇam //
2.44.d:
अथ मातुश्च चरणवभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः ।
उवाच प्रणतो वाक्यं तयोः संहर्षकारणम् ॥
2.44.m: Then, having greeted his mother’s feet with joined palms, / he, bowed down, spoke words that were a cause of joy for both of them.

2.44.s:
rāma uvāca
pitastava prabhāveṇa tapaso 'tidurāsadaḥ /
kārttavīryo hato yuddhe samutrabalavāhanaḥ //
2.44.d:
राम उवाच
पितस्तव प्रभावेण तपसो ऽतिदुरासदः ।
कार्त्तवीर्यो हतो युद्धे समुत्रबलवाहनः ॥
2.44.m:
Rāma said:
"Father, by the power of your asceticism, Kārttavīryārjuna,
who was exceedingly unassailable, was slain in battle along with his army and mounts.

2.44.s:
yaste 'parādhaṃ kṛtavānduṣṭamantripracoditaḥ /
tasya daṇḍo mayā dattaḥ prasahya munipuṅgava //
2.44.d:
यस्ते ऽपराधं कृतवान्दुष्टमन्त्रिप्रचोदितः ।
तस्य दण्डो मया दत्तः प्रसह्य मुनिपुङ्गव ॥
2.44.m:
The punishment for the wrong he committed against you, instigated by his evil ministers,
has been forcefully inflicted by me, O best of sages.

2.44.s:
bhavantaṃ tu namaskṛtya gato 'haṃ brahmaṇoṃ'tikam /
taṃ namaskṛtya vidhivatsvakāryaṃ pratyavedayam //
2.44.d:
भवन्तं तु नमस्कृत्य गतो ऽहं ब्रह्मणोंऽतिकम् ।
तं नमस्कृत्य विधिवत्स्वकार्यं प्रत्यवेदयम् ॥
2.44.m:
Having bowed to you, I went into the presence of Brahmā.
Having bowed to him according to rule, I reported my purpose.

2.44.s:
samāmuvāca bhagavāñchrutvā vṛttāntamāditaḥ /
vraja svakāryasiddhyarthaṃ śivalokaṃ sanātanam //
2.44.d:
समामुवाच भगवाञ्छ्रुत्वा वृत्तान्तमादितः ।
व्रज स्वकार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं शिवलोकं सनातनम् ॥
2.44.m:
Having heard the entire account from the beginning, the Blessed One said to me:
'Go to the eternal world of Śiva for the accomplishment of your purpose.'

2.44.s:
śrutvāhaṃ tadvayastāta namaskṛtya pitā maham /
gatavāñchivalokaṃ vai haradarśanakāṅkṣayā //
2.44.d:
श्रुत्वाहं तद्वयस्तात नमस्कृत्य पिता महम् ।
गतवाञ्छिवलोकं वै हरदर्शनकाङ्क्षया ॥
2.44.m:
Having heard his word, O father, and having bowed to the Grandfather,
I went to the world of Śiva, desiring a vision of Hara.

2.44.s:
praviśya tatra bhagavannumayā sahitaḥ śivaḥ /
namaskṛto mayā devo vāñchitārtha pradāyakaḥ //
2.44.d:
प्रविश्य तत्र भगवन्नुमया सहितः शिवः ।
नमस्कृतो मया देवो वाञ्छितार्थ प्रदायकः ॥
2.44.m:
Having entered there, O blessed one, Śiva, who is accompanied by Umā
and who bestows desired boons, was saluted by me.

2.44.s:
tadagre nikhilaḥ svīyo vṛttānto viniveditaḥ /
mayā samāhitadhiyā sa sarvaṃ śrutavānapi //
2.44.d:
तदग्रे निखिलः स्वीयो वृत्तान्तो विनिवेदितः ।
मया समाहितधिया स सर्वं श्रुतवानपि ॥
2.44.m:
Before him, my whole account was related
by me with an attentive mind, and he heard it all.

2.44.s:
śrutvā vicārya ta tsarvaṃ dadau mahyaṃ kṛpānvitaḥ /
trailokyavijayaṃ nāma kavacaṃ sarvasiddhidam //
2.44.d:
श्रुत्वा विचार्य त त्सर्वं ददौ मह्यं कृपान्वितः ।
त्रैलोक्यविजयं नाम कवचं सर्वसिद्धिदम् ॥
2.44.m:
Having heard and considered all that, full of compassion he gave to me
the armour named Trailokyavijaya, which grants all accomplishments.

2.44.s:
tallabdhvā taṃ namaskṛtya puṣkaraṃ samupāgataḥ /
tatrāhaṃ sādhayitvā tu kavacaṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ //
2.44.d:
तल्लब्ध्वा तं नमस्कृत्य पुष्करं समुपागतः ।
तत्राहं साधयित्वा तु कवचं हृष्टमानसः ॥
2.44.m:
Having obtained that and bowed to him, I went to Puṣkara.
There, having perfected the armour, with a joyful mind,

2.44.s:
kārttavīryaṃ nihatyājau śivalokaṃ punargataḥ /
tatra tau tu mayā dṛṣṭau dvāre skandavināyakau //
2.44.d:
कार्त्तवीर्यं निहत्याजौ शिवलोकं पुनर्गतः ।
तत्र तौ तु मया दृष्टौ द्वारे स्कन्दविनायकौ ॥
2.44.m:
having slain Kārttavīryārjuna in battle, I went once more to the world of Śiva.
There, Skanda and Vināyaka were seen by me at the gate.

2.44.s:
taunamaskṛtya dharmajña praveṣṭuṃ codyato 'bhavam /
sa māmavekṣya gāmapo viśantaṃ tvarayānvitam //
2.44.d:
तौनमस्कृत्य धर्मज्ञ प्रवेष्टुं चोद्यतो ऽभवम् ।
स मामवेक्ष्य गामपो विशन्तं त्वरयान्वितम् ॥
2.44.m:
Having bowed to them, O knower of dharma, I prepared to enter.
Seeing me entering with haste, the protector of the followers

2.44.s:
vārayāmāsa sahasā nādyāvasara ityatha /
mama tena pitastatra vāgyuddhaṃ hastakarṣaṇam //
2.44.d:
वारयामास सहसा नाद्यावसर इत्यथ ।
मम तेन पितस्तत्र वाग्युद्धं हस्तकर्षणम् ॥
2.44.m:
stopped me abruptly, saying, 'Now is not the time.'
Then, O father, there arose between me and him a battle of words and seizing of hands.

2.44.s:
sañjātaparaśukṣemamato 'bhūdbhṛgunandana /
sa tajjñātvā samudgṛhya māmadhaścorddhvameva ca //
2.44.d:
सञ्जातपरशुक्षेममतो ऽभूद्भृगुनन्दन ।
स तज्ज्ञात्वा समुद्गृह्य मामधश्चोर्द्ध्वमेव च ॥
2.44.m:
From that, O descendant of Bhṛgu, an exchange of axe-blows arose.
Realising that, he grasped me, and upwards and downwards

2.44.s:
kareṇa bhrāmayāmāsa punaścānītavāṃstataḥ /
taṃ dṛṣṭvātikrudhā kṣiptaḥ kuṭhāro hi mayā tataḥ //
2.44.d:
करेण भ्रामयामास पुनश्चानीतवांस्ततः ।
तं दृष्ट्वातिक्रुधा क्षिप्तः कुठारो हि मया ततः ॥
2.44.m:
swung me around with his trunk, and then brought me back again.
Seeing him, in intense anger the axe was hurled by me.

2.44.s:
danto nipati,stasya tato deva upāgataḥ /
pārvatī tatra ruṣṭābhūttadā kṛṣṇaḥ samāgataḥ //
2.44.d:
दन्तो निपति,स्तस्य ततो देव उपागतः ।
पार्वती तत्र रुष्टाभूत्तदा कृष्णः समागतः ॥
2.44.m:
His tusk fell off, and then the god arrived.
Pārvatī became angry there; at that time Kṛṣṇa arrived.

2.44.s:
rādhayā sahitastena sānunītā varaṃ dadau /
mahyaṃ kṛṣmo jagāmātha tena maitrīṃ vidhāya ca //
2.44.d:
राधया सहितस्तेन सानुनीता वरं ददौ ।
मह्यं कृष्मो जगामाथ तेन मैत्रीं विधाय च ॥
2.44.m:
Together with Rādhā, by him she was conciliated, and she granted a boon
to me. Then Kṛṣṇa, having forged friendship with him, departed.

2.44.s:
tataḥ praṇamya deveśau pārvatīparameśvarau /
āgatastava sānnidhyamakṛtavraṇasaṃyutaḥ //
2.44.d:
ततः प्रणम्य देवेशौ पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ।
आगतस्तव सान्निध्यमकृतव्रणसंयुतः ॥
2.44.m:
Then, having bowed to the two supreme rulers of the gods, Pārvatī and Parameśvara,
I have come into your presence, accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa."

2.44.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityaktvā bhārgavo rāmo virarāma ca bhūpate /
jamadagniruvācedaṃ rāmaṃ śatrunibarhaṇam //
2.44.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्यक्त्वा भार्गवो रामो विरराम च भूपते ।
जमदग्निरुवाचेदं रामं शत्रुनिबर्हणम् ॥
2.44.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Having spoken thus, Rāma the Bhārgava fell silent, O king.
Jamadagni said this to Rāma, the destroyer of foes:

2.44.s:
jamadagniruvāca
kṣatrahatyābhibhūtastvaṃ tāvaddoṣopaśāntaye /
prayaścittaṃ tatastāvadyathāvatkartumarhasi //
2.44.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच
क्षत्रहत्याभिभूतस्त्वं तावद्दोषोपशान्तये ।
प्रयश्चित्तं ततस्तावद्यथावत्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
2.44.m:
Jamadagni said:
"You are overcome by the sin of slaying kṣatriyas; therefore, for the pacification of that fault,
you ought to perform penance properly at once."

2.44.s:
ityuktaḥ prāha pitaraṃ rāmo matimatāṃ varaḥ /
prāyaścittaṃ tu tadyogyaṃ tvaṃ me nirdeṣṭumarhasi //
2.44.d:
इत्युक्तः प्राह पितरं रामो मतिमतां वरः ।
प्रायश्चित्तं तु तद्योग्यं त्वं मे निर्देष्टुमर्हसि ॥
2.44.m:
Being addressed thus, Rāma, best among the wise, said to his father:
"You ought to instruct me in the penance that is fitting for it."

2.44.s:
jamadagniruvāca
vrataiśca niyamaiścaiva karṣayandehamātmanaḥ /
śākamūlaphalāhāro dvādaśābdaṃ tapaścara //
2.44.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच
व्रतैश्च नियमैश्चैव कर्षयन्देहमात्मनः ।
शाकमूलफलाहारो द्वादशाब्दं तपश्चर ॥
2.44.m:
Jamadagni said:
"Mortifying your own body with vows and observances,
subsisting on vegetables, roots, and fruits, practice asceticism for twelve years."

2.44.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityuktaḥ praṇipatyainaṃ mātaraṃ ca bhṛgūdvahaḥ /
prayayau tapase rājannakṛtavraṇasaṃyutaḥ //
2.44.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्युक्तः प्रणिपत्यैनं मातरं च भृगूद्वहः ।
प्रययौ तपसे राजन्नकृतव्रणसंयुतः ॥
2.44.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Being addressed thus, that descendant of Bhṛgu bowed to him and to his mother,
and set out for asceticism, O king, accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa.

2.44.s:
sa gatvā parvata varaṃ mahendramarikarṣaṇaḥ /
kṛtvā'śramapadaṃ tasmiṃstapastepe suduścaram //
2.44.d:
स गत्वा पर्वत वरं महेन्द्रमरिकर्षणः ।
कृत्वाऽश्रमपदं तस्मिंस्तपस्तेपे सुदुश्चरम् ॥
2.44.m:
Having gone to Mahendra, the excellent mountain, the crusher of enemies
established a hermitage upon it and performed severe asceticism.

2.44.s:
vrataistapobhirniyamairdevatārādhanairapi /
ninye varṣāṇi kati cidrāmastasminmahāmanāḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde
sagaropākhyāne bhārgavacarite catuścatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 44//
2.44.d:
व्रतैस्तपोभिर्नियमैर्देवताराधनैरपि ।
निन्ये वर्षाणि कति चिद्रामस्तस्मिन्महामनाः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे
सगरोपाख्याने भार्गवचरिते चतुश्चत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 44॥
2.44.m:
Through vows, austerities, observances, and worship of deities,
the noble-minded Rāma spent several years there.

Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter in the Bhārgavacarita of the Sagaropākhyāna, in the third Upoddhātapāda of the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.45.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tataḥ kadācidvipine caturaṅgabalānvitaḥ /
mṛgayāmagamacchūraḥ śūrasenādibhiḥ saha //
2.45.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
ततः कदाचिद्विपिने चतुरङ्गबलान्वितः ।
मृगयामगमच्छूरः शूरसेनादिभिः सह ॥
2.45.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
Then once in the forest, accompanied by a fourfold army,
the heroic [king] went hunting along with Śūrasena and others.

2.45.s:
te praviśya mahāraṇyaṃ hatvā bahuvidhānmṛgān /
jagmustṛṣārttā madhyāhne saritaṃ narmadāmanu //
2.45.d:
ते प्रविश्य महारण्यं हत्वा बहुविधान्मृगान् ।
जग्मुस्तृषार्त्ता मध्याह्ने सरितं नर्मदामनु ॥
2.45.m:
Having entered the great wilderness and slain many kinds of deer,
they went, afflicted with thirst at midday, along the river Narmadā.

2.45.s:
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca vāri nadyā gataśramāḥ /
gacchanto dadṛśurmārgo jamadagnerathāśramam //
2.45.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च वारि नद्या गतश्रमाः ।
गच्छन्तो ददृशुर्मार्गो जमदग्नेरथाश्रमम् ॥
2.45.m:
Having bathed there and drunk the water of the river, their weariness gone,
as they were proceeding on their path, they saw the hermitage of Jamadagni.

2.45.s:
ddaṣṭvāśramapadaṃ ramyaṃ munīnāgacchataḥ pathi /
kasyedamiti papracchurbhāvikarmapracoditāḥ //
2.45.d:
द्दष्ट्वाश्रमपदं रम्यं मुनीनागच्छतः पथि ।
कस्येदमिति पप्रच्छुर्भाविकर्मप्रचोदिताः ॥
2.45.m:
Seeing that lovely hermitage and sages walking on the path,
impelled by their future destiny, they asked, 'Whose is this?'

2.45.s:
te procuratiśāntātmā jamadagnermahātapāḥ /
vasatyasminsuto yasya rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ //
2.45.d:
ते प्रोचुरतिशान्तात्मा जमदग्नेर्महातपाः ।
वसत्यस्मिन्सुतो यस्य रामः शस्त्रभृतां वरः ॥
2.45.m:
They replied, 'In this resides Jamadagni, of exceedingly peaceful mind and great austerity,
whose son is Rāma, best of weapon-bearers.'

2.45.s:
tachrutvā bhīrabhūtteṣāṃ rāmanāmānukīrttanāt /
krodhaṃ prasaṅyānṛśaṃsyaṃ pūrvavairamanusmaran //
2.45.d:
तछ्रुत्वा भीरभूत्तेषां रामनामानुकीर्त्तनात् ।
क्रोधं प्रसङ्यानृशंस्यं पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् ॥
2.45.m:
Hearing that, fear arose in them from the utterance of Rāma's name;
[yet] giving way to anger and cruelty, remembering their former enmity,

2.45.s:
atha te procuranyonyaṃ pitṛhanturvadhātpituḥ /
vaira niryātanaṃ kiṃ tu kariṣyāmo diśādhunā //
2.45.d:
अथ ते प्रोचुरन्योन्यं पितृहन्तुर्वधात्पितुः ।
वैर निर्यातनं किं तु करिष्यामो दिशाधुना ॥
2.45.m:
they said to one another: 'By slaying the slayer of our father,
shall we not avenge our father's enmity now in this region?'

2.45.s:
ityaktvā khaḍgahastāste saṃpraviśya tadāśramam /
prajāghnire prayāteṣu munivīreṣu sarvataḥ //
2.45.d:
इत्यक्त्वा खड्गहस्तास्ते संप्रविश्य तदाश्रमम् ।
प्रजाघ्निरे प्रयातेषु मुनिवीरेषु सर्वतः ॥
2.45.m:
Having spoken thus, holding swords in their hands, they entered that hermitage
and struck him down when the heroic sages had dispersed everywhere.

2.45.s:
taṃ hatvāsya śiro hṛtvā niṣādā iva nirdayāḥ /
prayayuste durātmānaḥ sabalāḥ svapurīṃ prati //
2.45.d:
तं हत्वास्य शिरो हृत्वा निषादा इव निर्दयाः ।
प्रययुस्ते दुरात्मानः सबलाः स्वपुरीं प्रति ॥
2.45.m:
Having slain him and severed his head like pitiless Niṣādas,
those evil-minded ones, accompanied by their forces, set out toward their own city.

2.45.s:
putrāstasya mahātmānau dṛṣṭvā svapitaraṃ hatam /
parivārya mahārāja ruruduḥ śokakarśitāḥ //
2.45.d:
पुत्रास्तस्य महात्मानौ दृष्ट्वा स्वपितरं हतम् ।
परिवार्य महाराज रुरुदुः शोककर्शिताः ॥
2.45.m:
Seeing their father slain, his noble sons
surrounded him, O great king, and wept, emaciated with sorrow.

2.45.s:
bharttāraṃ nihataṃ bhūmau patitaṃ vīkṣya reṇukā /
papāta mūrcchitā sadyo latevāśanitāḍitā //
2.45.d:
भर्त्तारं निहतं भूमौ पतितं वीक्ष्य रेणुका ।
पपात मूर्च्छिता सद्यो लतेवाशनिताडिता ॥
2.45.m:
Seeing her husband slain, fallen on the ground, Reṇukā
fell unconscious at once, like a creeper struck by lightning.

2.45.s:
sā svacetasi saṃmūcchya śokapāvakadīpitāḥ /
dūrapranaṣṭasaṃjñeva sadyaḥ prāṇairvyayujyata //
2.45.d:
सा स्वचेतसि संमूच्छ्य शोकपावकदीपिताः ।
दूरप्रनष्टसंज्ञेव सद्यः प्राणैर्व्ययुज्यत ॥
2.45.m:
Fainting in her mind, blazing with the fire of sorrow,
her consciousness entirely lost as it were, she was immediately separated from her life-breaths.

2.45.s:
anālapantyāṃ tasyāṃ tu saṃjñāṃ yātā hi te punaḥ /
nyapatanmūrcchitā bhūmau nimagnāḥ śokasāgare //
2.45.d:
अनालपन्त्यां तस्यां तु संज्ञां याता हि ते पुनः ।
न्यपतन्मूर्च्छिता भूमौ निमग्नाः शोकसागरे ॥
2.45.m:
When she did not speak, [the sons,] having regained consciousness,
fell unconscious to the ground once more, plunged in an ocean of grief.

2.45.s:
tatastapodhanā ye 'nye tatta povanavāsinaḥ /
sametyāśvāsayāmāsustulyaduḥkhāḥ sutānmune //
2.45.d:
ततस्तपोधना ये ऽन्ये तत्त पोवनवासिनः ।
समेत्याश्वासयामासुस्तुल्यदुःखाः सुतान्मुने ॥
2.45.m:
Then the other ascetics residing in that penance grove,
coming together, consoled the sons of the sage, sharing their grief.

2.45.s:
sāṃtvyamānā munigaṇairjāmadagnyā yathāvidhi /
ādhakṣurvacasā teṣāmagnau pitroḥ kalevare //
2.45.d:
सांत्व्यमाना मुनिगणैर्जामदग्न्या यथाविधि ।
आधक्षुर्वचसा तेषामग्नौ पित्रोः कलेवरे ॥
2.45.m:
Being consoled by the hosts of sages according to rule, the sons of Jamadagni,
at their word, burned the bodies of their two parents in fire.

2.45.s:
cakrureva tadūrddhvaṃ vai yatkarttavyamanantaram /
pitrormaraṇaduḥkhena pīḍyamānā divāniśam //
2.45.d:
चक्रुरेव तदूर्द्ध्वं वै यत्कर्त्तव्यमनन्तरम् ।
पित्रोर्मरणदुःखेन पीड्यमाना दिवानिशम् ॥
2.45.m:
Thereafter, they indeed performed whatever rites had to be done next,
tormented day and night by the grief of their parents' death.

2.45.s:
tataḥ kāle gate rāmaḥ samānāṃ dvādaśāvadhau /
nivṛttastapasaḥ sakhyā sahāgādāśramaṃ pituḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge sagaropākhyāne
bhārgavacarite pañcacatvāriṃśattamodhyāyaḥ // 45//
2.45.d:
ततः काले गते रामः समानां द्वादशावधौ ।
निवृत्तस्तपसः सख्या सहागादाश्रमं पितुः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे सगरोपाख्याने
भार्गवचरिते पञ्चचत्वारिंशत्तमोध्यायः ॥ 45॥
2.45.m:
Then, when the time had passed to the limit of twelve years,
Rāma, returned from his asceticism, came with his friend to his father's hermitage.

Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter in the Bhārgavacarita of the Sagaropākhyāna, in the middle section of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

2.46.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
sagacchanpathi śuśrāva munibhyasta ttvamāditaḥ /
rājaputravyavasitaṃ pitrauḥ svargatimeva ca //
2.46.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
सगच्छन्पथि शुश्राव मुनिभ्यस्त त्त्वमादितः ।
राजपुत्रव्यवसितं पित्रौः स्वर्गतिमेव च ॥

2.46.s:
pitustu jīvaharaṇaṃ śiroharaṇameva ca /
tanmṛtereva maraṇaṃ śrutvā mātuśca kevalam //
2.46.d:
पितुस्तु जीवहरणं शिरोहरणमेव च ।
तन्मृतेरेव मरणं श्रुत्वा मातुश्च केवलम् ॥
2.46.m:
the taking of his father's life and the cutting off of his head,
and hearing of the death of his mother solely from his death,

2.46.s:
vilalāpa mahābāhurduḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ /
tamathāśvāsayāmāsa tulyaduḥkho 'kṛtavraṇaḥ //
2.46.d:
विललाप महाबाहुर्दुःखशोकसमन्वितः ।
तमथाश्वासयामास तुल्यदुःखो ऽकृतव्रणः ॥
2.46.m:
the mighty-armed one lamented, overcome with pain and sorrow.
Then Akṛtavraṇa, sharing his grief, consoled him.

2.46.s:
hetubhiḥ śāstranirdiṣṭair vīryasāmarthyasūcakaiḥ /
yuktilaukikadṛṣṭāntaistacchokaṃ saṃvyaśāmayat //
2.46.d:
हेतुभिः शास्त्रनिर्दिष्टैर् वीर्यसामर्थ्यसूचकैः ।
युक्तिलौकिकदृष्टान्तैस्तच्छोकं संव्यशामयत् ॥
2.46.m: With reasons taught in the scriptures indicative of strength and valour, / with logical arguments and worldly examples, he completely appeased that grief.

2.46.s:
sāṃtvitastena maidhāvī dhṛtimālaṃbya bhārgavaḥ /
prayayau sahitaḥ sakhyā bhrātṝṇāṃ tu didṛkṣayā //
2.46.d:
सांत्वितस्तेन मैधावी धृतिमालंब्य भार्गवः ।
प्रययौ सहितः सख्या भ्रातॄणां तु दिदृक्षया ॥
2.46.m: Consoled by him, the wise Bhārgava, taking hold of his resolve, / departed along with his friend, wishing to see his brothers.

2.46.s:
sa tāndṛṣṭvābhivādyaitānduḥkhitānduḥkhakarśitaḥ /
śokāmaṣayutastaiśca saha tsthau dinatrayam //
2.46.d:
स तान्दृष्ट्वाभिवाद्यैतान्दुःखितान्दुःखकर्शितः ।
शोकामषयुतस्तैश्च सह त्स्थौ दिनत्रयम् ॥
2.46.m: Having seen them, emaciated with grief, he saluted those sorrowful ones; / filled with grief and wrath, he stayed with them for three days.

2.46.s:
tato 'sya sumāhānkrodhaḥ smarato nidhanaṃ pituḥ /
babhūva sahasā sarvalokasaṃharaṇakṣamaḥ //
2.46.d:
ततो ऽस्य सुमाहान्क्रोधः स्मरतो निधनं पितुः ।
बभूव सहसा सर्वलोकसंहरणक्षमः ॥
2.46.m: Then, as he remembered his father's death, an immense wrath arose / suddenly in him, capable of destroying all the worlds.

2.46.s:
māturarthe kṛtāṃ pūrvaṃ pratijñāṃ satyasaṃgaraḥ /
dṛḍhīcakāra hṛdaye sarvakṣatravadhodyataḥ //
2.46.d:
मातुरर्थे कृतां पूर्वं प्रतिज्ञां सत्यसंगरः ।
दृढीचकार हृदये सर्वक्षत्रवधोद्यतः ॥
2.46.m: True to his promise, he made firm in his heart / the vow previously made for his mother's sake, intent on slaying all kṣatriyas.

2.46.s:
kṣatravaṃśyānaśeṣeṇa hatvā taddehalohitaiḥ /
kariṣye tarpaṇaṃ pitroriti niścitya bhārgavaḥ //
2.46.d:
क्षत्रवंश्यानशेषेण हत्वा तद्देहलोहितैः ।
करिष्ये तर्पणं पित्रोरिति निश्चित्य भार्गवः ॥
2.46.m: "Having completely slain the descendants of the kṣatriya lineage, / I shall make libations to my parents with the blood of their bodies"—having thus resolved, the Bhārgava,

2.46.s:
bhrātṝṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāmākhyāyātmasamīhitam /
prayayau tadanujñātaḥ kṛtvā saṃsthāṃpituḥ kriyām //
2.46.d:
भ्रातॄणां चैव सर्वेषामाख्यायात्मसमीहितम् ।
प्रययौ तदनुज्ञातः कृत्वा संस्थांपितुः क्रियाम् ॥
2.46.m: disclosed his intention to all his brothers; / having performed the funeral rites for his father and permitted by them, he set forth.

2.46.s:
akṛtavraṇasaṃyuktaḥ prāpya māhiṣmatīṃ tataḥ /
tadbāhyopavane sthitvā sasmāra sa mahodaram //
2.46.d:
अकृतव्रणसंयुक्तः प्राप्य माहिष्मतीं ततः ।
तद्बाह्योपवने स्थित्वा सस्मार स महोदरम् ॥
2.46.m: Accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa, he then reached Māhiṣmatī; / staying in its outer park, he remembered Mahodara.

2.46.s:
sa tasmai rathacāpādyaṃ sahasāśvasamanvitam /
preṣayāmāsa rāmāya sarvasaṃhananāni ca //
2.46.d:
स तस्मै रथचापाद्यं सहसाश्वसमन्वितम् ।
प्रेषयामास रामाय सर्वसंहननानि च ॥
2.46.m: He quickly sent to that Rāma a chariot, bows, and other weapons, / along with horses, and all forms of body armour.

2.46.s:
rāmo 'pi rathamāruhya sannaddhaḥ saśaraṃ dhanuḥ /
gṛhītvāpūrayacchaṅkhaṃ rudradattamamitrajit //
2.46.d:
रामो ऽपि रथमारुह्य सन्नद्धः सशरं धनुः ।
गृहीत्वापूरयच्छङ्खं रुद्रदत्तममित्रजित् ॥
2.46.m: Mounting the chariot and clad in armour, Rāma, conqueror of enemies, / took his bow along with arrows and blew the conch given by Rudra.

2.46.s:
jyāghoṣaṃ ca cakāroccai rodasī kaṃpayanniva /
sahasāhotha sārathyaṃ cakre sārathināṃ varaḥ //
2.46.d:
ज्याघोषं च चकारोच्चै रोदसी कंपयन्निव ।
सहसाहोथ सारथ्यं चक्रे सारथिनां वरः ॥
2.46.m: And he made a twang of the bowstring loudly, as if shaking heaven and earth; / then Sahasāha, the best of charioteers, took charge of the driving.

2.46.s:
rathajyāśaṅkhanādaistu vadhātpitroramarṣiṇaḥ /
tasyābhūnnagarī sarvā saṃkṣubdhāśca naradvipāḥ //
2.46.d:
रथज्याशङ्खनादैस्तु वधात्पित्रोरमर्षिणः ।
तस्याभून्नगरी सर्वा संक्षुब्धाश्च नरद्विपाः ॥
2.46.m: By the sounds of the chariot, the bowstring, and the conch of him who was enraged by the murder of his parents, / that entire city was agitated, and its men and elephants were shaken.

2.46.s:
rāmaṃ tvāgatamājñāya sarvakṣatrakulāntakam /
saṃkṣubdhāścakrurudyogaṃ saṃgrāmāya nṛpātmajāḥ //
2.46.d:
रामं त्वागतमाज्ञाय सर्वक्षत्रकुलान्तकम् ।
संक्षुब्धाश्चक्रुरुद्योगं संग्रामाय नृपात्मजाः ॥
2.46.m: Having learnt that Rāma had arrived, the exterminator of the entire kṣatriya race, / the agitated sons of the king made preparation for battle.

2.46.s:
atha pañcarathāḥ śurāḥ śūrasenādayo nṛpa /
rāmeṇa yoddhuṃ sahitā rājabhiśca krurudyamam //
2.46.d:
अथ पञ्चरथाः शुराः शूरसेनादयो नृप ।
रामेण योद्धुं सहिता राजभिश्च क्रुरुद्यमम् ॥
2.46.m: Then the five charioteers, heroic Śūrasena and the others, O king, / joined with kings and made an effort to fight against Rāma.

2.46.s:
caturaṅgavalopetāstataste kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ /
rāmamāsādayāmāsuḥ pataṅgā iva pāvakam //
2.46.d:
चतुरङ्गवलोपेतास्ततस्ते क्षत्रियर्षभाः ।
राममासादयामासुः पतङ्गा इव पावकम् ॥
2.46.m: Endowed with fourfold armies, those bulls among kṣatriyas / then rushed at Rāma like moths into a fire.

2.46.s:
nivārya tānāpatato rathenaikena bhārgavaḥ /
yuyudhe pārthivaiḥ sarvaiḥ samare 'mitavikramaḥ //
2.46.d:
निवार्य तानापततो रथेनैकेन भार्गवः ।
युयुधे पार्थिवैः सर्वैः समरे ऽमितविक्रमः ॥
2.46.m: Warding them off as they rushed on, the Bhārgava of immeasurable prowess / fought with all the kings in battle with a single chariot.

2.46.s:
tataḥ punarabhūdyuddhaṃ rāmasya saha rājabhiḥ /
jaghāna yatra saṃkruddho rājñāṃ śatamudāradhīḥ //
2.46.d:
ततः पुनरभूद्युद्धं रामस्य सह राजभिः ।
जघान यत्र संक्रुद्धो राज्ञां शतमुदारधीः ॥
2.46.m: Then once again a battle took place between Rāma and the kings, / wherein the high-minded one, intensely enraged, slew a hundred kings.

2.46.s:
tataḥ sa śūrasenādīnhatvā sabalavāhanān /
traṇena pātayāmāsa kṣitau kṣatriyamaṇḍalam //
2.46.d:
ततः स शूरसेनादीन्हत्वा सबलवाहनान् ।
त्रणेन पातयामास क्षितौ क्षत्रियमण्डलम् ॥
2.46.m: Then, having slain Śūrasena and the others along with their armies and mounts, / he felled the host of kṣatriyas to the earth in an instant.

2.46.s:
tataste bhagnasaṃkalpā hatasvabalavāhanāḥ /
hataśiṣṭā nṛpatayo dudruvuḥ sarvatodiśam //
2.46.d:
ततस्ते भग्नसंकल्पा हतस्वबलवाहनाः ।
हतशिष्टा नृपतयो दुद्रुवुः सर्वतोदिशम् ॥
2.46.m: Then, their resolves broken, their armies and mounts destroyed, / the kings who survived the slaughter fled in all directions.

2.46.s:
evaṃ vidrāvya sainyāni hatvā jitvātha saṃyuge /
jaghāna śataśo rājñaḥ śūrāñcharavarāgninā //
2.46.d:
एवं विद्राव्य सैन्यानि हत्वा जित्वाथ संयुगे ।
जघान शतशो राज्ञः शूराञ्छरवराग्निना ॥
2.46.m: Having thus routed the armies, having slain and conquered in battle, / he killed hundreds of kings and heroes with the fire of his excellent arrows.

2.46.s:
tataḥ krodhaparītātmā dagdhukāmo 'khilāṃ purīm /
udairayadbhārgavo 'straṃ kālāgnisadṛśaprabham //
2.46.d:
ततः क्रोधपरीतात्मा दग्धुकामो ऽखिलां पुरीम् ।
उदैरयद्भार्गवो ऽस्त्रं कालाग्निसदृशप्रभम् ॥
2.46.m: Then, his mind consumed with anger, wishing to burn down the entire city, / the Bhārgava unleashed a divine weapon possessing splendour like the fire of dissolution.

2.46.s:
jvālākavalitāśeṣapuraprākāramālinīm /
purīṃ sahastyaśvanarāṃ sa dadāhāstrapāvakaḥ //
2.46.d:
ज्वालाकवलिताशेषपुरप्राकारमालिनीम् ।
पुरीं सहस्त्यश्वनरां स ददाहास्त्रपावकः ॥
2.46.m: Swallowing all the lines of city ramparts in flames, / that weapon-fire burned down the city together with its elephants, horses, and men.

2.46.s:
dahyamānāṃ purīṃ dṛṣṭvā prāṇatrāṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
jīvanāya jagāmāśu vītihotro bhayāturaḥ //
2.46.d:
दह्यमानां पुरीं दृष्ट्वा प्राणत्राणपरायणः ।
जीवनाय जगामाशु वीतिहोत्रो भयातुरः ॥
2.46.m: Seeing the city being burnt down, intent on saving his life, / Vītihotra quickly fled to survive, stricken with fear.

2.46.s:
astrāgninā purīṃ sarvāṃ dagdhvā hatvā ca śātravān /
prāśayāno 'khilān lokān sākṣātkāla ivāntakaḥ //
2.46.d:
अस्त्राग्निना पुरीं सर्वां दग्ध्वा हत्वा च शात्रवान् ।
प्राशयानो ऽखिलान् लोकान् साक्षात्काल इवान्तकः ॥
2.46.m: Having burnt the whole city with the weapon-fire and slain his foes, / he seemed to swallow all the worlds like Kāla, the Ender himself.

2.46.s:
akṛtavraṇasaṃyuktaḥ sahasāhena cānvitaḥ /
jagāmarathaghoṣeṇa kaṃpayanniva medinīm //
2.46.d:
अकृतव्रणसंयुक्तः सहसाहेन चान्वितः ।
जगामरथघोषेण कंपयन्निव मेदिनीम् ॥
2.46.m: Accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa and joined by Sahasāha, / he went, as if shaking the earth with the roar of his chariot.

2.46.s:
vinighnan kṣatriyānsarvān saṃśāmya pṛthivītale /
mahendrādriṃ yayau rāmastapase dhatamānasaḥ //
2.46.d:
विनिघ्नन् क्षत्रियान्सर्वान् संशाम्य पृथिवीतले ।
महेन्द्राद्रिं ययौ रामस्तपसे धतमानसः ॥
2.46.m: Striking down all the kṣatriyas, bringing peace to the earth's surface, / Rāma, his mind fixed on austerity, went to Mount Mahendra.

2.46.s:
tasminnaṣṭacatuṣkaṃ ca yāvatkṣatrasamudgamam /
pratyetya bhūyastaddhatyai baddhadīkṣo dhṛtavrataḥ //
2.46.d:
तस्मिन्नष्टचतुष्कं च यावत्क्षत्रसमुद्गमम् ।
प्रत्येत्य भूयस्तद्धत्यै बद्धदीक्षो धृतव्रतः ॥
2.46.m: Having bound himself by consecration and observed vows, he returned / for their slaughter after thirty-two [years], when the kṣatriyas rose again.

2.46.s:
kṣatrakṣetreṣu bhūyaśca kṣatramutpāditaṃ dvijaiḥ /
nijaghāna punarbhūmau rājña śatasahasraśaḥ //
2.46.d:
क्षत्रक्षेत्रेषु भूयश्च क्षत्रमुत्पादितं द्विजैः ।
निजघान पुनर्भूमौ राज्ञ शतसहस्रशः ॥
2.46.m: And in the kṣatriya wives, kṣatriyas were begotten anew by Brahmins; / he struck down kings on the earth again by the hundreds and thousands.

2.46.s:
varṣadvayena bhūyo 'pi kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyāṃ mahīm /
ṣaṭcatuṣṭayavarṣāntaṃ tapastepe punaśca saḥ //
2.46.d:
वर्षद्वयेन भूयो ऽपि कृत्वा निःक्षत्रियां महीम् ।
षट्चतुष्टयवर्षान्तं तपस्तेपे पुनश्च सः ॥
2.46.m: Having made the earth devoid of kṣatriyas once more within two years, / he again performed austerity for twenty-four years.

2.46.s:
bhūyo 'pi rājan saṃbuddhaṃ kṣatramutpāditaṃ dvijaiḥ /
jaghāna bhūmau niḥśeṣaṃ sākṣātkāla ivāntakaḥ //
2.46.d:
भूयो ऽपि राजन् संबुद्धं क्षत्रमुत्पादितं द्विजैः ।
जघान भूमौ निःशेषं साक्षात्काल इवान्तकः ॥
2.46.m: Again, O king, he slew without remainder on the earth the kṣatriyas / who had grown up, begotten by Brahmins, like Kāla, the Ender himself.

2.46.s:
kālena tāvatā bhūyaḥ samutpannaṃ nṛpāttvayam /
nighnaṃścacāra pṛthivīṃ varṣadvayamanāratam //
2.46.d:
कालेन तावता भूयः समुत्पन्नं नृपात्त्वयम् ।
निघ्नंश्चचार पृथिवीं वर्षद्वयमनारतम् ॥
2.46.m: Within that much time, kṣatriyas were born again; / slaying them, he traversed the earth continuously for two years.

2.46.s:
alaṃ rāmeṇa rājendra smaratā nidhanaṃ pituḥ /
triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī tena niḥkṣatriyā kṛtā //
2.46.d:
अलं रामेण राजेन्द्र स्मरता निधनं पितुः ।
त्रिः सप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी तेन निःक्षत्रिया कृता ॥
2.46.m: Enough! By Rāma, O king of kings, remembering his father's death, / the earth was made devoid of kṣatriyas thrice seven times.

2.46.s:
triḥsaptakṛtvastanmātā yaduraḥ svamatāḍayat /
tāvadrāmeṇa tasmāttu kṣatramutsāditaṃ bhuvi //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde bhārgavacarite ṣaṭcatvāriṃśatta mo 'dhyāyaḥ // 46//
2.46.d:
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वस्तन्माता यदुरः स्वमताडयत् ।
तावद्रामेण तस्मात्तु क्षत्रमुत्सादितं भुवि ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे भार्गवचरिते षट्चत्वारिंशत्त मो ऽध्यायः ॥ 46॥
2.46.m:
Because his mother struck her own chest thrice seven times, / for that reason Rāma exterminated the kṣatriyas on earth that many times.

Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, in the story of the Bhārgava, in the third section, the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part proclaimed by Vāyu, in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa of Brahmāṇḍa. // 46

2.47.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tato mūrddhābhiṣiktānāṃ rājñāmamitatejasām /
ṣaṭsahasradvayaṃ rāmo jīvagrāhaṃ gṛhītavān //
2.47.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
ततो मूर्द्धाभिषिक्तानां राज्ञाममिततेजसाम् ।
षट्सहस्रद्वयं रामो जीवग्राहं गृहीतवान् ॥
2.47.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Then Rāma captured alive twelve thousand / consecrated kings of boundless splendour.

2.47.s:
tato rājasahasrāṇi gṛhītvā munibhiḥ saha /
sa jagāma mahātejāḥ kurukṣetraṃ tapomayam //
2.47.d:
ततो राजसहस्राणि गृहीत्वा मुनिभिः सह ।
स जगाम महातेजाः कुरुक्षेत्रं तपोमयम् ॥
2.47.m: Then, taking thousands of kings along with the sages, / that one of great splendour went to Kurukṣetra, which consists of austerity.

2.47.s:
sarasāṃ pañcakaṃ tatra khānayitvā bhṛgudvahaḥ /
sukhāvagāhatīrthāni tāni cakre samantataḥ //
2.47.d:
सरसां पञ्चकं तत्र खानयित्वा भृगुद्वहः ।
सुखावगाहतीर्थानि तानि चक्रे समन्ततः ॥
2.47.m: Having had five lakes dug there, the best of the Bhṛgus / made them into sacred bathing sites of easy descent on every side.

2.47.s:
jaghāna tatra vai rājñaḥ śarīraprabhavāmṛjā /
sarāṃsi tāni vai pañca pūrayāmāsa bhārgavaḥ //
2.47.d:
जघान तत्र वै राज्ञः शरीरप्रभवामृजा ।
सरांसि तानि वै पञ्च पूरयामास भार्गवः ॥
2.47.m: There he slew the kings; with the liquid produced from their bodies / the Bhārgava filled those five lakes.

2.47.s:
snātvā teṣu yathānyāyaṃ jāmadagnayaḥ pratāpavān /
pitṝnsaṃtarpayāmāsa yathāśāstramatandritaḥ //
2.47.d:
स्नात्वा तेषु यथान्यायं जामदग्नयः प्रतापवान् ।
पितॄन्संतर्पयामास यथाशास्त्रमतन्द्रितः ॥
2.47.m: Having bathed in them in the proper manner, the glorious son of Jamadagni, / unflagging, satisfied his ancestors in accordance with the scriptures.

2.47.s:
pituḥ pretasya rājendra śrāddhādikamaśeṣataḥ /
brāhmaṇaiḥ saha mātuśca tatra cakre yathoditam //
2.47.d:
पितुः प्रेतस्य राजेन्द्र श्राद्धादिकमशेषतः ।
ब्राह्मणैः सह मातुश्च तत्र चक्रे यथोदितम् ॥
2.47.m: O best of kings, along with Brahmins he performed there entirely / the ancestral rites and other ceremonies as prescribed for his deceased father and mother.

2.47.s:
evaṃ tīrṇapratīkaḥ sa kurukṣetre tapomaye /
uvāsātandritaḥ samyak pitṛpūjāparāyaṇaḥ //
2.47.d:
एवं तीर्णप्रतीकः स कुरुक्षेत्रे तपोमये ।
उवासातन्द्रितः सम्यक् पितृपूजापरायणः ॥
2.47.m: Having thus fulfilled his pledge, in Kurukṣetra, which consists of austerity, / he dwelt, untiring and completely devoted to the worship of his ancestors.

2.47.s:
tataḥ prabhṛtyabhūdrājaṃstīrthānāmuttamottamam /
vihitaṃ jāmadagnyena kurukṣetre tapovane //
2.47.d:
ततः प्रभृत्यभूद्राजंस्तीर्थानामुत्तमोत्तमम् ।
विहितं जामदग्न्येन कुरुक्षेत्रे तपोवने ॥
2.47.m: From that time forth, O king, there came to be the highest of all sacred places, / established by the son of Jamadagni in the penance grove of Kurukṣetra,

2.47.s:
sasyamaṃ tapañcakamiti sthānaṃ trailokyaviśrutam /
yatra yakre bhṛguśreṣṭhaḥ pitṝṇāṃ tṛptimakṣayām //
2.47.d:
सस्यमं तपञ्चकमिति स्थानं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ।
यत्र यक्रे भृगुश्रेष्ठः पितॄणां तृप्तिमक्षयाम् ॥
2.47.m: the place known across the three worlds as Samantapañcaka, / where the best of the Bhṛgus brought imperishable satisfaction to his ancestors.

2.47.s:
snānadānatapohomadvijabhojanatarpaṇaiḥ /
bhṛśamāpyāyitāstena yatra te pitaro 'khilāḥ //
2.47.d:
स्नानदानतपोहोमद्विजभोजनतर्पणैः ।
भृशमाप्यायितास्तेन यत्र ते पितरो ऽखिलाः ॥
2.47.m: Where all those ancestors were abundantly gratified by him / through ablutions, gifts, austerities, fire offerings, feeding Brahmins, and libations,

2.47.s:
avāpurakṣayāṃ tṛptiṃ pitṛlokaṃ ca śāśvatam /
samantapañcakaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ loke pariśrutam //
2.47.d:
अवापुरक्षयां तृप्तिं पितृलोकं च शाश्वतम् ।
समन्तपञ्चकं नाम तीर्थं लोके परिश्रुतम् ॥
2.47.m: they attained imperishable satisfaction and the eternal realm of ancestors; / the sacred site celebrated in the world by the name Samantapañcaka

2.47.s:
sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ mahāpuṇyopabṛṃhitam /
martyānāṃ yatra yātānāmenāṃsi nikhilāni tu //
2.47.d:
सर्वपापक्षयकरं महापुण्योपबृंहितम् ।
मर्त्यानां यत्र यातानामेनांसि निखिलानि तु ॥
2.47.m: destroys all sins and is magnified by great merit; / when mortals go there, all their sins

2.47.s:
dūrādevāpayāsyanti pravāte śuṣkaparṇavat /
tatkṣetracaryāgamanaṃ martyānāmasatāmiha //
2.47.d:
दूरादेवापयास्यन्ति प्रवाते शुष्कपर्णवत् ।
तत्क्षेत्रचर्यागमनं मर्त्यानामसतामिह ॥
2.47.m: will flee far away, like dry leaves in a gust of wind. / For wicked mortals in this world, reaching and walking in that sacred precinct

2.47.s:
na labhyate mahārāja jātu janmaśatairapi /
samantapañcakaṃ tīrthaṃ kurukṣetre 'tipāvanam //
2.47.d:
न लभ्यते महाराज जातु जन्मशतैरपि ।
समन्तपञ्चकं तीर्थं कुरुक्षेत्रे ऽतिपावनम् ॥
2.47.m: cannot be obtained, O great king, even in hundreds of births— / the sacred site Samantapañcaka, supremely purifying in Kurukṣetra.

2.47.s:
yatra snātaḥ sarvatīrthaiḥ snāto bhavati mānavaḥ /
kṛtakṛtyastato rāmaḥ samyak pūrṇamanorathaḥ //
2.47.d:
यत्र स्नातः सर्वतीर्थैः स्नातो भवति मानवः ।
कृतकृत्यस्ततो रामः सम्यक् पूर्णमनोरथः ॥
2.47.m: bathing in which a person is bathed in all sacred waters. / Thereupon, having accomplished his task and fully fulfilled his desires, Rāma,

2.47.s:
uvāsa tatra niyataḥ kañcitkālaṃ mahāmatiḥ /
tataḥ saṃvatsarasyānte brāhmaṇaiḥ sahito vaśī //
2.47.d:
उवास तत्र नियतः कञ्चित्कालं महामतिः ।
ततः संवत्सरस्यान्ते ब्राह्मणैः सहितो वशी ॥
2.47.m: being self-controlled and highly wise, dwelt there restrained for some time. / Then, at the end of a year, accompanied by Brāhmaṇas,

2.47.s:
pitṛpiṇḍapradānāya jāmadagnyo 'gamadgayām /
tato gatvā tataḥ śrāddhe yathāśāstramarindamaḥ //
2.47.d:
पितृपिण्डप्रदानाय जामदग्न्यो ऽगमद्गयाम् ।
ततो गत्वा ततः श्राद्धे यथाशास्त्रमरिन्दमः ॥
2.47.m: Jāmadagnya, subduer of enemies, went to Gayā to offer rice balls to the ancestors. / Arriving there, at the ancestor-rite in accordance with the scriptures,

2.47.s:
brāhmaṇāṃstarpayāmāsa pitṝnuddiśya satkṛtān /
śaivaṃ tatra paraṃ sthānaṃ candrapādamiti smṛtam //
2.47.d:
ब्राह्मणांस्तर्पयामास पितॄनुद्दिश्य सत्कृतान् ।
शैवं तत्र परं स्थानं चन्द्रपादमिति स्मृतम् ॥
2.47.m: he gratified the honored Brāhmaṇas on behalf of the ancestors. / There is the supreme Śaiva site known as Candrapāda;

2.47.s:
pitṛtṛptikaraṃ kṣetraṃ tādṛgloke na vidyate /
yatrārcitāḥ svakulajairyathāśakti manāgapi //
2.47.d:
पितृतृप्तिकरं क्षेत्रं तादृग्लोके न विद्यते ।
यत्रार्चिताः स्वकुलजैर्यथाशक्ति मनागपि ॥
2.47.m: no sacred ground in the world is known like it for satisfying the ancestors, / where, if honored even a little according to ability by members of their family,

2.47.s:
pitaraḥ piṇḍadānādyaiḥ prāpsyanti gatimakṣayām /
pitṝnuddiśya tatrāsau tarppiteṣu dvijātiṣu //
2.47.d:
पितरः पिण्डदानाद्यैः प्राप्स्यन्ति गतिमक्षयाम् ।
पितॄनुद्दिश्य तत्रासौ तर्प्पितेषु द्विजातिषु ॥
2.47.m: the ancestors will attain an imperishable state through offerings of rice balls and the like. / When the twice-born were gratified there on behalf of the ancestors,

2.47.s:
dadau ca vidhivatpiṇḍaṃ pitṛbhaktisamanvitaḥ /
tatastatpitaraḥ sarve pitṛlokādupāgatāḥ //
2.47.d:
ददौ च विधिवत्पिण्डं पितृभक्तिसमन्वितः ।
ततस्तत्पितरः सर्वे पितृलोकादुपागताः ॥
2.47.m: he offered the rice ball according to the prescribed rite, filled with devotion to the ancestors. / Then all his ancestors arrived from the realm of the ancestors,

2.47.s:
jagṛhustatkṛtāṃ pūjāṃ jamadagnipurogamāḥ /
atha saṃprītamanasaḥ sametya bhṛgunandanam //
2.47.d:
जगृहुस्तत्कृतां पूजां जमदग्निपुरोगमाः ।
अथ संप्रीतमनसः समेत्य भृगुनन्दनम् ॥
2.47.m: headed by Jamadagni, and accepted the worship performed by him. / Then, their minds well pleased, approaching the descendant of Bhṛgu,

2.47.s:
ūcustatpitaraḥ sarve 'dṛśyā bhūtvāntarikṣagāḥ /
pitara ūcuḥ
mahatkarma kṛtaṃ vīra bhavatānyaiḥ suduṣkaram //
2.47.d:
ऊचुस्तत्पितरः सर्वे ऽदृश्या भूत्वान्तरिक्षगाः ।
पितर ऊचुः
महत्कर्म कृतं वीर भवतान्यैः सुदुष्करम् ॥
2.47.m: all his ancestors, remaining in the intermediate space invisible, spoke. / The ancestors said: / 'A great deed, very difficult for others to do, has been performed by you, hero!

2.47.s:
asmānapi yathānyāyaṃ samyak tarpitavānasi /
asmākamakṣayāṃ prītiṃ tathāpi tvaṃ na yacchasi //
2.47.d:
अस्मानपि यथान्यायं सम्यक् तर्पितवानसि ।
अस्माकमक्षयां प्रीतिं तथापि त्वं न यच्छसि ॥
2.47.m: You have also properly gratified us according to the rules; / nevertheless, you do not grant us imperishable satisfaction.

2.47.s:
kṣatrahatyāṃ hi kṛtvā tu kṛtakarmābhavadyataḥ /
kṣetrasyāsya prabhāveṇa bhaktyā ca tava darśanam //
2.47.d:
क्षत्रहत्यां हि कृत्वा तु कृतकर्माभवद्यतः ।
क्षेत्रस्यास्य प्रभावेण भक्त्या च तव दर्शनम् ॥
2.47.m: For because you performed the slaughter of the Kṣatriyas, your actions have brought consequence; / but through the power of this sacred place and through your devotion, we have obtained

2.47.s:
prāptāḥsma pūjitāḥ kiṃ tu nākṣayyaphalabhāginaḥ /
tsamāttvaṃ vīrahatyādipāpapraśamanāya hi //
2.47.d:
प्राप्ताःस्म पूजिताः किं तु नाक्षय्यफलभागिनः ।
त्समात्त्वं वीरहत्यादिपापप्रशमनाय हि ॥
2.47.m: sight [of you], and have been honored; yet we are not recipients of the imperishable fruit. / Therefore, for the pacification of the sin of slaying heroes and the rest,

2.47.s:
prāyaścittaṃ yathānyāyaṃ kuru dharmaṃ ca śāśvatam /
vadhācca vinivartasva kṣatriyāṇāmataḥ param //
2.47.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं यथान्यायं कुरु धर्मं च शाश्वतम् ।
वधाच्च विनिवर्तस्व क्षत्रियाणामतः परम् ॥
2.47.m: perform expiation according to the rules, and practice eternal dharma; / and desist from the slaughter of Kṣatriyas henceforth!

2.47.s:
piturnna te 'parādhyante na svatantraṃ yato jagat /
tannimittaṃ tu maraṇaṃ pituste vihitaṃ purā //
2.47.d:
पितुर्न्न ते ऽपराध्यन्ते न स्वतन्त्रं यतो जगत् ।
तन्निमित्तं तु मरणं पितुस्ते विहितं पुरा ॥
2.47.m: They did not commit an offense against your father, for the world is not independent; / the death of your father was already ordained formerly with them as the instrument.

2.47.s:
hantuṃ kaṃ kaḥ samarthaḥ syālloke rakṣitumeva vā /
nimittamātrameveha sarvaḥ sarvasya caitayoḥ //
2.47.d:
हन्तुं कं कः समर्थः स्याल्लोके रक्षितुमेव वा ।
निमित्तमात्रमेवेह सर्वः सर्वस्य चैतयोः ॥
2.47.m: Who in this world is able to slay whom, or indeed to protect anyone? / In these two matters, everyone is merely an instrument for everyone else.

2.47.s:
dhruvaṃ karmānurūpaṃ te ceṣṭante sarva eva hi /
kālānuvṛttaṃ balavānnṛloko nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.47.d:
ध्रुवं कर्मानुरूपं ते चेष्टन्ते सर्व एव हि ।
कालानुवृत्तं बलवान्नृलोको नात्र संशयः ॥
2.47.m: Truly, all beings act strictly in accordance with their karma; / the world of mortals is powerfully driven by time; there is no doubt in this.

2.47.s:
bādhituṃ bhuvi bhūtāni bhūtānāṃ na vidhiṃ vinā /
śakyate vatsa sarvo 'pi yataḥ śaktyā svakarmakṛt //
2.47.d:
बाधितुं भुवि भूतानि भूतानां न विधिं विना ।
शक्यते वत्स सर्वो ऽपि यतः शक्त्या स्वकर्मकृत् ॥
2.47.m: Beings cannot harm beings on earth without divine ordinance, / dear child, since each one acts according to their karma through their power.

2.47.s:
kṣatraṃ prati tato roṣaṃ vimucyāsmatpriyepsayā /
śamamā pnuhi bhadraṃ te sa hyasmākaṃ paraṃ balam //
2.47.d:
क्षत्रं प्रति ततो रोषं विमुच्यास्मत्प्रियेप्सया ।
शममा प्नुहि भद्रं ते स ह्यस्माकं परं बलम् ॥
2.47.m: Therefore, abandoning your anger toward the Kṣatriyas out of a desire for our welfare, / attain tranquility! May you have good fortune! That indeed is our highest strength.'

2.47.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
ityuktvāntardadhuḥ sarve pitaro bhṛgunandanam /
sa cāpi tadvacaḥ sarvaṃ pratijagrāha sādaram //
2.47.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधुः सर्वे पितरो भृगुनन्दनम् ।
स चापि तद्वचः सर्वं प्रतिजग्राह सादरम् ॥
2.47.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having spoken thus, all the ancestors vanished from the descendant of Bhṛgu; / and he too respectfully accepted all their words.

2.47.s:
akṛtavraṇasaṃyukto mudā paramayā yutaḥ /
prayayau ca tadā rāmastasmātsiddhavanāśramam //
2.47.d:
अकृतव्रणसंयुक्तो मुदा परमया युतः ।
प्रययौ च तदा रामस्तस्मात्सिद्धवनाश्रमम् ॥
2.47.m: Joined by Akṛtavraṇa, filled with supreme joy, / Rāma then set out from there to the hermitage in the Siddha Forest.

2.47.s:
tasminsthitvā bhṛguśreṣṭho brāhmaṇaiḥ sahito nṛpa /
tapase dhṛtasaṃkalpo babhūva sa mahāmanāḥ //
2.47.d:
तस्मिन्स्थित्वा भृगुश्रेष्ठो ब्राह्मणैः सहितो नृप ।
तपसे धृतसंकल्पो बभूव स महामनाः ॥
2.47.m: Staying there, O king, that noble-minded best of the Bhṛgus / resolved upon ascetic penance, accompanied by Brāhmaṇas.

2.47.s:
sarathaṃ sahasāhaṃ ca dhanuḥsaṃhananāni ca /
punarāgamasaṃketaṃ kṛtvā prāsthāpayattadā //
2.47.d:
सरथं सहसाहं च धनुःसंहननानि च ।
पुनरागमसंकेतं कृत्वा प्रास्थापयत्तदा ॥
2.47.m: He sent away his chariot, together with his arms and his implements for stringing bows, / making an appointment for their return at that time.

2.47.s:
tataḥ sa sarvatīrtheṣu cakre snānamatandritaḥ /
parītyapṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ pitṛdevādibūjakaḥ //
2.47.d:
ततः स सर्वतीर्थेषु चक्रे स्नानमतन्द्रितः ।
परीत्यपृथिवीं सर्वां पितृदेवादिबूजकः ॥
2.47.m: Then, unwearied, he bathed in all the sacred waters, / roaming the entire earth, worshipping ancestors, deities, and others.

2.47.s:
evaṃ krameṇa pṛthivīṃ trivāraṃ bhugunandanaḥ /
paricakrāma rājendra lokavṛttamanuvrataḥ //
2.47.d:
एवं क्रमेण पृथिवीं त्रिवारं भुगुनन्दनः ।
परिचक्राम राजेन्द्र लोकवृत्तमनुव्रतः ॥
2.47.m: In this manner, following the conduct of the world, the descendant of Bhṛgu / traversed the earth three times, O best of kings.

2.47.s:
tataḥ sa parvataśreṣṭhaṃ mahendraṃ punarapyatha /
jagāma tapase rājanbāhmaṇairabhisaṃvṛtaḥ //
2.47.d:
ततः स पर्वतश्रेष्ठं महेन्द्रं पुनरप्यथ ।
जगाम तपसे राजन्बाह्मणैरभिसंवृतः ॥
2.47.m: Then, O king, surrounded by Brāhmaṇas, he went again / to Mahendra, the best of mountains, for the sake of ascetic penance.

2.47.s:
sa tasmiṃścirarātrāya muni siddhaniṣevite /
nivāsamātmano rājankalpayāmāsa dharmavit //
2.47.d:
स तस्मिंश्चिररात्राय मुनि सिद्धनिषेविते ।
निवासमात्मनो राजन्कल्पयामास धर्मवित् ॥
2.47.m: On that mountain resorted to by Siddhas, O king, that knower of dharma, / the sage, prepared his abode for a long period.

2.47.s:
munayastaṃ tapasyantaṃ sarvakṣetranivāsinaḥ /
draṣṭukāmāḥ samājagmurniyatā brahmavādinaḥ //
2.47.d:
मुनयस्तं तपस्यन्तं सर्वक्षेत्रनिवासिनः ।
द्रष्टुकामाः समाजग्मुर्नियता ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥
2.47.m: Desiring to see him engaged in asceticism, the self-controlled sages, / expositors of the Veda dwelling in all sacred places, gathered together.

2.47.s:
dadṛśuste munigaṇāstapasyāsaktamānasam /
kṣātraṃ kakṣamaśeṣeṇa dagdhvā śāntamivānalam //
2.47.d:
ददृशुस्ते मुनिगणास्तपस्यासक्तमानसम् ।
क्षात्रं कक्षमशेषेण दग्ध्वा शान्तमिवानलम् ॥
2.47.m: Those hosts of sages saw him whose mind was intent on asceticism, / like a fire that has quieted down after burning all the fuel of the Kṣatriyas.

2.47.s:
atha tānāgatāndṛṣṭvā munīndivyāṃstapomayān /
arghyādisamudācāraiḥ pūjayāmāsa bhārgavaḥ //
2.47.d:
अथ तानागतान्दृष्ट्वा मुनीन्दिव्यांस्तपोमयान् ।
अर्घ्यादिसमुदाचारैः पूजयामास भार्गवः ॥
2.47.m: Then, seeing those divine sages embodied in ascetic power who had arrived, / the Bhārgava honored them with water offerings and traditional courtesies.

2.47.s:
kṛtakauśalasaṃpraśnapūrvakāḥ sumahodayāḥ /
teṣāṃ tasya ca saṃvṛttāḥ kathāḥ puṇyā manoharāḥ //
2.47.d:
कृतकौशलसंप्रश्नपूर्वकाः सुमहोदयाः ।
तेषां तस्य च संवृत्ताः कथाः पुण्या मनोहराः ॥
2.47.m: Beginning with inquiries of well-being, most auspicious, / sacred, and charming conversations took place between them and him.

2.47.s:
tatasteṣāmanumate munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām /
hayamedhaṃ mahāyajñamāhartumupacakrame //
2.47.d:
ततस्तेषामनुमते मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम् ।
हयमेधं महायज्ञमाहर्तुमुपचक्रमे ॥
2.47.m: Then, with the assent of those sages of purified self, / he undertook to perform the great sacrifice, the horse sacrifice.

2.47.s:
saṃbhṛtya sarvasaṃbhārānaurvādyaiḥ sahito nṛpa /
viśvāmitrabharadvājamārkaṇḍeyādibhistathā //
2.47.d:
संभृत्य सर्वसंभारानौर्वाद्यैः सहितो नृप ।
विश्वामित्रभरद्वाजमार्कण्डेयादिभिस्तथा ॥
2.47.m: Gathering all the sacrificial materials, accompanied by the descendants of Ūrva and others, O king, / as well as Viśvāmitra, Bharadvāja, Mārkaṇḍeya, and the rest,

2.47.s:
teṣā manumate kṛtvā kāśyapaṃ gurumātmanaḥ /
vājimedhaṃ tato rājannājahāra mahākratum //
2.47.d:
तेषा मनुमते कृत्वा काश्यपं गुरुमात्मनः ।
वाजिमेधं ततो राजन्नाजहार महाक्रतुम् ॥
2.47.m: and making Kāśyapa his officiating priest with their approval, / he then performed the great horse sacrifice, O king.

2.47.s:
tasyābhūtkāśyapo 'dhvaryurudgātā gautamo muniḥ /
viśvāmitro 'bhavaddhotā rāmasya viditātmanaḥ //
2.47.d:
तस्याभूत्काश्यपो ऽध्वर्युरुद्गाता गौतमो मुनिः ।
विश्वामित्रो ऽभवद्धोता रामस्य विदितात्मनः ॥
2.47.m: Kāśyapa became his adhvaryu, the sage Gautama the udgātā, / and Viśvāmitra was the hotā for Rāma of known self.

2.47.s:
brahmatvamakarottasya mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ /
bharadvājāgniveśyādyā veda vedāṅgapāragāḥ //
2.47.d:
ब्रह्मत्वमकरोत्तस्य मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ।
भरद्वाजाग्निवेश्याद्या वेद वेदाङ्गपारगाः ॥
2.47.m: The great sage Mārkaṇḍeya assumed the office of brahman priest; / Bharadvāja, Āgniveśya, and others, who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

2.47.s:
munayaścakruranyāni karmāṇyanye yathākramam /
puttraiḥ śiṣyaiḥ praśiṣyaiśca sahito bhagavānbhṛguḥ //
2.47.d:
मुनयश्चक्रुरन्यानि कर्माण्यन्ये यथाक्रमम् ।
पुत्त्रैः शिष्यैः प्रशिष्यैश्च सहितो भगवान्भृगुः ॥
2.47.m: and other sages performed the other rites in due order; / and the venerable Bhṛgu, along with his sons, disciples, and grand-disciples,

2.47.s:
sādasyamakarodrājannanyaiśca munibhiḥ saha /
sa taiḥ sahākhilaṃ karma samāpya bhṛgupuṅgavaḥ //
2.47.d:
सादस्यमकरोद्राजन्नन्यैश्च मुनिभिः सह ।
स तैः सहाखिलं कर्म समाप्य भृगुपुङ्गवः ॥
2.47.m: together with other sages, served as the assembly members, O king. / Having completed the entire rite with them, the eminent Bhṛgu

2.47.s:
brahmāṇaṃ pūjayāmāsa yathāvadguruṇā saha /
alaṅkṛtya yathānyāya kanyāṃ rūpavatīṃ mahīm //
2.47.d:
ब्रह्माणं पूजयामास यथावद्गुरुणा सह ।
अलङ्कृत्य यथान्याय कन्यां रूपवतीं महीम् ॥
2.47.m: duly honored the brahman priest along with the preceptor. / Adorning the beautiful earth according to proper custom, like a maiden,

2.47.s:
puragrāmaśatopetāṃ samudrāṃbaramālinīm /
āhūya bhṛguśārdūlaḥ saśailavanakānanām //
2.47.d:
पुरग्रामशतोपेतां समुद्रांबरमालिनीम् ।
आहूय भृगुशार्दूलः सशैलवनकाननाम् ॥
2.47.m: endowed with hundreds of cities and villages, garlanded with the ocean for its garment, / containing mountains, forests, and woods, the tiger among Bhṛgus summoned [Kāśyapa]

2.47.s:
kāśyapāya dadau sarvāmṛte taṃ śailamuttamam /
ātmanaḥ sannivāsārthaṃ taṃ rāmaḥ paryakalpayat //
2.47.d:
काश्यपाय ददौ सर्वामृते तं शैलमुत्तमम् ।
आत्मनः सन्निवासार्थं तं रामः पर्यकल्पयत् ॥
2.47.m: and gave it all to Kāśyapa, except for that excellent mountain; / that one Rāma reserved for his own habitation.

2.47.s:
tataḥ prabhṛtirājendra pūjayāmāsa śāstrataḥ /
hiraṇyaratnavastraśvagogajānnādibhistathā //
2.47.d:
ततः प्रभृतिराजेन्द्र पूजयामास शास्त्रतः ।
हिरण्यरत्नवस्त्रश्वगोगजान्नादिभिस्तथा ॥
2.47.m: From then on, O best of kings, he honored [them] according to the scriptures / with gold, jewels, garments, horses, cows, elephants, food, and the like.

2.47.s:
purā samāpya yajñānte tathā cāvabhṛthāplutaḥ /
cakre dravyaparityāgaṃ teṣāmanumate tadā //
2.47.d:
पुरा समाप्य यज्ञान्ते तथा चावभृथाप्लुतः ।
चक्रे द्रव्यपरित्यागं तेषामनुमते तदा ॥
2.47.m: Having concluded the sacrifice at the end and bathed in the final ablution, / he then distributed his wealth with their permission.

2.47.s:
dattvā ca sarvabhūtānāmabhayaṃ bhṛgunandanaḥ /
tatrāpi parvatavare tapaścartuṃ samārabhat //
2.47.d:
दत्त्वा च सर्वभूतानामभयं भृगुनन्दनः ।
तत्रापि पर्वतवरे तपश्चर्तुं समारभत् ॥
2.47.m: And granting freedom from fear to all beings, the descendant of Bhṛgu / began to practice ascetic penance there on that excellent mountain.

2.47.s:
tatastaṃ samanujñāya sadasyā ṛtvijastathā /
yayuryathāgataṃ sarve munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ //
2.47.d:
ततस्तं समनुज्ञाय सदस्या ऋत्विजस्तथा ।
ययुर्यथागतं सर्वे मुनयः शंसितव्रताः ॥
2.47.m: Then, taking leave of him, the assembly members, the officiating priests, / and all the sages of praised vows departed just as they had come.

2.47.s:
gateṣu teṣu bhagavānakṛtavraṇasaṃyutaḥ /
tapo mahatsamāsthāya tatraiva nyavasatsukhī //
2.47.d:
गतेषु तेषु भगवानकृतव्रणसंयुतः ।
तपो महत्समास्थाय तत्रैव न्यवसत्सुखी ॥
2.47.m: When they had departed, the venerable one, accompanied by Akṛtavraṇa, / undertook great asceticism and dwelt right there happily.

2.47.s:
kāśyapī tu tato bhūmirjananāthā hyanekaśaḥ /
sarvaduḥkhapraśāntyarthaṃ mārīcānumatena tu //
2.47.d:
काश्यपी तु ततो भूमिर्जननाथा ह्यनेकशः ।
सर्वदुःखप्रशान्त्यर्थं मारीचानुमतेन तु ॥
2.47.m: Then the earth, belonging to Kāśyapa, had many rulers; / and for the pacification of all sorrows, with the assent of [Kāśyapa] son of Marīci,

2.47.s:
tatra dīpapratiṣṭhākhyavrataṃ viṣṇumukhoditam /
cacāra dharaṇī samyak dukhairḥmuktābhavacca sā //
2.47.d:
तत्र दीपप्रतिष्ठाख्यव्रतं विष्णुमुखोदितम् ।
चचार धरणी सम्यक् दुखैर्ःमुक्ताभवच्च सा ॥
2.47.m: the earth properly performed the vow called the dedication of lamps, spoken from the mouth of Viṣṇu, / and she was liberated from sorrows.

2.47.s:
ityeṣa jāmadagnyasya prādurbhāva udāhṛtaḥ /
yasmiñśrute naraḥ sarvapātakairvipramucyate //
2.47.d:
इत्येष जामदग्न्यस्य प्रादुर्भाव उदाहृतः ।
यस्मिञ्श्रुते नरः सर्वपातकैर्विप्रमुच्यते ॥
2.47.m: Thus this manifestation of Jāmadagnya has been recounted, / upon hearing which a person is completely freed from all sins.

2.47.s:
prabhāvaḥ kārttavīryasya loke prathitatejasaḥ /
prasaṃgātkathitaḥ samyaṅnātisaṃkṣepavistaraḥ //
2.47.d:
प्रभावः कार्त्तवीर्यस्य लोके प्रथिततेजसः ।
प्रसंगात्कथितः सम्यङ्नातिसंक्षेपविस्तरः ॥
2.47.m: The majesty of Kārttavīrya, whose splendor was famed throughout the world, / has been fully recounted in this context, neither too concise nor too detailed.

2.47.s:
evaṃprabhāvaḥ sa nṛpaḥ kārttavīryo 'bhavadbhuvi /
na tādṛśaḥ pumātkaścidbhāvī bhūtāthavā śrutaḥ //
2.47.d:
एवंप्रभावः स नृपः कार्त्तवीर्यो ऽभवद्भुवि ।
न तादृशः पुमात्कश्चिद्भावी भूताथवा श्रुतः ॥
2.47.m: Such was the majesty of King Kārttavīrya on earth; / no such man will ever be, has ever been, or was ever heard of.

2.47.s:
dattātreyādvaraṃ vavre mṛtimuttamapūruṣāt /
yatpurā so 'gamanmuktiṃ raṇe rāmeṇa ghātitaḥ //
2.47.d:
दत्तात्रेयाद्वरं वव्रे मृतिमुत्तमपूरुषात् ।
यत्पुरा सो ऽगमन्मुक्तिं रणे रामेण घातितः ॥
2.47.m: From Dattātreya he chose the boon of death at the hands of the foremost person, / through which he formerly attained liberation when slain in battle by Rāma.

2.47.s:
tasyāsītpañcamaḥ putraḥ pakhyāto yo jayadhvajaḥ /
putrastasya mahābāhustālajaṅgho 'bhavannṛpa //
2.47.d:
तस्यासीत्पञ्चमः पुत्रः पख्यातो यो जयध्वजः ।
पुत्रस्तस्य महाबाहुस्तालजङ्घो ऽभवन्नृप ॥
2.47.m: He had a fifth son, celebrated as Jayadhvaja; / his son was the mighty-armed Tālajaṅgha, O king.

2.47.s:
abhūttasyāpi putrāṇāṃ śatamuttamadhanvinām /
tālajaṅghābhidhā yeṣāṃ vītihotro 'grajo 'bhavat //
2.47.d:
अभूत्तस्यापि पुत्राणां शतमुत्तमधन्विनाम् ।
तालजङ्घाभिधा येषां वीतिहोत्रो ऽग्रजो ऽभवत् ॥
2.47.m: He too had a hundred sons, excellent archers, / called the Tālajaṅghas, of whom Vītihotra was the eldest.

2.47.s:
putraiḥ savītihotrādyairhaihayādyaiśca rājabhiḥ /
kālaṃ mahāntamavasaddhimādrivānagahvare //
2.47.d:
पुत्रैः सवीतिहोत्राद्यैर्हैहयाद्यैश्च राजभिः ।
कालं महान्तमवसद्धिमाद्रिवानगह्वरे ॥
2.47.m: With his sons, headed by Vītihotra, and the Haihaya kings, / he lived for a long time in a cave in the forest of the Himavat mountains.

2.47.s:
yaḥ pūrvaṃ rāma bāṇena dravanpṛṣṭhe 'bhitāḍitaḥ /
tālajaṅgho 'patadbhūmau mūrchito gāḍhavedanaḥ //
2.47.d:
यः पूर्वं राम बाणेन द्रवन्पृष्ठे ऽभिताडितः ।
तालजङ्घो ऽपतद्भूमौ मूर्छितो गाढवेदनः ॥
2.47.m: Formerly struck in the back by Rāma's arrow as he fled, / Tālajaṅgha fell to the earth unconscious, in severe agony.

2.47.s:
dadarśa vītihotrastaṃ dravandaivavaśādiva /
rathamāropya vegena palāyanaparo 'bhavat //
2.47.d:
ददर्श वीतिहोत्रस्तं द्रवन्दैववशादिव ।
रथमारोप्य वेगेन पलायनपरो ऽभवत् ॥
2.47.m: Vītihotra, as if driven by fate, saw him as he fled; / placing him on his chariot, he quickly set about fleeing.

2.47.s:
te tatra nyavasansarve himādrau bhayapīḍitāḥ /
kṛcchraṃ mahāntamāsādya śākamūlaphalāśanaḥ //
2.47.d:
ते तत्र न्यवसन्सर्वे हिमाद्रौ भयपीडिताः ।
कृच्छ्रं महान्तमासाद्य शाकमूलफलाशनः ॥
2.47.m: Stricken with fear, they all dwelt there on the Himavat, / having met with great hardship, subsisting on herbs, roots, and fruits.

2.47.s:
tataḥ śāntiṃ gate rāme tapasyāsaktamānase /
jālajaṅghaḥ svakaṃ rājyaṃ saputraḥ pratyapadyata //
2.47.d:
ततः शान्तिं गते रामे तपस्यासक्तमानसे ।
जालजङ्घः स्वकं राज्यं सपुत्रः प्रत्यपद्यत ॥
2.47.m: Then, when Rāma had found peace and his mind was fixed on ascetic practice, / Tālajaṅgha, together with his sons, regained his own kingdom.

2.47.s:
sanniveśya purīṃ bhūyaḥ pūrvavannṛpasattamaḥ /
vasaṃstadā nijaṃ rājyamāpālayadarindamaḥ //
2.47.d:
सन्निवेश्य पुरीं भूयः पूर्ववन्नृपसत्तमः ।
वसंस्तदा निजं राज्यमापालयदरिन्दमः ॥
2.47.m: Having re-established the city as before, that best of kings, / living there, that subduer of enemies governed his realm.

2.47.s:
suputraḥ sānugabalaḥ pūrvavairamanusmaran /
abhyāyayau mahārāja tālajaṅghaḥ puraṃ tava //
2.47.d:
सुपुत्रः सानुगबलः पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् ।
अभ्याययौ महाराज तालजङ्घः पुरं तव ॥
2.47.m: Accompanied by his worthy sons and an army of followers, remembering the ancient enmity, / Tālajaṅgha marched against your city, O great king.

2.47.s:
caturaṅgabalopetaḥ kaṃpayanniva medinīm /
rurodābhyetya nagarīmayodhyāṃ sa mahīpatiḥ //
2.47.d:
चतुरङ्गबलोपेतः कंपयन्निव मेदिनीम् ।
रुरोदाभ्येत्य नगरीमयोध्यां स महीपतिः ॥
2.47.m: Endowed with a fourfold army, as though making the earth tremble, / that ruler of the earth approached and besieged the city of Ayodhyā.

2.47.s:
tato niṣkramya nagarātphalagutantro 'pi te pitā /
yuyudhe tairnṛpaiḥ sarvairvṛddho 'pi taruṇo yathā //
2.47.d:
ततो निष्क्रम्य नगरात्फलगुतन्त्रो ऽपि ते पिता ।
युयुधे तैर्नृपैः सर्वैर्वृद्धो ऽपि तरुणो यथा ॥
2.47.m: Then your father, going forth from the city though with feeble forces, / fought with all those kings, though old, as if he were a youth.

2.47.s:
nihatānekamātagaturaṅgarathasainikaḥ /
śatrubhirnirjito vṛddhaḥ palāyanaparo ' bhavat //
2.47.d:
निहतानेकमातगतुरङ्गरथसैनिकः ।
शत्रुभिर्निर्जितो वृद्धः पलायनपरो ' भवत् ॥
2.47.m: Having slain many of their elephant-, horse-, and chariot-soldiers, / the old man, defeated by the enemies, took to flight.

2.47.s:
tyaktvā sa nagaraṃ rājyaṃ sakośabalavāhanam /
antarvatnyā ca te mātrā sahito vanamāviśat //
2.47.d:
त्यक्त्वा स नगरं राज्यं सकोशबलवाहनम् ।
अन्तर्वत्न्या च ते मात्रा सहितो वनमाविशत् ॥
2.47.m: Abandoning city and kingdom, along with his treasury, army, and mounts, / he entered the forest together with your pregnant mother.

2.47.s:
tatra caurvāśramopānte nivasannacirādiva /
śokāmarṣasamāviṣṭo vṛddhabhāvena ca svayam //
2.47.d:
तत्र चौर्वाश्रमोपान्ते निवसन्नचिरादिव ।
शोकामर्षसमाविष्टो वृद्धभावेन च स्वयम् ॥
2.47.m: Dwelling there near Aurva's hermitage, not long after, / overcome with grief and anger, and also by his advanced age,

2.47.s:
vilokyamāno mātrā te bāṣpagadgadakaṇṭhayā /
anātha iva rājendra svargalokamito gataḥ //
2.47.d:
विलोक्यमानो मात्रा ते बाष्पगद्गदकण्ठया ।
अनाथ इव राजेन्द्र स्वर्गलोकमितो गतः ॥
2.47.m: as your mother watched with a throat choked with tears, / he departed from this world for heaven like a helpless man, O foremost of kings.

2.47.s:
tataste jananī rājanduḥkhaśokasamanvitā /
citāmāropayadbhartū rudatī sā kalevaram //
2.47.d:
ततस्ते जननी राजन्दुःखशोकसमन्विता ।
चितामारोपयद्भर्तू रुदती सा कलेवरम् ॥
2.47.m: Then your mother, O king, filled with misery and grief, / weeping, placed her husband's body upon the pyre.

2.47.s:
anaśanādiduḥkhena bhartturvyasanakarśitā /
cakārāgnipraveśāya sudṛḍhāṃ matimātmanaḥ //
2.47.d:
अनशनादिदुःखेन भर्त्तुर्व्यसनकर्शिता ।
चकाराग्निप्रवेशाय सुदृढां मतिमात्मनः ॥
2.47.m: Wasted by the torment of her husband's plight and the suffering of fasting and the like, / she made a firm resolution to enter the fire.

2.47.s:
aurvastadakhilaṃ śrutvā svayameva mahāmuniḥ /
nirgatya cāśramāttāṃ ca vārayannidamabravīt //
2.47.d:
और्वस्तदखिलं श्रुत्वा स्वयमेव महामुनिः ।
निर्गत्य चाश्रमात्तां च वारयन्निदमब्रवीत् ॥
2.47.m: Hearing all that, the great sage Aurva himself / came out of the hermitage and, preventing her, said this:

2.47.s:
na marttavyaṃ tvayā rājñi sāṃprataṃ jaṭhare tava /
putrastiṣṭhati sarveṣāṃ pravaraścavarttinām //
2.47.d:
न मर्त्तव्यं त्वया राज्ञि सांप्रतं जठरे तव ।
पुत्रस्तिष्ठति सर्वेषां प्रवरश्चवर्त्तिनाम् ॥
2.47.m: "You must not die, O queen! At present in your womb / dwells a son who will be the foremost of all universal emperors."

2.47.s:
iti tadvacanaṃ śrutvā mātā tava manasvinī /
virarāma mṛtestāṃ tu muniḥ svāśramamānayat /
tataḥ sā sarvaduḥkhāni niyamya tvanmukhāṃbujam //
2.47.d:
इति तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा माता तव मनस्विनी ।
विरराम मृतेस्तां तु मुनिः स्वाश्रममानयत् ।
ततः सा सर्वदुःखानि नियम्य त्वन्मुखांबुजम् ॥
2.47.m: Hearing his words, your high-minded mother / desisted from dying, and the sage led her to his hermitage. / Then she, checking all her sorrows, eager to behold your lotus face,

2.47.s:
didṛkṣurāśramopānte tasyaiva nyavasatsukham /
suṣāva ca tataḥ kāle sā tvāmaurvāśrame tadā //
2.47.d:
दिदृक्षुराश्रमोपान्ते तस्यैव न्यवसत्सुखम् ।
सुषाव च ततः काले सा त्वामौर्वाश्रमे तदा ॥
2.47.m: dwelt happily near his hermitage. / Then, in due course, she gave birth to you there in Aurva's hermitage.

2.47.s:
jātakarmādikaṃ sarvaṃ bhavataḥ so 'karonmuniḥ /
aurvāśrame vivṛddhaśca bhavāṃstenānukaṃpitaḥ //
2.47.d:
जातकर्मादिकं सर्वं भवतः सो ऽकरोन्मुनिः ।
और्वाश्रमे विवृद्धश्च भवांस्तेनानुकंपितः ॥
2.47.m: The sage performed all your rites, beginning with the birth ceremonies; / and you, favored by him, grew up in Aurva's hermitage.

2.47.s:
tvayaiva viditaṃ sarvamataḥ paramarindama /
evaṃ prabhāvo nṛpatiḥ kārttavīryo 'bhavadbhuvi //
2.47.d:
त्वयैव विदितं सर्वमतः परमरिन्दम ।
एवं प्रभावो नृपतिः कार्त्तवीर्यो ऽभवद्भुवि ॥
2.47.m: All beyond this is known to you yourself, O subduer of enemies. / Such was the majesty of King Kārttavīrya on earth,

2.47.s:
vratasyāsya prabhāveṇa sarvalokeṣu viśrutaḥ /
yadvaṃśajairjito yuddhe pitā te vanamādiśat //
2.47.d:
व्रतस्यास्य प्रभावेण सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतः ।
यद्वंशजैर्जितो युद्धे पिता ते वनमादिशत् ॥
2.47.m: renowned throughout all the worlds through the power of this observance, / whose descendants conquered your father in battle and drove him to the forest.

2.47.s:
tadvṛttāntamaśeṣeṇa mayā te samudīritam /
etacca sarvamākhyātaṃ vratānāmuttamaṃ tava //
2.47.d:
तद्वृत्तान्तमशेषेण मया ते समुदीरितम् ।
एतच्च सर्वमाख्यातं व्रतानामुत्तमं तव ॥
2.47.m: I have told you that story in its entirety; / and this best of observances has all been related to you,

2.47.s:
samantratantraṃ lokeṣu sarvalokaphalapradam /
na hyasya kartturnṛpateḥ puruṣārthacatuṣṭaye //
2.47.d:
समन्त्रतन्त्रं लोकेषु सर्वलोकफलप्रदम् ।
न ह्यस्य कर्त्तुर्नृपतेः पुरुषार्थचतुष्टये ॥
2.47.m: with its mantras and rites, known in the worlds, yielding fruit to all people. / Indeed, for the king who performs it, among the four goals of human life,

2.47.s:
bhavatyabhīpsitaṃ kiñciddarllabhaṃ bhuvanatraye /
saṃkṣepeṇa mayākhyātaṃ vrataṃ haihayabhūbhujaḥ /
jāmadagnyasya ca mune kimanyatkathayāmi te //
2.47.d:
भवत्यभीप्सितं किञ्चिद्दर्ल्लभं भुवनत्रये ।
संक्षेपेण मयाख्यातं व्रतं हैहयभूभुजः ।
जामदग्न्यस्य च मुने किमन्यत्कथयामि ते ॥
2.47.m: no desired thing is difficult to attain in the three worlds. / I have told in brief the observance of the Haihaya king / and of the sage Jāmadagnya. What else shall I relate to you?

2.47.s:
jaiminiruvāca
tataḥ sa sagaro rājā kṛtāñjalipuṭo munim //
2.47.d:
जैमिनिरुवाच
ततः स सगरो राजा कृताञ्जलिपुटो मुनिम् ॥
2.47.m: Jaimini said: / Then that king Sagara, with hands joined in reverence, to the sage

2.47.s:
uvāca bhagavannetatkartumicchāmyahaṃ vratam /
samyaktamupadeśena tatrānujñāṃ prayaccha me //
2.47.d:
उवाच भगवन्नेतत्कर्तुमिच्छाम्यहं व्रतम् ।
सम्यक्तमुपदेशेन तत्रानुज्ञां प्रयच्छ मे ॥
2.47.m: said: "O venerable one, I wish to perform this observance / properly according to instruction; give me permission for that.

2.47.s:
karmaṇānena viprarṣe kṛtārtho 'smi na saṃśayaḥ /
ityuktastena rājñātu tathetyuktvā mahāmuniḥ //
2.47.d:
कर्मणानेन विप्रर्षे कृतार्थो ऽस्मि न संशयः ।
इत्युक्तस्तेन राज्ञातु तथेत्युक्त्वा महामुनिः ॥
2.47.m: By this action, O brāhmaṇa sage, I shall have achieved my goal, without a doubt." / Thus addressed by that king, the great sage said, "So be it,"

2.47.s:
dīkṣayāmāsa rājānaṃ śastroktenaiva vartmanā /
sa dīkṣito vasiṣṭhena sagaro rājasattamaḥ //
2.47.d:
दीक्षयामास राजानं शस्त्रोक्तेनैव वर्त्मना ।
स दीक्षितो वसिष्ठेन सगरो राजसत्तमः ॥
2.47.m: and initiated the king according to the method prescribed in the scriptures. / Initiated by Vasiṣṭha, Sagara, the best of kings,

2.47.s:
dravyāṇyānīya vidhivatpracacāra śubhavratam /
pūjayitvā jagannāthaṃ vidhinā tena pārthivaḥ //
2.47.d:
द्रव्याण्यानीय विधिवत्प्रचचार शुभव्रतम् ।
पूजयित्वा जगन्नाथं विधिना तेन पार्थिवः ॥
2.47.m: having brought the materials in accordance with the rules, undertook the auspicious observance. / Having worshipped the Lord of the Universe with that rite, the monarch,

2.47.s:
samāpya ca yathāyogyamanujñāya guruṃ tataḥ /
pratijñāmakarodrājā vratametadanuttamam //
2.47.d:
समाप्य च यथायोग्यमनुज्ञाय गुरुं ततः ।
प्रतिज्ञामकरोद्राजा व्रतमेतदनुत्तमम् ॥
2.47.m: having concluded it appropriately and obtained leave from his guru, / the king took a vow regarding this incomparable observance:

2.47.s:
ājīvāntaṃ dhariṣyāmi yatneneti mahāmatiḥ /
athānujñāpya rājānaṃ vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ //
2.47.d:
आजीवान्तं धरिष्यामि यत्नेनेति महामतिः ।
अथानुज्ञाप्य राजानं वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः ॥
2.47.m: "I shall maintain it diligently until the end of my life," resolved the noble-minded one. / Then, having granted leave to the king, the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha,

2.47.s:
sannivartyānugacchantaṃ prajagāma nijāśramam //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde sagaropākhyāne vasiṣṭhagamanaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.47.d:
सन्निवर्त्यानुगच्छन्तं प्रजगाम निजाश्रमम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे सगरोपाख्याने वसिष्ठगमनं नाम सप्तचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.47.m:
turning back [the king] who followed after him, departed for his own hermitage.

Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter, called 'The Departure of Vasiṣṭha', in the Story of Sagara in the third [section], the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part proclaimed by Vāyu in the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

2.48.s:
jaiminiruvāca
gate tasminmunivare sagaro rājasattamaḥ /
ayodhyāyāmadhivasnpālayāmāsa medinīm //
2.48.d:
जैमिनिरुवाच
गते तस्मिन्मुनिवरे सगरो राजसत्तमः ।
अयोध्यायामधिवस्न्पालयामास मेदिनीम् ॥
2.48.m: Jaimini said: / When that foremost of sages had departed, Sagara, the best of kings, / residing in Ayodhyā, protected the earth.

2.48.s:
sarvasaṃpadgaṇopetaḥ sarvadharmārthatattvavit /
vayasaiva sa bālo 'bhūtkarmaṇā vṛddhasaṃmataḥ //
2.48.d:
सर्वसंपद्गणोपेतः सर्वधर्मार्थतत्त्ववित् ।
वयसैव स बालो ऽभूत्कर्मणा वृद्धसंमतः ॥
2.48.m: Endowed with a multitude of all fortunes, knowing the truth of all dharma and statecraft, / in age alone he was a youth, but in deed regarded as mature.

2.48.s:
tathāpi na divā bhukteṃ śete vā niśi saṃsmaran /
sudīrghaṃ niḥśvasityuṣṇamudvignahṛdayo 'niśam //
2.48.d:
तथापि न दिवा भुक्तें शेते वा निशि संस्मरन् ।
सुदीर्घं निःश्वसित्युष्णमुद्विग्नहृदयो ऽनिशम् ॥
2.48.m: Even so, remembering, he did not eat by day nor sleep at night; / he sighed deeply and hotly, his heart constantly distressed.

2.48.s:
śrutvā rājā svarājyaṃ nijagurumavajityāribhiḥ saṃgṛhītaṃ mātrā sārddhaṃ prayāntaṃ vanamatigahanaṃsvargataṃ taṃ ca tasmin /
śokāviṣṭaḥ saroṣaṃ sakalaripukulocchittaye satpratijñaścake sadyaḥ pratijñāṃ paribhavamanalaṃ soḍhumikṣvākuvaṃśyaḥ //
2.48.d:
श्रुत्वा राजा स्वराज्यं निजगुरुमवजित्यारिभिः संगृहीतं मात्रा सार्द्धं प्रयान्तं वनमतिगहनंस्वर्गतं तं च तस्मिन् ।
शोकाविष्टः सरोषं सकलरिपुकुलोच्छित्तये सत्प्रतिज्ञश्चके सद्यः प्रतिज्ञां परिभवमनलं सोढुमिक्ष्वाकुवंश्यः ॥
2.48.m: Having heard that his own kingdom had been seized by enemies who had defeated his father, that [his father] had gone to the dense forest with his mother and died there, / the descendant of Ikṣvāku, overwhelmed with grief, full of anger, resolute in his good vow, unable to bear the humiliation, made a vow at once for the destruction of the entire host of his enemies.

2.48.s:
sa kadācinmahīpālaḥ kṛtakautukamaṅgalaḥ /
ripuṃ jetuṃ manaścakre diśaśca sakalāḥ kramāt //
2.48.d:
स कदाचिन्महीपालः कृतकौतुकमङ्गलः ।
रिपुं जेतुं मनश्चक्रे दिशश्च सकलाः क्रमात् ॥
2.48.m: Once, having performed auspicious and festive rites, that protector of the earth / resolved to conquer the enemy and all the quarters in succession.

2.48.s:
anekarathasāhasrairgajāśvarathasainikaiḥ /
sarvataḥ saṃvṛto rājā niścakrāma purottamāt //
2.48.d:
अनेकरथसाहस्रैर्गजाश्वरथसैनिकैः ।
सर्वतः संवृतो राजा निश्चक्राम पुरोत्तमात् ॥
2.48.m: Surrounded on all sides by thousands of chariots and by troops of elephants, horses, and chariots, / the king marched forth from the foremost of cities.

2.48.s:
śatrūnhantuṃ pratasthe nijabalanivahenotpatadbhisturaṅgairnāsattvormijālākulajalanidhinibhenātha ṣāḍaṅgikena /
mattairmātaṅgayūthaiḥ sakulagirikulenaiva bhūmaṇḍalena śvetacchatradhvajaughairapi śaśisukarābhātakhenaiva sārddham //
2.48.d:
शत्रून्हन्तुं प्रतस्थे निजबलनिवहेनोत्पतद्भिस्तुरङ्गैर्नासत्त्वोर्मिजालाकुलजलनिधिनिभेनाथ षाडङ्गिकेन ।
मत्तैर्मातङ्गयूथैः सकुलगिरिकुलेनैव भूमण्डलेन श्वेतच्छत्रध्वजौघैरपि शशिसुकराभातखेनैव सार्द्धम् ॥
2.48.m: He set out to slay his enemies with his own host of troops—with leaping horses, with his sixfold army resembling the ocean agitated by waves of myriad sea-monsters, / with herds of rutting elephants resembling the earth accompanied by mountain ranges, and with hosts of white parasols and banners resembling the sky illuminated by the lovely rays of the moon.

2.48.s:
tasyāgresarasainyayūthacaraṇaprakṣuṇṇaśailoccayakṣodāpūritanimnabhāgamavanīpālasya saṃyāsyataḥ /
pratyekaṃ caturaṅgasainyanikaraprakṣodasaṃbhūtabhūreṇuprāvṛtirutsthalī samabhavadbhūmistu tatrāniśam //
2.48.d:
तस्याग्रेसरसैन्ययूथचरणप्रक्षुण्णशैलोच्चयक्षोदापूरितनिम्नभागमवनीपालस्य संयास्यतः ।
प्रत्येकं चतुरङ्गसैन्यनिकरप्रक्षोदसंभूतभूरेणुप्रावृतिरुत्स्थली समभवद्भूमिस्तु तत्रानिशम् ॥
2.48.m: As that ruler of the earth marched along, the depressions in the terrain were filled with the crushed debris of mountain heaps trampled by the feet of his vanguard divisions, / and, veiled by the earth's dust produced from the pulverizing [tread] of each of the four arms of his army, the earth there became an uneven ground continuously.

2.48.s:
nighnandṛptānanekāndvipaturagarathavyūhasaṃbhinnavīrānsadyaḥ śobhāṃ dadhāno 'suranikaracamūrnighnataścandramauliḥ /
dūrādevābhiśaṃsannarinagaranirodheṣu karmābhiṣaṅge teṣāṃ śīghrāpayānakṣaṇamabhidiśati prāṇidhairyaṃ vidhatte //
2.48.d:
निघ्नन्दृप्ताननेकान्द्विपतुरगरथव्यूहसंभिन्नवीरान्सद्यः शोभां दधानो ऽसुरनिकरचमूर्निघ्नतश्चन्द्रमौलिः ।
दूरादेवाभिशंसन्नरिनगरनिरोधेषु कर्माभिषङ्गे तेषां शीघ्रापयानक्षणमभिदिशति प्राणिधैर्यं विधत्ते ॥
2.48.m: Slaying many haughty warriors scattered among the arrays of elephants, horses, and chariots, instantly bearing the splendour of the moon-crested god [Śiva] as he slays the armies of the Asura hosts, / proclaiming it even from afar, in the press of actions while laying siege to enemy cities, he granted courage to living beings, determining the moment for their swift retreat.

2.48.s: vijigīṣurdiśo rājā rājño yasyābhiyāsyati //
2.48.d: विजिगीषुर्दिशो राजा राज्ञो यस्याभियास्यति ॥
2.48.m: The king, desiring to conquer the quarters, marched against whichever king’s

2.48.s:
viṣayaṃ sa nṛpastasya sadyaḥ praṇatimeṣyati /
vijitya nṛpatīnsarvānkṛtvā ca svapadānugān //
2.48.d:
विषयं स नृपस्तस्य सद्यः प्रणतिमेष्यति ।
विजित्य नृपतीन्सर्वान्कृत्वा च स्वपदानुगान् ॥
2.48.m: realm—that king would immediately bow in submission. / Having conquered all kings and made them his followers,

2.48.s:
saṃketa gāminaḥ kāṃścitkṛtvā rājye nyavarttata /
evaṃ sa visarandikṣu dakṣiṇābhimukho nṛpaḥ //
2.48.d:
संकेत गामिनः कांश्चित्कृत्वा राज्ये न्यवर्त्तत ।
एवं स विसरन्दिक्षु दक्षिणाभिमुखो नृपः ॥
2.48.m: and having made some bound by oath, he returned to his kingdom. / Thus advancing through the quarters, the king, turning toward the south,

2.48.s:
smaranpūrvakṛtaṃ vairaṃ haihayānabhyavarttata /
tatastasya nṛpaiḥ sārddhaṃ samagrarathakuñjaraiḥ //
2.48.d:
स्मरन्पूर्वकृतं वैरं हैहयानभ्यवर्त्तत ।
ततस्तस्य नृपैः सार्द्धं समग्ररथकुञ्जरैः ॥
2.48.m: remembered the feud of old and marched against the Haihayas. / Then between him and the kings with all their chariots and elephants,

2.48.s:
babhūva haihayairvīraiḥ saṃgrāmo romaharṣaṇaḥ /
rājñāṃ yatra sahasrāṇi sa balāni mahāhave //
2.48.d:
बभूव हैहयैर्वीरैः संग्रामो रोमहर्षणः ।
राज्ञां यत्र सहस्राणि स बलानि महाहवे ॥
2.48.m: a hair-raising battle took place with the heroic Haihayas, / in which the mighty-armed lord of Kosala, enraged,

2.48.s:
nijaghāna mahābāhuḥ saṃkruddhaḥ kosaleśvaraḥ /
jitvā haihayabhūpālānbhaṅktvā dagdhvā ca tatpurīm //
2.48.d:
निजघान महाबाहुः संक्रुद्धः कोसलेश्वरः ।
जित्वा हैहयभूपालान्भङ्क्त्वा दग्ध्वा च तत्पुरीम् ॥
2.48.m: slew thousands of kings and their forces in the great fight. / Having conquered the Haihaya kings, and having broken and burnt their city,

2.48.s:
niḥśeṣaśūnyā makarodvairāntakaraṇo nṛpaḥ /
samagrabalasaṃmarddapramṛṣṭāśeṣabhūtalaḥ //
2.48.d:
निःशेषशून्या मकरोद्वैरान्तकरणो नृपः ।
समग्रबलसंमर्द्दप्रमृष्टाशेषभूतलः ॥
2.48.m: the king, putting an end to the feud, made it completely desolate. / Having swept away the entire surface of the earth by crushing their whole army,

2.48.s:
haihayānāmaśeṣaṃ tu cakre rājyaṃ rajaḥsamam /
rājyaṃ purīṃ cāpahāya bhraṣṭaiśvaryā hatatviṣaḥ //
2.48.d:
हैहयानामशेषं तु चक्रे राज्यं रजःसमम् ।
राज्यं पुरीं चापहाय भ्रष्टैश्वर्या हतत्विषः ॥
2.48.m: he reduced the entire realm of the Haihayas to dust. / Abandoning their kingdom and capital, their sovereignty ruined, their splendour destroyed,

2.48.s:
rājāno hatabhūyiṣṭhā vyadravanta samantataḥ /
abhidrutya nṛpāṃstāṃstu dravamāṇānmahīpatiḥ //
2.48.d:
राजानो हतभूयिष्ठा व्यद्रवन्त समन्ततः ।
अभिद्रुत्य नृपांस्तांस्तु द्रवमाणान्महीपतिः ॥
2.48.m: the kings, most of whom were killed, fled in all directions. / But chasing down those fleeing kings, the lord of the earth

2.48.s:
jaghāna sānugānmattaḥ prajāḥ kruddha ivāntakaḥ /
tatastānprati sakrodhaḥ sagaraḥ samare 'rihā //
2.48.d:
जघान सानुगान्मत्तः प्रजाः क्रुद्ध इवान्तकः ।
ततस्तान्प्रति सक्रोधः सगरः समरे ऽरिहा ॥
2.48.m: in a fury slew them along with their followers, as the enraged god of death [slays] living beings. / Then, enraged toward them in battle, Sagara, the slayer of foes,

2.48.s:
mumocāstraṃ mahāraudraṃ bhārgavaṃ rīpubhīṣaṇam /
tenotsṛṣṭātiraudratribhuvanabhayadaprasphuradbhārgavāstrajvālādandahyamānāvaśatanutatayaste nṛpāḥ sādya eva /
vāyvastrāvṛttadhūmodgamapaṭalatamomuṣṭadṛṣṭiprasārā bhremurbhūpṛṣṭaloṭhadbahulatamarajogūḍhamātrā muhūrttam //
2.48.d:
मुमोचास्त्रं महारौद्रं भार्गवं रीपुभीषणम् ।
तेनोत्सृष्टातिरौद्रत्रिभुवनभयदप्रस्फुरद्भार्गवास्त्रज्वालादन्दह्यमानावशतनुततयस्ते नृपाः साद्य एव ।
वाय्वस्त्रावृत्तधूमोद्गमपटलतमोमुष्टदृष्टिप्रसारा भ्रेमुर्भूपृष्टलोठद्बहुलतमरजोगूढमात्रा मुहूर्त्तम् ॥
2.48.m: discharged the Bhārgava weapon, exceedingly terrible and terrifying to enemies. / Scorched by the blazing flames of that exceedingly terrible Bhārgava weapon discharged by him, which terrified the three worlds, those kings instantly lost control of their bodies, / and with their range of sight snatched away by the darkness of the rising masses of smoke rolled back by the wind weapon, they wandered for a moment, simply concealed by the thick dust rolling upon the earth's surface.

2.48.s:
āganeyāstrapratāpapratihatagatayo 'dṛṣṭamārgāḥ samantā dbhūpālā naṣṭasaṃghāḥ paravaśatanavo vyākulībhūtacittāḥ /
bhītāḥ saṃtyuktavastrāyudhakavacavibhūṣādikā muktakeśā vispaṣṭonmattabhāvānbhṛśa taramanukurvantyagrataḥ śātravāṇām //
2.48.d:
आगनेयास्त्रप्रतापप्रतिहतगतयो ऽदृष्टमार्गाः समन्ता द्भूपाला नष्टसंघाः परवशतनवो व्याकुलीभूतचित्ताः ।
भीताः संत्युक्तवस्त्रायुधकवचविभूषादिका मुक्तकेशा विस्पष्टोन्मत्तभावान्भृश तरमनुकुर्वन्त्यग्रतः शात्रवाणाम् ॥
2.48.m: Their passage checked by the fierce heat of the fiery weapon, seeing no path on all sides, the kings, their ranks shattered, their bodies helpless, their minds thrown into confusion, / terrified, casting aside clothes, weapons, armour, and ornaments, with dishevelled hair, clearly imitated the behaviour of madmen before their enemies.

2.48.s:
vijitya haihayānsarvānsamare sagaro balī /
saṃkṣubdhasāgarākāraḥ kāṃbojānabhyavarttata //
2.48.d:
विजित्य हैहयान्सर्वान्समरे सगरो बली ।
संक्षुब्धसागराकारः कांबोजानभ्यवर्त्तत ॥
2.48.m: Having conquered all the Haihayas in battle, the mighty Sagara, / resembling an agitated ocean, marched against the Kāmbojas.

2.48.s:
nānāvāditraghoṣāhatapaṭaharavākarṇanadhvastadhairyāḥ sadyaḥ saṃtyaktarājyasvabalapurapurandhrīsamūhā vimūḍhāḥ /
kāṃbojāstālajaṅghāḥ śakayavanakirātādayaḥ sākamete bhremurbhūryastrabhītyā diśi diśi ripavo yasya pūrvāparādhāḥ //
2.48.d:
नानावादित्रघोषाहतपटहरवाकर्णनध्वस्तधैर्याः सद्यः संत्यक्तराज्यस्वबलपुरपुरन्ध्रीसमूहा विमूढाः ।
कांबोजास्तालजङ्घाः शकयवनकिरातादयः साकमेते भ्रेमुर्भूर्यस्त्रभीत्या दिशि दिशि रिपवो यस्य पूर्वापराधाः ॥
2.48.m: Their courage shattered by hearing the roar of drums struck by sounds of various musical instruments, instantly abandoning their kingdoms, their own armies, and the women of their cities, bewildered, / these Kāmbojas, Tālajaṅghas, Śakas, Yavanas, Kirātas, and others together, his enemies who had committed former offenses, wandered in every direction out of fear of his manifold weapons.

2.48.s:
bhītāstasya nareśvarasya ripavaḥ kecitpratā pānalajvālāmuṣṭadṛśo visṛjya vasatiṃ rājyaṃ ca putrādibhiḥ /
dviṭsainyaiḥ samabhidrutā vanabhuvaṃ saṃprāpya tatrāpi te 'staimityaṃ samupāgatā giriguhāsuptotthitena dviṣaḥ //
2.48.d:
भीतास्तस्य नरेश्वरस्य रिपवः केचित्प्रता पानलज्वालामुष्टदृशो विसृज्य वसतिं राज्यं च पुत्रादिभिः ।
द्विट्सैन्यैः समभिद्रुता वनभुवं संप्राप्य तत्रापि ते ऽस्तैमित्यं समुपागता गिरिगुहासुप्तोत्थितेन द्विषः ॥
2.48.m: Terrified of that lord of men, some enemies, their eyes blinded by the blazing flames of his fiery splendour, abandoned their dwelling and their kingdom along with their sons and others; / pursued by the enemy forces, they reached the forest regions, and even there those foes were rendered motionless by [the sound] of his roar, like that of [a lion] rising from sleep in a mountain cave.

2.48.s:
tālajaṅghānnihatyājau rājā sa balavāhanān /
krameṇa nāśayāmāsa tadrājyamarikarṣaṇaḥ //
2.48.d:
तालजङ्घान्निहत्याजौ राजा स बलवाहनान् ।
क्रमेण नाशयामास तद्राज्यमरिकर्षणः ॥
2.48.m: Having slain the Tālajaṅghas in battle along with their armies and mounts, / that king, the tormentor of foes, gradually destroyed their realm.

2.48.s:
tato yavanakāṃbojakirātādīnanekaśaḥ /
nijaghāna ruṣāviṣṭaḥ palhavānpāradānapi //
2.48.d:
ततो यवनकांबोजकिरातादीननेकशः ।
निजघान रुषाविष्टः पल्हवान्पारदानपि ॥
2.48.m: Then, overcome with fury, he slew Yavanas, Kāmbojas, Kirātas, and many others, / as well as Palhavas and Pāradas.

2.48.s:
hanyamānāstu te sarve rājānastena saṃyuge /
dudruvuḥ saṃghaśo bhītā hataśiṣṭāḥ samantataḥ //
2.48.d:
हन्यमानास्तु ते सर्वे राजानस्तेन संयुगे ।
दुद्रुवुः संघशो भीता हतशिष्टाः समन्ततः ॥
2.48.m: While being slaughtered by him in battle, all those kings, / the survivors of the slaughter, fled in crowds on all sides in terror.

2.48.s:
yuṣmābhiryasya rājyaṃ bahubhirapatdṛtaṃ tasya putro 'dhunāhaṃ hantuṃ vaḥ sapratijñaṃ prasabhamupagato vairaniryātanaiṣī /
