ityuccaiḥ śrāvayāṇo yudhi nijacaritaṃ vairibhirnāgavīryaḥ kṣatrairvidhvaṃsitejāḥ sagaranarapatiḥ smārayāmāsa bhūpaḥ //
2.48.d:
युष्माभिर्यस्य राज्यं बहुभिरपत्दृतं तस्य पुत्रो ऽधुनाहं हन्तुं वः सप्रतिज्ञं प्रसभमुपगतो वैरनिर्यातनैषी ।
इत्युच्चैः श्रावयाणो युधि निजचरितं वैरिभिर्नागवीर्यः क्षत्रैर्विध्वंसितेजाः सगरनरपतिः स्मारयामास भूपः ॥
2.48.m: “I am the son of him whose kingdom was seized by many of you, and I have now come by force under vow to slay you, seeking vengeance for the feud!” / Proclaiming aloud in battle his own conduct thus, the king, lord Sagara, possessing the strength of an elephant, made the kṣatriya enemies whose splendour was ruined remember [their deed].

2.48.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājavaryaṃ sakalaripukulaprakṣayopāttadīkṣaṃ bhītāḥ strībālapūrvaṃ śaraṇamabhiyayuḥ svāsusarakṣaṇāya /
ikṣvākūṇāṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ kulagurumabhitaḥ sapta rājñāṃ kaleṣu prakhyātāḥ saṃprasūtā nṛpavararipavaḥ pāradāḥ palhavādyāḥ //
2.48.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा राजवर्यं सकलरिपुकुलप्रक्षयोपात्तदीक्षं भीताः स्त्रीबालपूर्वं शरणमभिययुः स्वासुसरक्षणाय ।
इक्ष्वाकूणां वसिष्ठं कुलगुरुमभितः सप्त राज्ञां कलेषु प्रख्याताः संप्रसूता नृपवररिपवः पारदाः पल्हवाद्याः ॥
2.48.m: Seeing that best of kings dedicated to the complete extermination of the whole race of enemies, terrified, they went together with their women and children for refuge to save their lives / to Vasiṣṭha, the family guru of the Ikṣvākus; the enemies of that best of kings, born in the lineages of seven kings, famous—the Pāradas, Palhavas, and others—surrounded him.

2.48.s:
vasiṣṭhamāśramopānte vasaṃtamṛṣibhirvṛtam /
upagamyābruvansarve kṛtāñjalipuṭā nṛpāḥ //
2.48.d:
वसिष्ठमाश्रमोपान्ते वसंतमृषिभिर्वृतम् ।
उपगम्याब्रुवन्सर्वे कृताञ्जलिपुटा नृपाः ॥
2.48.m: Approaching Vasiṣṭha who was dwelling near his hermitage surrounded by sages, / all those kings with folded hands said:

2.48.s:
śaraṇaṃ bhaṃva no brahmannārttānāmabhayaiṣiṇām /
sagarāstrāgninirdagdhaśarīrāṇāṃ mumūrṣatām //
2.48.d:
शरणं भंव नो ब्रह्मन्नार्त्तानामभयैषिणाम् ।
सगरास्त्राग्निनिर्दग्धशरीराणां मुमूर्षताम् ॥
2.48.m: “Be our refuge, O holy man, for us who are afflicted and seek freedom from fear, / whose bodies are burned by the fire of Sagara's weapons and who are on the verge of death!

2.48.s:
sa hantyasamānaśeṣeṇa vairāntakaraṇonmukhaḥ /
tasmādbhayāddhi niṣkrāntā vayaṃ jīvitakāṅkṣiṇaḥ //
2.48.d:
स हन्त्यसमानशेषेण वैरान्तकरणोन्मुखः ।
तस्माद्भयाद्धि निष्क्रान्ता वयं जीवितकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
2.48.m: Intent on putting an end to the feud, he is slaying us without remnant; / out of fear of him we have fled, desiring our lives.

2.48.s:
vibhinnarājyabhogarddhisvadārāpatyabāndhavāḥ /
kevalaṃ prāṇarakṣārthaṃ tvāṃ tvayaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
2.48.d:
विभिन्नराज्यभोगर्द्धिस्वदारापत्यबान्धवाः ।
केवलं प्राणरक्षार्थं त्वां त्वयं शरणं गतः ॥
2.48.m: Deprived of the prosperity and enjoyments of our kingdoms, of our own wives, children, and kinsmen, / solely to save our lives have we come to you for refuge.

2.48.s:
na hyanyo 'sti pumāṃlloke sauhṛdena balena vā /
yastaṃ nivarttayitvāsmānpālayenmahato bhayāt //
2.48.d:
न ह्यन्यो ऽस्ति पुमांल्लोके सौहृदेन बलेन वा ।
यस्तं निवर्त्तयित्वास्मान्पालयेन्महतो भयात् ॥
2.48.m: Indeed, there is no other person in the world, whether through friendship or power, / who could turn him back and protect us from this great danger.

2.48.s:
tvaṃ kilārkānvayabhuvāṃ rājñāṃ kulagurur vṛtaḥ /
tadvaṃśapūrvajairbhūpaistvataprabhāvaśca tādṛśaḥ //
2.48.d:
त्वं किलार्कान्वयभुवां राज्ञां कुलगुरुर् वृतः ।
तद्वंशपूर्वजैर्भूपैस्त्वतप्रभावश्च तादृशः ॥
2.48.m: For you were chosen as the family guru of the kings born in the solar lineage / by the royal ancestors of that dynasty, and such is your spiritual power.

2.48.s:
tenāyaṃ sagaro 'pyadya gurugauravayantritaḥ /
bhavannideśaṃ nātyeti velāmiva mahodadhiḥ //
2.48.d:
तेनायं सगरो ऽप्यद्य गुरुगौरवयन्त्रितः ।
भवन्निदेशं नात्येति वेलामिव महोदधिः ॥
2.48.m: Therefore even Sagara today, restrained by reverence for his guru, / will not transgress your command, just as the great ocean does not transgress its shore.

2.48.s:
tvaṃ naḥ suhṛtpitā mātā lokānāṃ ca gururvibho /
tasmādasmānmahābhāga paritrātuṃ tvamarhasi //
2.48.d:
त्वं नः सुहृत्पिता माता लोकानां च गुरुर्विभो ।
तस्मादस्मान्महाभाग परित्रातुं त्वमर्हसि ॥
2.48.m: You are our friend, father, mother, and the guru of the worlds, O almighty lord; / therefore, O highly fortunate one, you ought to protect us.”

2.48.s:
jaiminiruvāca
iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ /
śanairvilokayāmāsa śaraṇaṃ samupāgatān //
2.48.d:
जैमिनिरुवाच
इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः ।
शनैर्विलोकयामास शरणं समुपागतान् ॥
2.48.m: Jaimini said: / Hearing their words, the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha / slowly looked upon those who had come for refuge.

2.48.s:
vṛddhastrībālabhūyiṣṭhānhataśeṣānnṛpānvayān /
dṛṣṭvā tvatapyadbhagavānsarvabhūtānukaṃpakaḥ //
2.48.d:
वृद्धस्त्रीबालभूयिष्ठान्हतशेषान्नृपान्वयान् ।
दृष्ट्वा त्वतप्यद्भगवान्सर्वभूतानुकंपकः ॥
2.48.m: Seeing the survivors of the royal lineages, consisting mostly of old people, women, and children, / the venerable one, who is compassionate to all beings, felt pity.

2.48.s:
ciraṃ nirūpya manasā tānvilokya ca sādaram /
ujjīvayañchanairvācā mā bhaiṣṭeti mahāmatiḥ //
2.48.d:
चिरं निरूप्य मनसा तान्विलोक्य च सादरम् ।
उज्जीवयञ्छनैर्वाचा मा भैष्टेति महामतिः ॥
2.48.m: Reflecting in his mind for a long time and looking at them with kindness, / the highly intelligent one, reviving them slowly with his speech, saying, “Do not fear!”

2.48.s:
athāvocanmahābhāgaḥ kṛpayā parayānvitaḥ /
samaye sthāpayāmāsa rājñastāñjīvitārthinaḥ //
2.48.d:
अथावोचन्महाभागः कृपया परयान्वितः ।
समये स्थापयामास राज्ञस्ताञ्जीवितार्थिनः ॥
2.48.m: then spoke, full of supreme compassion; / the highly fortunate one bound those kings who sought their lives by an agreement.

2.48.s:
bhūpavyā kopadagdhaṃ nṛpakulavihitāśeṣadharmādapetaṃ kṛtvā teṣāṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ samayamavanipālapratijñānivṛttyai /
gatvā taṃ rājavaryaṃ svayamatha śanakaiḥ sāṃtvayitvā yathāvatsaprāṇānāmarīṇāmapagamanavidhāvabhyanujñāṃ yayāce //
2.48.d:
भूपव्या कोपदग्धं नृपकुलविहिताशेषधर्मादपेतं कृत्वा तेषां वसिष्ठः समयमवनिपालप्रतिज्ञानिवृत्त्यै ।
गत्वा तं राजवर्यं स्वयमथ शनकैः सांत्वयित्वा यथावत्सप्राणानामरीणामपगमनविधावभ्यनुज्ञां ययाचे ॥
2.48.m: After making an agreement with them to ward off the king's vow, since they were burnt by the king's anger and deprived of all the duties prescribed for a royal line, Vasiṣṭha went in person to that best of kings, consoled him gently as was fitting, and asked permission for his enemies to depart with their lives.

2.48.s:
sakrodho 'pi mahīpatirguruvacaḥ saṃbhāvayaṃstānarīndharmasya svakulocitasya ca tathā veṣasya saṃtyāgataḥ /
śrautasmārttavibhinnakarmaniratānvipraiśca dūroñjhitānsāsūnkevalamatyajanmṛtasamānekaikaśaḥ pārthivān //
2.48.d:
सक्रोधो ऽपि महीपतिर्गुरुवचः संभावयंस्तानरीन्धर्मस्य स्वकुलोचितस्य च तथा वेषस्य संत्यागतः ।
श्रौतस्मार्त्तविभिन्नकर्मनिरतान्विप्रैश्च दूरोञ्झितान्सासून्केवलमत्यजन्मृतसमानेकैकशः पार्थिवान् ॥
2.48.m: Though enraged, the king respected his guru's word, and one by one spared those rulers alive, yet as good as dead, having caused them to abandon the dharma and dress suited to their own families, setting them to engage in acts at variance with Śruti and Smṛti, and having them cast far off by the brahmins.

2.48.s:
arddhamuṇḍāñchakāṃścakre palhavān śmaśrudhāriṇaḥ /
yavanānvigataśmaśrūnkāṃbojāṃścabukānvitān //
2.48.d:
अर्द्धमुण्डाञ्छकांश्चक्रे पल्हवान् श्मश्रुधारिणः ।
यवनान्विगतश्मश्रून्कांबोजांश्चबुकान्वितान् ॥
2.48.m: He made the Śakas half-shaven; the Pahlavas he made wear beards; / the Yavanas shaven-bearded; and the Kāmbojas keep beards on their chins.

2.48.s:
evaṃ virūpānanyāṃśca sa cakāra nṛpānvayān /
vedoktakarmanirmuktānvipraiśca parivarjitān //
2.48.d:
एवं विरूपानन्यांश्च स चकार नृपान्वयान् ।
वेदोक्तकर्मनिर्मुक्तान्विप्रैश्च परिवर्जितान् ॥
2.48.m: In this way, he disfigured other royal lineages as well, / freeing them from the rites prescribed in the Veda and cast out by brahmins.

2.48.s:
kṛtvā saṃsthāpya samaye jīvatastānvya sarjayat /
tataste ripavastasya tyaktasvācāralakṣaṇāḥ //
2.48.d:
कृत्वा संस्थाप्य समये जीवतस्तान्व्य सर्जयत् ।
ततस्ते रिपवस्तस्य त्यक्तस्वाचारलक्षणाः ॥
2.48.m: Having done so and binding them to the agreement, he released them alive. / Thereupon, those enemies of his, abandoning the marks of their proper conduct,

2.48.s:
vrātyatāṃ samanuprāptāḥ sarvavarṇavinintitāḥ /
dhikkṛtā satataṃ sarvenṛśaṃsā nirapatrapāḥ //
2.48.d:
व्रात्यतां समनुप्राप्ताः सर्ववर्णविनिन्तिताः ।
धिक्कृता सततं सर्वेनृशंसा निरपत्रपाः ॥
2.48.m: became outcasts, reviled by all varnas, / constantly censured by all, cruel and shameless.

2.48.s: krūrāśca saṃghaśo loke babhūvurmlechajātayaḥ //
2.48.d: क्रूराश्च संघशो लोके बभूवुर्म्लेछजातयः ॥
2.48.m: Fierce, they became hosts of Mleccha castes in the world.

2.48.s:
muktāstenātha rājñā śakayavanakirātādayaḥ sadya eva tyaktasvācāraveṣā girigahanaguhādyāśayāḥ saṃbabhūvuḥ /
etā adyāpi sadbhiḥ satatamavamatā jātayo 'satpravṛttyā varttante duṣṭaceṣṭā jagati narapateḥ pālayantaḥ pratijñām //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde sagaropākhyāne sagarapratijñāpālanaṃ nāmāṣṭācatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 48//
2.48.d:
मुक्तास्तेनाथ राज्ञा शकयवनकिरातादयः सद्य एव त्यक्तस्वाचारवेषा गिरिगहनगुहाद्याशयाः संबभूवुः ।
एता अद्यापि सद्भिः सततमवमता जातयो ऽसत्प्रवृत्त्या वर्त्तन्ते दुष्टचेष्टा जगति नरपतेः पालयन्तः प्रतिज्ञाम् ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे सगरोपाख्याने सगरप्रतिज्ञापालनं नामाष्टाचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 48॥
2.48.m:
Released by that king, the Śakas, Yavanas, Kirātas, and others instantly abandoned their proper conduct and dress, making their dwellings in mountains, thickets, caves, and the like. / Even today these castes, constantly despised by the virtuous because of their unrighteous ways, live in the world acting wickedly, keeping the king's vow.

Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, named 'Fulfillment of Sagara's Vow' in the Sagara episode, in the third section, the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, spoken by Vāyu. // 48

2.49.s:
jaiminiruvāca
athānujñāya sagaro vasiṣṭhamṛṣisattamam /
balena mahatā yukto vidarbhānabhyavarttata //
2.49.d:
जैमिनिरुवाच
अथानुज्ञाय सगरो वसिष्ठमृषिसत्तमम् ।
बलेन महता युक्तो विदर्भानभ्यवर्त्तत ॥
2.49.m: Jaimini said: / Then, having taken leave of Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages, / Sagara, accompanied by a great army, set out toward Vidarbha.

2.49.s:
tato vidarbharāṭ tasmai svasutāṃ prītipūrvakam /
keśinyākhyāmanupamāmanurūpāṃ nyavedayat //
2.49.d:
ततो विदर्भराट् तस्मै स्वसुतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ।
केशिन्याख्यामनुपमामनुरूपां न्यवेदयत् ॥
2.49.m: Then the king of Vidarbha affectionately offered him / his own daughter named Keśinī, matchless and suitable for him.

2.49.s:
sa tasyā rājaśārdūlo vidhivadvahnisākṣikam /
śubhe muhūrte keśinyāḥ pārṇiṃ jagrāha bhūmipaḥ //
2.49.d:
स तस्या राजशार्दूलो विधिवद्वह्निसाक्षिकम् ।
शुभे मुहूर्ते केशिन्याः पार्णिं जग्राह भूमिपः ॥
2.49.m: That tiger among kings, the ruler of the earth, / took Keśinī's hand according to rule before the witness of fire, at an auspicious moment.

2.49.s:
sthitvā dināni katicidgṛhe tasyātisatkṛtaḥ /
vidarbharājñā saṃmantrya tato gantuṃ prajakrame //
2.49.d:
स्थित्वा दिनानि कतिचिद्गृहे तस्यातिसत्कृतः ।
विदर्भराज्ञा संमन्त्र्य ततो गन्तुं प्रजक्रमे ॥
2.49.m: Having stayed a few days in his house, highly honored, / he consulted with the king of Vidarbha and then prepared to depart.

2.49.s:
anujñātastatastena pāribarhaiśca satkṛtaḥ /
niṣkramya tatpurādrājā śūrasenānupeyivān //
2.49.d:
अनुज्ञातस्ततस्तेन पारिबर्हैश्च सत्कृतः ।
निष्क्रम्य तत्पुराद्राजा शूरसेनानुपेयिवान् ॥
2.49.m: Permitted by him and honored with wedding gifts, / the king departed from that city and went to the Śūrasenas.

2.49.s:
saṃbhāvitastataścaiva yādavairmātṛsodaraiḥ /
dhanaughaistarpitastaiśca madhurāyā viniryayau //
2.49.d:
संभावितस्ततश्चैव यादवैर्मातृसोदरैः ।
धनौघैस्तर्पितस्तैश्च मधुराया विनिर्ययौ ॥
2.49.m: Then, respected by the Yādavas, the brothers of his mother, / and gratified by them with streams of wealth, he set out from Mathurā.

2.49.s:
evaṃ sa sagaro rājā vijitya vasudhāmimām /
karaiśca sa nṛpānsarvāṃścakre saṃketagānapi //
2.49.d:
एवं स सगरो राजा विजित्य वसुधामिमाम् ।
करैश्च स नृपान्सर्वांश्चक्रे संकेतगानपि ॥
2.49.m: Having thus conquered this earth, King Sagara / made all kings pay tribute and bound them to agreements.

2.49.s:
tato 'numānya nṛpatīnnijarājyāya sānugān /
anujajñe narapatiḥ samastānanuyāyinaḥ //
2.49.d:
ततो ऽनुमान्य नृपतीन्निजराज्याय सानुगान् ।
अनुजज्ञे नरपतिः समस्ताननुयायिनः ॥
2.49.m: Then, having granted permission to the kings and their followers to return to their own kingdoms, / the ruler of men gave leave to all his followers.

2.49.s:
tato balena mahātā skandhāvārasamanvitaḥ /
śanairapīḍayandeśānsvarājyamupajagmivān //
2.49.d:
ततो बलेन महाता स्कन्धावारसमन्वितः ।
शनैरपीडयन्देशान्स्वराज्यमुपजग्मिवान् ॥
2.49.m: Then, accompanied by his army camp and with a great force, / he went gently without oppressing the lands, returning to his own kingdom.

2.49.s:
saṃbhāvyamānaśca muhurupadābhiranekaśaḥ /
nānājanapadaistūrmamayodhyāṃ samupāgamat //
2.49.d:
संभाव्यमानश्च मुहुरुपदाभिरनेकशः ।
नानाजनपदैस्तूर्ममयोध्यां समुपागमत् ॥
2.49.m: Being honored continually with gifts of varied kinds / by diverse provinces, he swiftly arrived at Ayodhyā.

2.49.s:
tadāgamanamājñāya nāgaraḥ sakalo janaḥ /
nagarīṃ tāmalañcakre mahotsavasamutsukaḥ //
2.49.d:
तदागमनमाज्ञाय नागरः सकलो जनः ।
नगरीं तामलञ्चक्रे महोत्सवसमुत्सुकः ॥
2.49.m: Learning of his arrival, all the city folk, / eager for a great festival, decorated that city.

2.49.s:
tataḥ sā nagarī sarvā kṛtakautukamaṅgalā /
siktasaṃmṛṣṭabhūbhāgā pūrṇakumbhaśatāvṛtā //
2.49.d:
ततः सा नगरी सर्वा कृतकौतुकमङ्गला ।
सिक्तसंमृष्टभूभागा पूर्णकुम्भशतावृता ॥
2.49.m: Then that entire city had auspicious rituals performed, / its ground sprinkled and swept, filled with hundreds of full jars,

2.49.s:
samucchritadhvajaśatā patākābhiraṃlakṛtā /
sarvatrāgarudhūpāñaḍhyā vicitrakusumojjvalā //
2.49.d:
समुच्छ्रितध्वजशता पताकाभिरंलकृता ।
सर्वत्रागरुधूपाञढ्या विचित्रकुसुमोज्ज्वला ॥
2.49.m: with hundreds of raised standards, adorned with banners, / rich everywhere with the incense of agallochum, bright with colorful flowers,

2.49.s:
sadratnatoraṇottuṅgagopurāṭṭalabhūṣitā /
prasūnalājavarṣaiśca svalaṅkṛtamahāpathā //
2.49.d:
सद्रत्नतोरणोत्तुङ्गगोपुराट्टलभूषिता ।
प्रसूनलाजवर्षैश्च स्वलङ्कृतमहापथा ॥
2.49.m: adorned with archways of fine gems, lofty gateway towers, and battlements, / its broad highways well adorned with showers of flowers and parched grain.

2.49.s:
mahotsavasamāyuktā pratigehamabhūtpurī /
saṃbūjitāśeṣavāstudevatāgṛhamālinī //
2.49.d:
महोत्सवसमायुक्ता प्रतिगेहमभूत्पुरी ।
संबूजिताशेषवास्तुदेवतागृहमालिनी ॥
2.49.m: At every house the city was filled with great festivities, / hung with garlands for all the house-deities who had been worshipped;

2.49.s:
dikcakrajayino rājñaḥ saṃdarśanamudānvitaiḥ /
paurajānapadairtdṛṣṭaiḥ sarvataḥ samalaṅkṛtā //
2.49.d:
दिक्चक्रजयिनो राज्ञः संदर्शनमुदान्वितैः ।
पौरजानपदैर्त्दृष्टैः सर्वतः समलङ्कृता ॥
2.49.m: it was adorned on all sides by joyful citizens and country folk / who were filled with joy at the sight of the king, the conqueror of all the directions.

2.49.s:
tataḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarve tathāntaḥ puravāsinaḥ /
vārakātākadabaiśca nagarībhiśca savṛtāḥ //
2.49.d:
ततः प्रकृतयः सर्वे तथान्तः पुरवासिनः ।
वारकाताकदबैश्च नगरीभिश्च सवृताः ॥
2.49.m: Then all the subjects and the dwellers of the inner apartments, / surrounded by hosts of courtesans and city women,

2.49.s:
abhyāyayustataḥ sarve samatya puravāsinaḥ /
sa taiḥ sametya nṛpatirlabdhāśīrvāda saktkriyaḥ //
2.49.d:
अभ्याययुस्ततः सर्वे समत्य पुरवासिनः ।
स तैः समेत्य नृपतिर्लब्धाशीर्वाद सक्त्क्रियः ॥
2.49.m: and all the city dwellers came together and approached. / The king, having met with them and received blessings and honors,

2.49.s:
badhirīkṛtadikcakro jayaśabdena bhūriṇā /
nānāvāditrasaṃghoṣamiśreṇa madhureṇa ca //
2.49.d:
बधिरीकृतदिक्चक्रो जयशब्देन भूरिणा ।
नानावादित्रसंघोषमिश्रेण मधुरेण च ॥
2.49.m: deafening the compass of the directions with a great sound of victory / mingled with the sweet noise of various musical instruments,

2.49.s:
satkṛtya tānyathā yogaṃ sahitastairmudānvitaiḥ /
ānandayanprajāḥ sarvāḥ praviveśa purottamam //
2.49.d:
सत्कृत्य तान्यथा योगं सहितस्तैर्मुदान्वितैः ।
आनन्दयन्प्रजाः सर्वाः प्रविवेश पुरोत्तमम् ॥
2.49.m: honoring them as was fitting, accompanied by those delighted people / and gladdening all his subjects, entered the supreme city.

2.49.s:
vedaghoṣaiḥ sumadhurairbrāhmaṇairabhinanditaḥ /
saṃstūyamānaḥ subhṛśaṃ sūtamāgadhavandibhiḥ //
2.49.d:
वेदघोषैः सुमधुरैर्ब्राह्मणैरभिनन्दितः ।
संस्तूयमानः सुभृशं सूतमागधवन्दिभिः ॥
2.49.m: Welcomed with the sweetest Vedic recitations by brahmins, / praised exceedingly by bards, panegyrists, and minstrels,

2.49.s:
jayaśabdaiśca parito nānājanapaderitaiḥ /
kalatālaravonmiśravīṇāveṇutalasvanaiḥ //
2.49.d:
जयशब्दैश्च परितो नानाजनपदेरितैः ।
कलतालरवोन्मिश्रवीणावेणुतलस्वनैः ॥
2.49.m: with shouts of victory sounded on all sides by diverse peoples, / with sounds of lutes, flutes, and cymbals mingled with soft rhythmic beats,

2.49.s:
gāyadbhirgāyakajanairnṛtyadbhirgaṇikājanaiḥ /
anvīyamāno vilasacchvetacchatravirājitaḥ //
2.49.d:
गायद्भिर्गायकजनैर्नृत्यद्भिर्गणिकाजनैः ।
अन्वीयमानो विलसच्छ्वेतच्छत्रविराजितः ॥
2.49.m: surrounded by singing singers and dancing courtesans, / shining with a radiant white parasol,

2.49.s:
vikīryamāṇaḥ paritaḥ sallājakusumotkaraiḥ /
purīmayodhyāmaviśatsvapurīmiva vāsavaḥ //
2.49.d:
विकीर्यमाणः परितः सल्लाजकुसुमोत्करैः ।
पुरीमयोध्यामविशत्स्वपुरीमिव वासवः ॥
2.49.m: scattered all around with showers of fine parched grain and flowers, / he entered the city of Ayodhyā as Indra enters his own city.

2.49.s:
dṛṣṭipūtena gandhena brāhmaṇānāṃ ca vartmanā /
jagāma madhyenagaraṃ gṛhaṃ śrīmadalaṅkṛtam //
2.49.d:
दृष्टिपूतेन गन्धेन ब्राह्मणानां च वर्त्मना ।
जगाम मध्येनगरं गृहं श्रीमदलङ्कृतम् ॥
2.49.m: Along the pathway purified by the sight and sweet scent of the brahmins, / he went through the midst of the city to his glorious and adorned palace.

2.49.s:
avaruhya tato yānādbhāryābhyāṃ sahito mudā /
praviveśa gṛhaṃ māturhṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāyutam //
2.49.d:
अवरुह्य ततो यानाद्भार्याभ्यां सहितो मुदा ।
प्रविवेश गृहं मातुर्हृष्टपुष्टजनायुतम् ॥
2.49.m: Then, joyfully stepping down from the chariot together with his two wives, / he entered his mother's house, which was filled with delighted and prosperous people.

2.49.s:
paryaṅkasthāmupāgamya mātaraṃ vinayānvitaḥ /
tatpādau saṃspṛśanmūrdhnā praṇāmamakarottadā //
2.49.d:
पर्यङ्कस्थामुपागम्य मातरं विनयान्वितः ।
तत्पादौ संस्पृशन्मूर्ध्ना प्रणाममकरोत्तदा ॥
2.49.m: Approaching his mother, who sat upon a couch, full of modesty, / he touched her feet with his head and made his prostration.

2.49.s:
sābhinandya tamāśīrbhirharṣagadgadayā girā /
sasaṃbhramaṃ samutthāya paryaṣvajata cātmajam //
2.49.d:
साभिनन्द्य तमाशीर्भिर्हर्षगद्गदया गिरा ।
ससंभ्रमं समुत्थाय पर्यष्वजत चात्मजम् ॥
2.49.m: Greeting him with blessings in a voice stammering with joy, / she rose in excitement and embraced her son.

2.49.s:
saharṣaṃ bahudhāśīrbhirabhyanandadubhe snuṣe /
sa tāṃ saṃbhāvya kathayā tatra sthitvā cirādiva //
2.49.d:
सहर्षं बहुधाशीर्भिरभ्यनन्ददुभे स्नुषे ।
स तां संभाव्य कथया तत्र स्थित्वा चिरादिव ॥
2.49.m: With joy she repeatedly blessed both her daughters-in-law; / and having honored her with conversation and stayed there for a while,

2.49.s:
anujñātastayā rājā niścakrāma tadālayāt /
tataḥ sānucaro rājā śvetavyajanavījitaḥ //
2.49.d:
अनुज्ञातस्तया राजा निश्चक्राम तदालयात् ।
ततः सानुचरो राजा श्वेतव्यजनवीजितः ॥
2.49.m: the king, taking leave of her, departed from her abode. / Then the king, accompanied by his attendants and fanned with white fly-whisks,

2.49.s:
surarāja iva śrīmānsabhāṃ samagamacchanaiḥ /
saṃpraviśya sabhāṃ divyāmanekanṛpasevitām //
2.49.d:
सुरराज इव श्रीमान्सभां समगमच्छनैः ।
संप्रविश्य सभां दिव्यामनेकनृपसेविताम् ॥
2.49.m: like the glorious king of the gods, went slowly to the assembly hall. / Having entered the divine assembly hall attended by many kings,

2.49.s:
natvā gurujanaṃ sarvamāśīrbhiścābhinanditaḥ /
siṃhāsane śubhe divye niṣasāda nareśvaraḥ //
2.49.d:
नत्वा गुरुजनं सर्वमाशीर्भिश्चाभिनन्दितः ।
सिंहासने शुभे दिव्ये निषसाद नरेश्वरः ॥
2.49.m: bowing down to all the elders and greeted with blessings, / the lord of men sat down upon an auspicious, divine throne.

2.49.s:
saṃsevyamānaśca nṛpairnānājanapadeśvaraiḥ /
nānāvidhāḥ kathāḥ kurvansa tatra nṛpasattamaḥ //
2.49.d:
संसेव्यमानश्च नृपैर्नानाजनपदेश्वरैः ।
नानाविधाः कथाः कुर्वन्स तत्र नृपसत्तमः ॥
2.49.m: Attended by kings, the lords of various lands, / and conversing on various subjects, that best of kings,

2.49.s:
saṃprīyamāmaḥ sutarāmuvāsa saha bandhubhiḥ /
pratijñāṃ pālayitvaivaṃ jitadiṅmaṇḍalo nṛpaḥ //
2.49.d:
संप्रीयमामः सुतरामुवास सह बन्धुभिः ।
प्रतिज्ञां पालयित्वैवं जितदिङ्मण्डलो नृपः ॥
2.49.m: exceedingly delighted, dwelt together with his kinsmen. / Having thus fulfilled his vow, the king, the conqueror of the circle of the quarters,

2.49.s:
anvatiṣṭhadyanthānyāya marthatrayamudāradhīḥ /
svaprabhāvajitāśeṣavairirdiṅmaṇḍalādhipaḥ //
2.49.d:
अन्वतिष्ठद्यन्थान्याय मर्थत्रयमुदारधीः ।
स्वप्रभावजिताशेषवैरिर्दिङ्मण्डलाधिपः ॥
2.49.m: noble in mind, pursued the three aims [of life] in accordance with propriety. / Having conquered all enemies by his own splendor, the lord of the circle of the quarters

2.49.s:
ekātapatrāṃ pṛthivīmanvaśāsadvṛṣo yathā /
svaryātasya pituḥ pūrvaṃ paribhāvamamarṣitaḥ //
2.49.d:
एकातपत्रां पृथिवीमन्वशासद्वृषो यथा ।
स्वर्यातस्य पितुः पूर्वं परिभावममर्षितः ॥
2.49.m: ruled over the earth under a single royal parasol like a bull, / having earlier resented the humiliation of his father who had gone to heaven.

2.49.s:
sa yāṃ pratijñāmārūḍhastāṃ samyakparipūrya ca /
saptadvīpābdhinagaragrāmāyatanamālinīm //
2.49.d:
स यां प्रतिज्ञामारूढस्तां सम्यक्परिपूर्य च ।
सप्तद्वीपाब्धिनगरग्रामायतनमालिनीम् ॥
2.49.m: Having fully carried out the vow he had undertaken, / [he protected the earth] garlanded with its seven continents, oceans, cities, villages, and hermitages.

2.49.s:
jitvā śatrūnaśeṣeṇa pālayāmāsa medinīma /
evaṃ gacchati kāle ca vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ //
2.49.d:
जित्वा शत्रूनशेषेण पालयामास मेदिनीम ।
एवं गच्छति काले च वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः ॥
2.49.m: Having conquered his enemies entirely, he protected the earth. / And as time passed in this way, the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha,

2.49.s:
abhyajagāma taṃ bhūyo draṣṭukāmo jareśvaram /
tamāyāntamatiprekṣya munivaryaṃ sasaṃbhramaḥ //
2.49.d:
अभ्यजगाम तं भूयो द्रष्टुकामो जरेश्वरम् ।
तमायान्तमतिप्रेक्ष्य मुनिवर्यं ससंभ्रमः ॥
2.49.m: wishing to see the lord of men again, came there. / Seeing that foremost of sages arriving, in haste,

2.49.s:
pratyujjagāmārghahastaḥ sahitastairnapairnṛpaḥ /
ardhyapādyādibhiḥ samyakpūjayitvā mahāmatiḥ //
2.49.d:
प्रत्युज्जगामार्घहस्तः सहितस्तैर्नपैर्नृपः ।
अर्ध्यपाद्यादिभिः सम्यक्पूजयित्वा महामतिः ॥
2.49.m: the king, together with those kings, went out to meet him with respectful offering in hand. / Having duly honoured him with respectful offering, water for the feet, and other rites, the wise one

2.49.s:
praṇāmamakarottasmai gurubhaktisamanvitaḥ /
āśīrbhirvarddhayitvā taṃ vasiṣṭhaḥ sagaraṃ tadā //
2.49.d:
प्रणाममकरोत्तस्मै गुरुभक्तिसमन्वितः ।
आशीर्भिर्वर्द्धयित्वा तं वसिष्ठः सगरं तदा ॥
2.49.m: bowed down to him, filled with devotion to the guru. / Then Vasiṣṭha, having congratulated Sagara with blessings,

2.49.s:
āsyatāmiti hovāca saha sarvairnareśvaraiḥ /
upāviśattato rājā kāñcane paramāsane //
2.49.d:
आस्यतामिति होवाच सह सर्वैर्नरेश्वरैः ।
उपाविशत्ततो राजा काञ्चने परमासने ॥
2.49.m: said to him: “Be seated, along with all the rulers of men.” / Thereupon the king sat down upon an excellent golden seat,

2.49.s:
muninā samanujñātaḥ sabhāryaḥ saha rājabhiḥ /
āpavastunṛpaśreṣṭhamupāsīnamupahvare //
2.49.d:
मुनिना समनुज्ञातः सभार्यः सह राजभिः ।
आपवस्तुनृपश्रेष्ठमुपासीनमुपह्वरे ॥
2.49.m: permitted by the sage, accompanied by his wife and the kings. / Then Āpava [Vasiṣṭha] addressed the foremost of kings, who was seated close by,

2.49.s:
uvāca śṛṇvatāṃ rājñāṃ śanairmṛdvakṣaraṃ vacaḥ /
vasiṣṭha uvāca
kuśalaṃ nanu te rājanvāhyeṣvābhyantareṣu ca //
2.49.d:
उवाच शृण्वतां राज्ञां शनैर्मृद्वक्षरं वचः ।
वसिष्ठ उवाच
कुशलं ननु ते राजन्वाह्येष्वाभ्यन्तरेषु च ॥
2.49.m: speaking softly and gently so that the kings could hear: / Vasiṣṭha said: / “Is all well with you, O king, among external and internal affairs,

2.49.s:
mantriṣvamātyavargeṣu rājye vā sakale 'dhunā /
diṣṭyā ca vijitāḥ sarve samagrabalavāhanāḥ //
2.49.d:
मन्त्रिष्वमात्यवर्गेषु राज्ये वा सकले ऽधुना ।
दिष्ट्या च विजिताः सर्वे समग्रबलवाहनाः ॥
2.49.m: among your counsellors, assemblies of ministers, and in your entire kingdom now? / By good fortune all your enemies, with all their forces and conveyances,

2.49.s:
ayatnenaiva yuddheṣu bhavatā ripavo hi yat /
diṣṭyārūḍhapratijñena mama mānayatā vacaḥ //
2.49.d:
अयत्नेनैव युद्धेषु भवता रिपवो हि यत् ।
दिष्ट्यारूढप्रतिज्ञेन मम मानयता वचः ॥
2.49.m: have indeed been conquered by you in battle without effort! / By good fortune you, holding firm to your vow and honouring my word,

2.49.s:
arayastyaktadharmāṇastvayā jīvavisarjitāḥ /
tānvijityetarāñjetuṃ punardigvijayecchayā //
2.49.d:
अरयस्त्यक्तधर्माणस्त्वया जीवविसर्जिताः ।
तान्विजित्येतराञ्जेतुं पुनर्दिग्विजयेच्छया ॥
2.49.m: have spared the lives of those enemies who abandoned dharma. / Having conquered them, wishing to conquer others in a campaign of universal conquest,

2.49.s:
gatassavāhanabalastvamityaśṛṇavaṃ vacaḥ /
jitadiṅmaṇḍalaṃ bhūyaḥ śrutvā tvāṃ nagarasthitam //
2.49.d:
गतस्सवाहनबलस्त्वमित्यशृणवं वचः ।
जितदिङ्मण्डलं भूयः श्रुत्वा त्वां नगरस्थितम् ॥
2.49.m: you set out with conveyances and armies—so I heard word. / Having heard that you, having conquered the circle of the quarters, are once more settled in your city,

2.49.s:
prītyāhamāgato draṣṭumidānīṃ rājasattama /
jaiminiruvāca
vasiṣṭhenaivamuktastu sagarastālajaṅghajit //
2.49.d:
प्रीत्याहमागतो द्रष्टुमिदानीं राजसत्तम ।
जैमिनिरुवाच
वसिष्ठेनैवमुक्तस्तु सगरस्तालजङ्घजित् ॥
2.49.m: I have come now out of affection to see you, O best of kings.” / Jaimini said: / Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, Sagara, conqueror of the Tālajaṅghas,

2.49.s:
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā pratyuvāca mahāmunim /
sagara uvāca
kuśalaṃ nanu sarvatra maharṣe nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.49.d:
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच महामुनिम् ।
सगर उवाच
कुशलं ननु सर्वत्र महर्षे नात्र संशयः ॥
2.49.m: folded his hands in reverence and replied to the great sage: / Sagara said: / “All is indeed well in every way, O great sage; of this there is no doubt.

2.49.s:
kalyāṇābhimukhāḥ sarve devatāśca mune 'niśam /
bhavāndhyāyati kalyāṇaṃ manasā yasya saṃtatam //
2.49.d:
कल्याणाभिमुखाः सर्वे देवताश्च मुने ऽनिशम् ।
भवान्ध्यायति कल्याणं मनसा यस्य संततम् ॥
2.49.m: All deities are constantly inclined toward welfare, O sage, / for him whose welfare you continually contemplate in your mind.

2.49.s:
tasya me copasargāśca saṃbhavanti kathaṃ mune /
bhavatānugṛhīto 'smi kṛtārthaścādhunā kṛtaḥ //
2.49.d:
तस्य मे चोपसर्गाश्च संभवन्ति कथं मुने ।
भवतानुगृहीतो ऽस्मि कृतार्थश्चाधुना कृतः ॥
2.49.m: How could afflictions befall me, O sage? / I have been favoured by you, and now made accomplished in my purpose,

2.49.s:
yanmāṃ draṣṭumihāyātaḥ svayameva bhavānguro /
yanmahyamāha bhagavānvipakṣavijayādikam //
2.49.d:
यन्मां द्रष्टुमिहायातः स्वयमेव भवान्गुरो ।
यन्मह्यमाह भगवान्विपक्षविजयादिकम् ॥
2.49.m: in that you, O guru, have yourself come here to see me. / As for what your reverence spoke of concerning the conquest of adversaries and the like,

2.49.s:
tattathānuṣṭhitaṃ kiṃ tu sarvaṃ bhavadanugrahāt /
bhavatprasādataḥ sarvaṃ manye prāptaṃ mahīkṣitām //
2.49.d:
तत्तथानुष्ठितं किं तु सर्वं भवदनुग्रहात् ।
भवत्प्रसादतः सर्वं मन्ये प्राप्तं महीक्षिताम् ॥
2.49.m: all that was accomplished in that way solely through your grace. / Through your favour, I deem, everything is obtained by rulers of the earth.

2.49.s:
anyathā mama kā śaktiḥ śatrūnhantuṃ tathāvidhān /
analpī kurute phalyaṃ yanme vyavasitaṃ bhavān //
2.49.d:
अन्यथा मम का शक्तिः शत्रून्हन्तुं तथाविधान् ।
अनल्पी कुरुते फल्यं यन्मे व्यवसितं भवान् ॥
2.49.m: Otherwise, what power would I have had to slay such enemies? / That you magnify my undertaking as fruitful—

2.49.s:
phalamalpamapi prītyai syādagasyādhiropituḥ /
jaiminiruvāca
evaṃ saṃbhāvitaḥ samyaksageraṇa mahāmuniḥ //
2.49.d:
फलमल्पमपि प्रीत्यै स्यादगस्याधिरोपितुः ।
जैमिनिरुवाच
एवं संभावितः सम्यक्सगेरण महामुनिः ॥
2.49.m: even a small fruit would bring joy to one who planted the tree.” / Jaimini said: / Having been thus duly honoured by Sagara, the great sage,

2.49.s:
abhyanujñāya taṃ bhūyaḥ prajāgāma nijāśramam /
vasiṣṭe tu gate rājā sagaraḥprītamānasaḥ //
2.49.d:
अभ्यनुज्ञाय तं भूयः प्रजागाम निजाश्रमम् ।
वसिष्टे तु गते राजा सगरःप्रीतमानसः ॥
2.49.m: after bidding him farewell, departed once again to his own hermitage. / When Vasiṣṭha had departed, King Sagara, glad at heart,

2.49.s:
ayodhyāyāmabhivasanpraśaśāsākhilāṃ bhuvam /
bhāryābhyāṃ samupetābhyāṃ rūpaśīlaguṇādibhiḥ //
2.49.d:
अयोध्यायामभिवसन्प्रशशासाखिलां भुवम् ।
भार्याभ्यां समुपेताभ्यां रूपशीलगुणादिभिः ॥
2.49.m: dwelling in Ayodhyā, ruled the whole earth. / Accompanied by his two wives endowed with beauty, good character, and virtues,

2.49.s:
bubhuje viṣayānramyānyathākāmaṃ yathāsukham /
sumatiḥ keśinī cobhe vikasadvadanāṃbuje //
2.49.d:
बुभुजे विषयान्रम्यान्यथाकामं यथासुखम् ।
सुमतिः केशिनी चोभे विकसद्वदनांबुजे ॥
2.49.m: he enjoyed delightful objects of sense at will and at pleasure. / Both Sumati and Keśinī, whose lotus-faces were blooming,

2.49.s:
rūpaudāryaguṇopete pīnavṛttapayodhare /
nīlakuñcitakeśāḍhye sarvābharaṇabhūṣite //
2.49.d:
रूपौदार्यगुणोपेते पीनवृत्तपयोधरे ।
नीलकुञ्चितकेशाढ्ये सर्वाभरणभूषिते ॥
2.49.m: endowed with beauty and nobility of virtues, with plump, rounded breasts, / graced with dark, curly hair, adorned with all ornaments,

2.49.s:
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpanne navayauvanagocare /
priye sannihite tasya nityaṃ priyahite rate //
2.49.d:
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्ने नवयौवनगोचरे ।
प्रिये सन्निहिते तस्य नित्यं प्रियहिते रते ॥
2.49.m: endowed with every auspicious mark, in the bloom of fresh youth, / beloved and close to him, were ever devoted to his pleasure and welfare.

2.49.s:
svācārabhāvaceṣṭābhirjahratustanmano 'niśam /
sa cāpi bharaṇotkarṣapratītātmā mahīpatiḥ //
2.49.d:
स्वाचारभावचेष्टाभिर्जह्रतुस्तन्मनो ऽनिशम् ।
स चापि भरणोत्कर्षप्रतीतात्मा महीपतिः ॥
2.49.m: Through their good conduct, affection, and graceful gestures, they continually captivated his heart; / and that lord of the earth, his soul renowned for excellence in providing for others,

2.49.s:
ramamāṇo yathākāmaṃ saha tābhyāṃ pure 'vasat /
anyeṣāṃ bhuvi rājñāṃ tu rājaśabdo na cāpyabhūt //
2.49.d:
रममाणो यथाकामं सह ताभ्यां पुरे ऽवसत् ।
अन्येषां भुवि राज्ञां तु राजशब्दो न चाप्यभूत् ॥
2.49.m: dwelt in the city sporting at will with both of them. / Indeed, the title of ‘king’ was not held by other kings on earth

2.49.s:
guṇena cābhavattasya sagarasya mahātmanaḥ /
alpo 'pi dharmaḥ satataṃ yathā bhavati mānase //
2.49.d:
गुणेन चाभवत्तस्य सगरस्य महात्मनः ।
अल्पो ऽपि धर्मः सततं यथा भवति मानसे ॥
2.49.m: by virtue of merit as it was by that high-souled Sagara. / In order that even a small dharma might constantly remain in his mind,

2.49.s:
rā5stasyārthakāmau tu na tathā vipulāvapi /
alubdhamānasor'thaṃ ca bheje dharmamapīḍayan //
2.49.d:
रा5स्तस्यार्थकामौ तु न तथा विपुलावपि ।
अलुब्धमानसोर्ऽथं च भेजे धर्ममपीडयन् ॥
2.49.m: [he did not let] wealth and desire, even though extensive, [harm it]. / With a mind free of greed, he pursued wealth without injuring dharma,

2.49.s:
tadarthameva rājendra kāmaṃ cāpīḍayaṃstayoḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde sagaradigvijayo nāmaikonapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 49//
2.49.d:
तदर्थमेव राजेन्द्र कामं चापीडयंस्तयोः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे सगरदिग्विजयो नामैकोनपञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 49॥
2.49.m:
and for that very purpose, O king of kings, he enjoyed pleasure without harming either of them.

Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, named ‘The Universal Conquest of Sagara,’ in the third [section], the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part proclaimed by Vāyu in the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa.

2.50.s:
jaiminiruvāca
evaṃ sa rājā vidhivatpālayāmāsa medinīm /
saptadvīpavatīṃ samyaksākṣāddharma ivāparaḥ //
2.50.d:
जैमिनिरुवाच
एवं स राजा विधिवत्पालयामास मेदिनीम् ।
सप्तद्वीपवतीं सम्यक्साक्षाद्धर्म इवापरः ॥
2.50.m: Jaimini said: / Thus that king duly protected the earth / possessing the seven continents, like another Dharma incarnate.

2.50.s:
brāhmaṇādīṃstathā varṇānsvesve dharme pṛthakpṛthak /
sthāpayitvā yathānyāyaṃ rarakṣāvyāhatendriyaḥ //
2.50.d:
ब्राह्मणादींस्तथा वर्णान्स्वेस्वे धर्मे पृथक्पृथक् ।
स्थापयित्वा यथान्यायं ररक्षाव्याहतेन्द्रियः ॥
2.50.m: Having established the varṇas, beginning with the brāhmaṇas, each in their respective dharma according to rule, / he protected them with unsubdued senses.

2.50.s:
prajāśca sarvavarṇeṣu yathāśreṣṭhānuvarttinaḥ /
varṇāścaivānulomyena tadvadartheṣu ca kramāt //
2.50.d:
प्रजाश्च सर्ववर्णेषु यथाश्रेष्ठानुवर्त्तिनः ।
वर्णाश्चैवानुलोम्येन तद्वदर्थेषु च क्रमात् ॥
2.50.m: The subjects across all varṇas followed the most distinguished among them, / and the varṇas followed in natural order and likewise in their pursuits successively.

2.50.s:
na sati sthavire bālaṃ mṛtyurabhayupagacchati /
sarvavarṇeṣu bhūpāle mahīṃ tasminpraśāsati //
2.50.d:
न सति स्थविरे बालं मृत्युरभयुपगच्छति ।
सर्ववर्णेषु भूपाले महीं तस्मिन्प्रशासति ॥
2.50.m: Death did not overtake a child while an elder was alive, / across all the varṇas, while that protector of the earth was ruling the world.

2.50.s:
sphītānyapetabādhāni tadā rāṣṭrāṇi kṛtsnaśaḥ /
teṣvasaṃkhyā janapadāścāturvarṇyajanāvṛtāḥ //
2.50.d:
स्फीतान्यपेतबाधानि तदा राष्ट्राणि कृत्स्नशः ।
तेष्वसंख्या जनपदाश्चातुर्वर्ण्यजनावृताः ॥
2.50.m: The realms then were prosperous in their entirety, free from afflictions; / in them were countless provinces inhabited by people of the four varṇas,

2.50.s:
te cāsaṃkhyāgṛhagrāmaśatopetā vibhāgaśaḥ /
deśāścāvāsabhuyiṣṭā nṛpe tasminpraśāsati //
2.50.d:
ते चासंख्यागृहग्रामशतोपेता विभागशः ।
देशाश्चावासभुयिष्टा नृपे तस्मिन्प्रशासति ॥
2.50.m: and these were divided into countless hundreds of homes and villages, / with territories thickly populated, while that king ruled.

2.50.s:
anāśramī dvijaḥ kaścinna babhūva tadābhuvi /
prajānāṃ sarvavarṇeṣu prāraṃbhāḥ phaladāyinaḥ //
2.50.d:
अनाश्रमी द्विजः कश्चिन्न बभूव तदाभुवि ।
प्रजानां सर्ववर्णेषु प्रारंभाः फलदायिनः ॥
2.50.m: No twice-born on earth at that time was without an āśrama; / the undertakings of the subjects across all varṇas bore fruit.

2.50.s:
svocitānyeva karmāṇi prārabhante ca mānavāḥ /
puruṣārthopapannāni karmāṇi ca tadā nṛṇām //
2.50.d:
स्वोचितान्येव कर्माणि प्रारभन्ते च मानवाः ।
पुरुषार्थोपपन्नानि कर्माणि च तदा नृणाम् ॥
2.50.m: Human beings undertook only the actions proper to themselves, / and the deeds of men at that time were endowed with the ends of human life.

2.50.s:
mahotsavasamudyuktāḥ puragrāmavrajākarāḥ /
anyonyapriyakāmāśca rājabhaktisamanvitāḥ //
2.50.d:
महोत्सवसमुद्युक्ताः पुरग्रामव्रजाकराः ।
अन्योन्यप्रियकामाश्च राजभक्तिसमन्विताः ॥
2.50.m: Cities, villages, cattle pens, and mines were ever eager for great festivities; / people were mutually affectionate and filled with devotion to the king.

2.50.s:
nanindito 'bhiśasto vā daridro vyādhito 'pi vā /
prajāsu kaścillubdho vā kṛpaṇo vāpi nābhavat //
2.50.d:
ननिन्दितो ऽभिशस्तो वा दरिद्रो व्याधितो ऽपि वा ।
प्रजासु कश्चिल्लुब्धो वा कृपणो वापि नाभवत् ॥
2.50.m: None among the subjects was blameworthy, cursed, poor, or diseased, / nor was anyone greedy or miserable.

2.50.s:
janāḥ paraguṇaprītāḥ svasaṃparkābhikāṅkṣiṇāḥ /
guruṣu praṇatā nityaṃ sadvidyāvyasanādṛtāḥ //
2.50.d:
जनाः परगुणप्रीताः स्वसंपर्काभिकाङ्क्षिणाः ।
गुरुषु प्रणता नित्यं सद्विद्याव्यसनादृताः ॥
2.50.m: People were delighted by the virtues of others, desirous of association with good people, / ever bowed before gurus, and devoted to attachment to true learning.

2.50.s:
parāpavādabhītāśca svadāraratayo 'niśam /
nisargātkhalasaṃsargaviratā dharmatatparāḥ //
2.50.d:
परापवादभीताश्च स्वदाररतयो ऽनिशम् ।
निसर्गात्खलसंसर्गविरता धर्मतत्पराः ॥
2.50.m: Fearful of slandering others, ever delighting in their own wives, / by nature turning away from the company of wicked people, intent upon dharma,

2.50.s:
āstikāḥ sarvaśo 'bhūvan prajāstasminpraśāsati /
evaṃ subāhutanye svapratāpārjitāṃ mahīm //
2.50.d:
आस्तिकाः सर्वशो ऽभूवन् प्रजास्तस्मिन्प्रशासति ।
एवं सुबाहुतन्ये स्वप्रतापार्जितां महीम् ॥
2.50.m: the subjects were everywhere orthodox believers while he ruled. / Thus, the son of Subāhu [ruled] the earth acquired by his own valour.

2.50.s:
ṛtavaśca mahābhāga yathākālānuvartinaḥ /
śālibhūyiṣṭhasasyāḍhyā sadaiva sakalā mahī //
2.50.d:
ऋतवश्च महाभाग यथाकालानुवर्तिनः ।
शालिभूयिष्ठसस्याढ्या सदैव सकला मही ॥
2.50.m: The seasons, O fortunate one, followed their proper times; / the entire earth was always rich in crops, predominantly rice,

2.50.s: babhūva nṛpaśārdūle tasmin rājyāni śāsati //
2.50.d: बभूव नृपशार्दूले तस्मिन् राज्यानि शासति ॥
2.50.m: while that tiger among kings was ruling the realms.

2.50.s:
yasyāṣṭādaśamaṇḍalādhipatibhiḥ sevārthamabhyāgataiḥ prakhyātoruparākramairnṛpaśatairmūrddhābhiṣiktaiḥ pṛthak /
saṃviṣṭairmaṇiviṣṭareṣu nitarāmadhyāsyamānāmaraiḥ śakrasyeva virājate divi sabhā ratnaprabhodbhāsitā //
2.50.d:
यस्याष्टादशमण्डलाधिपतिभिः सेवार्थमभ्यागतैः प्रख्यातोरुपराक्रमैर्नृपशतैर्मूर्द्धाभिषिक्तैः पृथक् ।
संविष्टैर्मणिविष्टरेषु नितरामध्यास्यमानामरैः शक्रस्येव विराजते दिवि सभा रत्नप्रभोद्भासिता ॥
2.50.m: His assembly hall—attended on every side by the lords of the eighteen realms who had arrived to pay homage, by hundreds of consecrated kings renowned for their vast valour, seated on jewelled seats—shone illumined with the radiance of gems, like the celestial hall of Śakra in heaven occupied by the immortals.

2.50.s:
saṃketāviṣayāntarābhyupagamāḥ sarve 'pi sopāyanāḥ kṛtvā sainyaniveśanāni paritaḥ puryāḥ pṛthak pārthivāḥ /
draṣṭuṃ kāṅkṣitarājakāḥ satanayāvijñāpayanto muhurdvāsthaireva nareśvarāya suciraṃ vatsyantamantaḥpure //
2.50.d:
संकेताविषयान्तराभ्युपगमाः सर्वे ऽपि सोपायनाः कृत्वा सैन्यनिवेशनानि परितः पुर्याः पृथक् पार्थिवाः ।
द्रष्टुं काङ्क्षितराजकाः सतनयाविज्ञापयन्तो मुहुर्द्वास्थैरेव नरेश्वराय सुचिरं वत्स्यन्तमन्तःपुरे ॥
2.50.m: Having agreed to treaties and other conditions, all kings, bearing tribute, / pitched their camps all around the city separately. / Desiring to see [him], the gathered kings together with their sons repeatedly announced themselves through the door-keepers / to the king who was to dwell for a long time within his inner chambers.

2.50.s:
namannaredramukuṭaśreṇīnāmatigharṣaṇāt /
kiṇīkṛtau virājete caraṇau tasya bhūbhujaḥ //
2.50.d:
नमन्नरेद्रमुकुटश्रेणीनामतिघर्षणात् ।
किणीकृतौ विराजेते चरणौ तस्य भूभुजः ॥
2.50.m: From the excessive friction against the rows of crowns of bowing kings, / the two feet of that ruler of the earth, calloused, shone brightly.

2.50.s:
sevāgatanaredraughavinikīrṇaiḥ samantataḥ /
ratnairbhāti sabhā tasya guhā some ravī yathā //
2.50.d:
सेवागतनरेद्रौघविनिकीर्णैः समन्ततः ।
रत्नैर्भाति सभा तस्य गुहा सोमे रवी यथा ॥
2.50.m: With the jewels scattered all around by the throngs of kings who came to serve him, / his assembly hall shone like a cave [brightened] by the moon and the sun.

2.50.s:
evaṃ sa rājā dharmeṇa bhānuvaṃśaśikhāmaṇiḥ /
ananyaśāsanāmurvīmanvaśāsadarindamaḥ //
2.50.d:
एवं स राजा धर्मेण भानुवंशशिखामणिः ।
अनन्यशासनामुर्वीमन्वशासदरिन्दमः ॥
2.50.m: Thus that king, the crest-jewel of the solar dynasty, / the subduer of enemies, ruled the earth with righteousness, his command brookable by none.

2.50.s:
itthaṃ pālayataḥ pṛthvīṃ sagarasya mahīpateḥ /
na cāpapāta mut putramukhālokanajṛṃbhitā //
2.50.d:
इत्थं पालयतः पृथ्वीं सगरस्य महीपतेः ।
न चापपात मुत् पुत्रमुखालोकनजृंभिता ॥
2.50.m: As King Sagara was protecting the earth in this way, / no joy arose [in him] that is born from gazing upon the face of a son.

2.50.s:
vinā tāṃ duḥkhito 'tyarthaṃ citayāmāsa naikadhā /
aho kaṣṭamaputro 'hamasminvaṃśe dhruvaṃ tu yat //
2.50.d:
विना तां दुःखितो ऽत्यर्थं चितयामास नैकधा ।
अहो कष्टमपुत्रो ऽहमस्मिन्वंशे ध्रुवं तु यत् ॥
2.50.m: Being extremely sorrowful without that, he reflected in many ways: / “Alas, what misery! I am childless in this lineage, where surely

2.50.s:
prayānti nūnamasmākaṃ pitaraḥ piṇḍaviplavam /
nirayādapi satputre saṃjāte pitaraḥ kila //
2.50.d:
प्रयान्ति नूनमस्माकं पितरः पिण्डविप्लवम् ।
निरयादपि सत्पुत्रे संजाते पितरः किल ॥
2.50.m: our ancestors are heading toward the loss of funeral rice-balls! / Even from hell, indeed, when a virtuous son is born, the ancestors,

2.50.s:
prītyā prayānti tadgehaṃ jātakarmakriyotsukāḥ /
mahatā sukṛtenāpi saṃprāptasya divaṃ kila //
2.50.d:
प्रीत्या प्रयान्ति तद्गेहं जातकर्मक्रियोत्सुकाः ।
महता सुकृतेनापि संप्राप्तस्य दिवं किल ॥
2.50.m: eager for the performance of the birth-rites, go with joy to his house. / Even for one who has reached heaven by great merit,

2.50.s:
aputrasyāmarāḥ svarge dvāraṃ noddhāṭayanti hi /
pitā tu lokamubhayoḥ svarlokaṃ tatpitāmahāḥ //
2.50.d:
अपुत्रस्यामराः स्वर्गे द्वारं नोद्धाटयन्ति हि ।
पिता तु लोकमुभयोः स्वर्लोकं तत्पितामहाः ॥
2.50.m: the gods do not open the gate of heaven if he is sonless. / The father indeed [wins] the world of both, while his grandfathers will conquer heaven,

2.50.s:
jeṣyanti kila satputre jāte vaṃśadvaye 'pi ca /
anapatyatayāhaṃ tu putriṇāṃ yā bhavedgatiḥ //
2.50.d:
जेष्यन्ति किल सत्पुत्रे जाते वंशद्वये ऽपि च ।
अनपत्यतयाहं तु पुत्रिणां या भवेद्गतिः ॥
2.50.m: when a virtuous son is born in both lines. / But because of childlessness, the state which belongs to those who have sons

2.50.s:
na tāṃ prāpkyāmi vai nūnaṃ sudurlabhatarā hi sā /
padādaindrātkilābhinnamṛddhaṃ rājyamakhaṇḍitam //
2.50.d:
न तां प्राप्क्यामि वै नूनं सुदुर्लभतरा हि सा ।
पदादैन्द्रात्किलाभिन्नमृद्धं राज्यमखण्डितम् ॥
2.50.m: I shall surely not attain, for that is exceedingly difficult to reach. / This flourishing, undivided kingdom, surely not different from the station of Indra,

2.50.s:
mama yattadapuṇyasya yāti niṣphalatāmiha /
idaṃ matpūrvajaireva siṃhāsanamadhiṣṭhitam //
2.50.d:
मम यत्तदपुण्यस्य याति निष्फलतामिह ।
इदं मत्पूर्वजैरेव सिंहासनमधिष्ठितम् ॥
2.50.m: which belongs to me, an unmeritorious one, goes to fruitlessness here! / This throne, occupied by my own ancestors,

2.50.s:
aputratvena rājyaṃ ca parādhīnatvameṣyati /
tasmādaurvāśramamahaṃ gatvā taṃ munipuṅgavam //
2.50.d:
अपुत्रत्वेन राज्यं च पराधीनत्वमेष्यति ।
तस्मादौर्वाश्रममहं गत्वा तं मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥
2.50.m: and the kingdom will fall under the control of others due to sonlessness. / Therefore, having gone to the hermitage of Aurva, to that bull among sages,

2.50.s:
prasādayiṣye putrārthaṃ bhāryābhyāṃ sahito 'dhunā /
gatvā tasmai tvaputratvaṃ vinivedya mahātmane //
2.50.d:
प्रसादयिष्ये पुत्रार्थं भार्याभ्यां सहितो ऽधुना ।
गत्वा तस्मै त्वपुत्रत्वं विनिवेद्य महात्मने ॥
2.50.m: I shall now propitiate him for the sake of a son, together with my two wives. / Having gone and made known my sonlessness to that great-souled one,

2.50.s:
sa yadvakṣyati tatsarvaṃ kariṣye nātra saṃśayaḥ /
iti sañcintya manasā sagarorājasattamaḥ //
2.50.d:
स यद्वक्ष्यति तत्सर्वं करिष्ये नात्र संशयः ।
इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा सगरोराजसत्तमः ॥
2.50.m: I will do everything that he speaks; there is no doubt about this.” / Reflecting thus in his mind, Sagara, the best of kings,

2.50.s:
ityeṣa kṛtyavidrājangantumaurvāśramaṃ prati /
sa mantripravare rājyaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tato vanam //
2.50.d:
इत्येष कृत्यविद्राजन्गन्तुमौर्वाश्रमं प्रति ।
स मन्त्रिप्रवरे राज्यं प्रतिष्ठाप्य ततो वनम् ॥
2.50.m: this knower of duties, O king, [set out] to go toward the hermitage of Aurva. / Having established the kingdom in the care of his foremost minister, he then [went] to the forest.

2.50.s:
prayayau rathamāruhya bhāryābhyāṃ sahito mudā /
jagāma rathaghoṣeṇa meghanādātiśaṅkibhiḥ //
2.50.d:
प्रययौ रथमारुह्य भार्याभ्यां सहितो मुदा ।
जगाम रथघोषेण मेघनादातिशङ्किभिः ॥
2.50.m: Mounting his chariot together with his two wives, he set forth joyfully. / He proceeded with the rumble of the chariot, while peacocks, suspecting it to be the rumble of clouds,

2.50.s:
stabdhekṣaṇairlakṣyamāṇo mārgopānte śikhaṇḍibhiḥ /
priyābhyāṃ darśayanrājansāraṅgāṃstimitekṣaṇān //
2.50.d:
स्तब्धेक्षणैर्लक्ष्यमाणो मार्गोपान्ते शिखण्डिभिः ।
प्रियाभ्यां दर्शयन्राजन्सारङ्गांस्तिमितेक्षणान् ॥
2.50.m: watched him with motionless eyes by the edge of the road, O king; / showing to his two beloveds the deer with steady eyes,

2.50.s:
kṣamamūrdhvamukhānsadyaḥ palāyanaparānpunaḥ /
vṛkṣānpuṣpaphalopetānvilokya mudito 'bhavat //
2.50.d:
क्षममूर्ध्वमुखान्सद्यः पलायनपरान्पुनः ।
वृक्षान्पुष्पफलोपेतान्विलोक्य मुदितो ऽभवत् ॥
2.50.m: their faces upturned for a moment, and then intent on flight, / and seeing trees laden with flowers and fruits, he became delighted:

2.50.s:
amlānakusumaiḥ svāduphalaiḥ śādvalabhūmikaiḥ /
susnigdhapallavacchāyairabhitaḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ nagaiḥ //
2.50.d:
अम्लानकुसुमैः स्वादुफलैः शाद्वलभूमिकैः ।
सुस्निग्धपल्लवच्छायैरभितः संभृतं नगैः ॥
2.50.m: [the forest] filled on all sides with trees bearing unfading flowers and sweet fruits, / with grassy grounds and having the shade of glossy tender leaves;

2.50.s:
cūtāgrapallavāsvādasnigdhakaṇṭhapikāravaiḥ /
śrotrābhirāmajanakaissaṃghuṣṭaṃ sarvatodiśam //
2.50.d:
चूताग्रपल्लवास्वादस्निग्धकण्ठपिकारवैः ।
श्रोत्राभिरामजनकैस्संघुष्टं सर्वतोदिशम् ॥
2.50.m: resounding in every quarter with the sweet-voiced calls of the cuckoos / whose throats were smoothed by tasting the tips of mango shoots, delighting the ears;

2.50.s:
sarvartukusumopetaṃ bhramadbhramaramaṇḍitam /
prasūnastabakānamraballarīvellitadrumam //
2.50.d:
सर्वर्तुकुसुमोपेतं भ्रमद्भ्रमरमण्डितम् ।
प्रसूनस्तबकानम्रबल्लरीवेल्लितद्रुमम् ॥
2.50.m: endowed with flowers of all seasons, adorned with hovering bees, / its trees entwined with creeping vines bent low with clusters of blossoms;

2.50.s:
kapiyūthasamākrāntava naspatiśatāvṛtam /
unmattaśikhisāraṅgakūjatpakṣigaṇānvitam //
2.50.d:
कपियूथसमाक्रान्तव नस्पतिशतावृतम् ।
उन्मत्तशिखिसारङ्गकूजत्पक्षिगणान्वितम् ॥
2.50.m: filled with hundreds of great trees climbed over by troops of monkeys, / accompanied by flocks of birds singing along with frenzied peacocks and deer;

2.50.s:
gāyadvidyādharavadhūgītikāsumanoharam /
saṃcaratkinnarīdvandvavirājadvanagahvaram //
2.50.d:
गायद्विद्याधरवधूगीतिकासुमनोहरम् ।
संचरत्किन्नरीद्वन्द्वविराजद्वनगह्वरम् ॥
2.50.m: exceedingly charming with the songs of singing Vidyādhara maidens, / its forest caves splendid with moving Kinnara couples;

2.50.s:
haṃsasārasacakrāhvakāraṇḍavaśukādibhiḥ /
susvarairāvṛtopāntaiḥ sarobhiḥ parivāritam //
2.50.d:
हंससारसचक्राह्वकारण्डवशुकादिभिः ।
सुस्वरैरावृतोपान्तैः सरोभिः परिवारितम् ॥
2.50.m: surrounded by lakes whose borders were crowded with sweet-voiced / swans, cranes, cakravākas, kāraṇḍavas, parrots, and others;

2.50.s:
saraḥ svaṃbuja kahlārakumudotpalarāśiṣu /
śanaiḥ parivahanmandamārutāpūrṇadiṅmukham //
2.50.d:
सरः स्वंबुज कह्लारकुमुदोत्पलराशिषु ।
शनैः परिवहन्मन्दमारुतापूर्णदिङ्मुखम् ॥
2.50.m: with the gentle breeze slowly blowing over the masses of lotuses, kahlāras, white lilies, and blue lotuses in the lakes, / filling the directions.

2.50.s:
evaṃvidhaguṇopetamadhigāhya tapovanam /
gacchanrathenātha nṛpaḥ praharṣaṃ paramaṃ yayau //
2.50.d:
एवंविधगुणोपेतमधिगाह्य तपोवनम् ।
गच्छन्रथेनाथ नृपः प्रहर्षं परमं ययौ ॥
2.50.m: Having entered the penance grove endowed with such qualities, / the king, proceeding by chariot, attained the highest delight.

2.50.s:
upaśāntāśayaḥ so 'tha saṃprāpyāśramamaṇḍalam /
bhāryābhyāṃ sahitaḥ śrīmānvāhādavaruroha vai //
2.50.d:
उपशान्ताशयः सो ऽथ संप्राप्याश्रममण्डलम् ।
भार्याभ्यां सहितः श्रीमान्वाहादवरुरोह वै ॥
2.50.m: Then, his mind calmed, having reached the circle of the hermitage, / the glorious one descended from the chariot along with his two wives.

2.50.s:
dhuryānviśrāmayetyuktvā yantāramavanīpatiḥ /
āsasādāśramopāntaṃ maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ //
2.50.d:
धुर्यान्विश्रामयेत्युक्त्वा यन्तारमवनीपतिः ।
आससादाश्रमोपान्तं महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः ॥
2.50.m: Having said to the charioteer, “Rest the draft-animals,” / the lord of the earth approached the vicinity of the hermitage of the purified great sage.

2.50.s:
sa śrutvā muniśiṣyebhyaḥ kṛtanityakriyādaram /
muniṃ draṣṭuṃ vinītātmā praviveśāśramaṃ tadā //
2.50.d:
स श्रुत्वा मुनिशिष्येभ्यः कृतनित्यक्रियादरम् ।
मुनिं द्रष्टुं विनीतात्मा प्रविवेशाश्रमं तदा ॥
2.50.m: Hearing from the sage’s disciples that he had completed his daily rites with reverence, / [the king], modest in demeanor, then entered the hermitage to see the sage.

2.50.s:
munimadhye samāsīnamṛṣivṛndaiḥ samanvitam /
nanāma śirasā rājā bhāryābhyāṃ sahito mudā //
2.50.d:
मुनिमध्ये समासीनमृषिवृन्दैः समन्वितम् ।
ननाम शिरसा राजा भार्याभ्यां सहितो मुदा ॥
2.50.m: The king, along with his two wives, bowed down with his head in joy / to the sage seated in the midst, surrounded by groups of ṛṣis.

2.50.s:
kṛtapraṇāmaṃ nṛpatimṛṣiraurvaḥ pratāpavān /
upaviśeti premṇā vai saha tābhyāṃ samādiśat //
2.50.d:
कृतप्रणामं नृपतिमृषिरौर्वः प्रतापवान् ।
उपविशेति प्रेम्णा वै सह ताभ्यां समादिशत् ॥
2.50.m: To the king who had offered obeisance, the glorious sage Aurva / affectionately commanded, “Be seated,” together with the two of them.

2.50.s:
arghyapādyādibhiḥ samyakpūjayitvā mahāmuniḥ /
ātithyena ca vanyena sabhāryaṃ tamatoṣayat //
2.50.d:
अर्घ्यपाद्यादिभिः सम्यक्पूजयित्वा महामुनिः ।
आतिथ्येन च वन्येन सभार्यं तमतोषयत् ॥
2.50.m: Having honored him properly with guest-water, foot-water, and other offerings, / the great sage gratified him and his wives with forest-born hospitality.

2.50.s:
athātithyopaviśrāntaṃ praṇamyā sīnamagrataḥ /
rājānamabravīdaurvaḥ śanairmṛdvakṣaraṃ vacaḥ //
2.50.d:
अथातिथ्योपविश्रान्तं प्रणम्या सीनमग्रतः ।
राजानमब्रवीदौर्वः शनैर्मृद्वक्षरं वचः ॥
2.50.m: Then, to the king who had rested from the hospitality and sat before him having bowed, / Aurva spoke slowly in gentle words:

2.50.s:
kuśalaṃ nanu te rājye bāhyeṣvābhyantareṣu ca /
apidharmeṇa sakalāḥ prajāstvaṃ parirakṣasi //
2.50.d:
कुशलं ननु ते राज्ये बाह्येष्वाभ्यन्तरेषु च ।
अपिधर्मेण सकलाः प्रजास्त्वं परिरक्षसि ॥
2.50.m: “Is all well with your kingdom, in external and internal matters? / Do you protect all your subjects in accordance with dharma?

2.50.s:
api jetuṃ trivargaṃ tvamupāyaiḥ samyagīhase /
phalanti hi guṇāstubhyaṃ tvayā samyakpracoditāḥ //
2.50.d:
अपि जेतुं त्रिवर्गं त्वमुपायैः सम्यगीहसे ।
फलन्ति हि गुणास्तुभ्यं त्वया सम्यक्प्रचोदिताः ॥
2.50.m: Do you endeavor to master the threefold path of life properly through expedient means? / For virtues properly prompted by you bear fruit for you.

2.50.s:
diṣṭyātvayā jitāḥ sarve ripavo nṛpasattama /
diṣṭyā ca sakalaṃ rājyaṃ tvayā dharmeṇa rakṣyate //
2.50.d:
दिष्ट्यात्वया जिताः सर्वे रिपवो नृपसत्तम ।
दिष्ट्या च सकलं राज्यं त्वया धर्मेण रक्ष्यते ॥
2.50.m: By good fortune all enemies have been conquered by you, O best of kings! / By good fortune the entire kingdom is protected by you with dharma!

2.50.s:
dharma eva sthitiryeṣāṃ teṣāṃ nāstyatraviplavaḥ /
na taṃ rakṣati kiṃ dharmaḥ svayaṃ yenābhirakṣitaḥ //
2.50.d:
धर्म एव स्थितिर्येषां तेषां नास्त्यत्रविप्लवः ।
न तं रक्षति किं धर्मः स्वयं येनाभिरक्षितः ॥
2.50.m: Those whose foundation is dharma suffer no ruin here. / Does not dharma protect him by whom it has itself been preserved?

2.50.s:
pūrvamevāhamaśrauṣaṃ vijitya sakalāṃ mahīm /
sabalonagarīṃ prāptaḥ kṛtadāro bhavāniti //
2.50.d:
पूर्वमेवाहमश्रौषं विजित्य सकलां महीम् ।
सबलोनगरीं प्राप्तः कृतदारो भवानिति ॥
2.50.m: Earlier indeed I heard that, having conquered the entire earth, / you arrived at the city with your army and took wives.

2.50.s:
rājñāṃ tu pravaro dharmo yatprajāparipālanam /
bhavanti sukhino nūnaṃ tenaiveha paratra ca //
2.50.d:
राज्ञां तु प्रवरो धर्मो यत्प्रजापरिपालनम् ।
भवन्ति सुखिनो नूनं तेनैवेह परत्र च ॥
2.50.m: The foremost duty of kings is the protection of subjects; / surely by that alone they become happy in this world and the next.

2.50.s:
sa bhavānrājya bharaṇaṃ parityajya madantikam /
bhāryābhyāṃ sahito rājansamāyāto 'si me vada //
2.50.d:
स भवान्राज्य भरणं परित्यज्य मदन्तिकम् ।
भार्याभ्यां सहितो राजन्समायातो ऽसि मे वद ॥
2.50.m: Relinquishing the governance of the kingdom, you / have come to my presence with your two wives, O king; tell me [the reason].”

2.50.s:
jaiminiruvāca
evamuktastu muninā sagaro rājasattamaḥ /
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā prāha taṃ madhuraṃ vacaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde sagarasyaurvāśramagamanaṃ nāma pañcaśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 50//
2.50.d:
जैमिनिरुवाच
एवमुक्तस्तु मुनिना सगरो राजसत्तमः ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा प्राह तं मधुरं वचः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे सगरस्यौर्वाश्रमगमनं नाम पञ्चशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 50॥
2.50.m:
Jaimini said: / Being spoken to thus by the sage, Sagara, the best of kings, / made an añjali fold with his hands and spoke these sweet words to him.

Thus ends the fiftieth chapter, named ‘The Going of Sagara to the Hermitage of Aurva’, in the third Upoddhātapāda in the middle part of the glorious Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa, proclaimed by Vāyu. // 50

2.51.s:
sagara uvāca
kuśalaṃ mama sarvatra maharṣe nātra saṃśayaḥ /
yasya me tvamanudhyātā śamaṃ bhārgavasattamaḥ //
2.51.d:
सगर उवाच
कुशलं मम सर्वत्र महर्षे नात्र संशयः ।
यस्य मे त्वमनुध्याता शमं भार्गवसत्तमः ॥
2.51.m: Sagara said: / “All is well with me everywhere, O great sage; there is no doubt of this, / since you, the best of the Bhārgavas, wish for my peace.

2.51.s:
yastathā śikṣitaḥ pūrvamastre śastre ca sāṃpratam /
so 'haṃ kathamaśaktaḥ syāṃ sakalārivinigrahe //
2.51.d:
यस्तथा शिक्षितः पूर्वमस्त्रे शस्त्रे च सांप्रतम् ।
सो ऽहं कथमशक्तः स्यां सकलारिविनिग्रहे ॥
2.51.m: Having been instructed in that manner formerly in missiles and now in weapons, / how could I be powerless in suppressing all enemies?

2.51.s:
tvaṃ me guruḥ suhṛddaivaṃ bandhurmitraṃ ca kevalam /
na hyanyamabhijānāmi tvāmṛte pitaraṃ ca me //
2.51.d:
त्वं मे गुरुः सुहृद्दैवं बन्धुर्मित्रं च केवलम् ।
न ह्यन्यमभिजानामि त्वामृते पितरं च मे ॥
2.51.m: You alone are my guru, well-wisher, deity, kinsman, and friend; / indeed, I know of no other father than you.

2.51.s:
tvayopadiṣṭenāstreṇa sakalā bhūbhṛto mayā /
vijitā yadanusmṛtyā śaktiḥ sā tapasastava //
2.51.d:
त्वयोपदिष्टेनास्त्रेण सकला भूभृतो मया ।
विजिता यदनुस्मृत्या शक्तिः सा तपसस्तव ॥
2.51.m: With the missile taught by you, all kings were conquered by me; / remembering it, that [victory] is the power of your ascetic heat.

2.51.s:
tapasā tvaṃ jagatsarvaṃ punāsi paripāsi ca /
sraṣṭuṃ saṃharttumapi ca śaknoṣyeva na saṃśayaḥ //
2.51.d:
तपसा त्वं जगत्सर्वं पुनासि परिपासि च ।
स्रष्टुं संहर्त्तुमपि च शक्नोष्येव न संशयः ॥
2.51.m: Through ascetic heat you purify and protect the entire world; / you are even able to create and destroy it—there is no doubt.

2.51.s:
mahānananyasāmānyaprabhāvastapasaśca te /
iha tasyaikadeśo 'pi dṛśyate vismayapradaḥ //
2.51.d:
महाननन्यसामान्यप्रभावस्तपसश्च ते ।
इह तस्यैकदेशो ऽपि दृश्यते विस्मयप्रदः ॥
2.51.m: Great and unequalled is the power of your ascetic heat; / even a single part of it seen here evokes wonder.

2.51.s:
paśyasiṃhāsane bālyādupetya mṛgapotakaḥ /
pibatyaṃbhaḥ śanairbrahmanniḥśaṅkaṃ te tapovane //
2.51.d:
पश्यसिंहासने बाल्यादुपेत्य मृगपोतकः ।
पिबत्यंभः शनैर्ब्रह्मन्निःशङ्कं ते तपोवने ॥
2.51.m: Look: in childish innocence a fawn approaches the lion's seat / and slowly drinks water, O Brahmin, without fear in your hermitage.

2.51.s:
dhayatyatrātivisraṃbhāt kṛśāpi hariṇī stanam /
karoti mṛgaśṛṅgāgre gaṇḍakaṇḍūyanaṃ ruruḥ //
2.51.d:
धयत्यत्रातिविस्रंभात् कृशापि हरिणी स्तनम् ।
करोति मृगशृङ्गाग्रे गण्डकण्डूयनं रुरुः ॥
2.51.m: Here, out of utter trust, even an emaciated doe suckles at the breast [of another]; / a stag scratches its cheek against the tip of a deer's horn.

2.51.s:
navaprasūtāṃ hariṇīṃ hatvā vṛttyai vanāntare /
vyāghrī tvattapasāvāse saiva puṣṇāti tacchiśūn //
2.51.d:
नवप्रसूतां हरिणीं हत्वा वृत्त्यै वनान्तरे ।
व्याघ्री त्वत्तपसावासे सैव पुष्णाति तच्छिशून् ॥
2.51.m: A tigress that killed a newly-calved doe for food in another forest / nourishes the very same fawns in the dwelling of your ascetic heat.

2.51.s:
gajaṃ drutamanudrutya siṃho yasmādidaṃ vanam /
praviṣṭo 'nusarantau tvadbhayādekatra tiṣṭhataḥ //
2.51.d:
गजं द्रुतमनुद्रुत्य सिंहो यस्मादिदं वनम् ।
प्रविष्टो ऽनुसरन्तौ त्वद्भयादेकत्र तिष्ठतः ॥
2.51.m: Because a lion entered this forest chasing swiftly after an elephant, / the two of them, though pursuing, stay together in one place out of fear of you.

2.51.s:
nakulastvāśumārjāramayūraśaśapannagāḥ /
vṛkasūkaraśārdūlaśarabharkṣaplavaṅgamāḥ //
2.51.d:
नकुलस्त्वाशुमार्जारमयूरशशपन्नगाः ।
वृकसूकरशार्दूलशरभर्क्षप्लवङ्गमाः ॥
2.51.m: Mongoose, swift cat, peacock, hare, and serpent; / wolf, boar, tiger, śarabha, bear, and monkey;

2.51.s:
sṛgālā gavayāgāvo hariṇā mahiṣāstathā /
vane 'tra sahajaṃ vairaṃ hitvā maitrīmupāgatāḥ //
2.51.d:
सृगाला गवयागावो हरिणा महिषास्तथा ।
वने ऽत्र सहजं वैरं हित्वा मैत्रीमुपागताः ॥
2.51.m: Jackals, gayals, cows, deer, and likewise buffaloes— / abandoning their natural enmity in this forest, have attained friendship.

2.51.s:
evaṃvidhā tapaḥśaktirlokavismayadāyinī /
na kvāpi dṛśyate brahmaṃstvāmṛte bhuvi durlabhā //
2.51.d:
एवंविधा तपःशक्तिर्लोकविस्मयदायिनी ।
न क्वापि दृश्यते ब्रह्मंस्त्वामृते भुवि दुर्लभा ॥
2.51.m: Such power of ascetic heat, bestowing wonder upon the world / and rare on earth, is seen nowhere, O Brahmin, except in you.

2.51.s:
ahaṃ tu tvatprasādena vijitya vasudhāmi mām /
ripubhiḥ saha viprarṣe svarājyaṃ samupāgataḥ //
2.51.d:
अहं तु त्वत्प्रसादेन विजित्य वसुधामि माम् ।
रिपुभिः सह विप्रर्षे स्वराज्यं समुपागतः ॥
2.51.m: Having conquered this earth together with its enemies by your grace, / O Brahmin sage, I have returned to my own kingdom.

2.51.s:
vaśyāmātyastrivarge 'pi yathāyogyakṛtādaraḥ /
tvayopadiṣṭamārgeṇa samyagrājyamapālayam //
2.51.d:
वश्यामात्यस्त्रिवर्गे ऽपि यथायोग्यकृतादरः ।
त्वयोपदिष्टमार्गेण सम्यग्राज्यमपालयम् ॥
2.51.m: With ministers obedient and due regard paid appropriately to the three aims of life, / I properly protected the realm in the manner instructed by you.

2.51.s:
evaṃ pravarttamānasya mama rājye 'vatiṣṭhataḥ /
bhavaddidṛkṣā saṃjātā sāpekṣā bhṛgupuṅgava //
2.51.d:
एवं प्रवर्त्तमानस्य मम राज्ये ऽवतिष्ठतः ।
भवद्दिदृक्षा संजाता सापेक्षा भृगुपुङ्गव ॥
2.51.m: As I remained thus acting within the kingdom, / a desire arose, full of longing, to see you, O best of the Bhṛgus.

2.51.s:
kiṃ tvadya mayi paryāptamanapatyatayaiva me /
pitṛpiṇḍapradānena saha saṃrakṣaṇaṃ bhuvaḥ //
2.51.d:
किं त्वद्य मयि पर्याप्तमनपत्यतयैव मे ।
पितृपिण्डप्रदानेन सह संरक्षणं भुवः ॥
2.51.m: Yet today, on account of my childlessness alone, / the protection of the earth together with the offering of balls of rice to the ancestors seems insufficient to me.

2.51.s:
tadidaṃ duḥśamatyarthamanivāryaṃ manogatam /
nānayo 'paharttāṃ lokaṃ'smin mameti tvāmupāgataḥ //
2.51.d:
तदिदं दुःशमत्यर्थमनिवार्यं मनोगतम् ।
नानयो ऽपहर्त्तां लोकंऽस्मिन् ममेति त्वामुपागतः ॥
2.51.m: This deep, irresistible sorrow in my heart is hard to calm; / 'There is no remover of it in this world for me'—thinking thus, I have come to you."

2.51.s:
ityuktaḥ sagareṇātha sthitvā so 'tarmanāḥ kṣaṇam /
uvāca bhagavānaurvaḥ sanideśamidaṃ vacaḥ //
2.51.d:
इत्युक्तः सगरेणाथ स्थित्वा सो ऽतर्मनाः क्षणम् ।
उवाच भगवानौर्वः सनिदेशमिदं वचः ॥
2.51.m: Thus addressed by Sagara, the venerable Aurva paused a moment, reflective in mind, / and then spoke these words containing an instruction:

2.51.s:
niyamya saha bhāryābhyāṃ kiñcitkālamihāvasa /
avāpsyati tato 'bhīṣṭaṃ bhavānnātra vicāramā //
2.51.d:
नियम्य सह भार्याभ्यां किञ्चित्कालमिहावस ।
अवाप्स्यति ततो ऽभीष्टं भवान्नात्र विचारमा ॥
2.51.m: "Practising self-restraint together with your two wives, dwell here for some time; / then you will obtain your desire—let there be no doubt about this."

2.51.s:
sa ca tatrāvasatprītastacchuśrūṣāparāyamaḥ /
patnībhyāṃ saha dharmātmā bhaktiyuktaściraṃ tadā //
2.51.d:
स च तत्रावसत्प्रीतस्तच्छुश्रूषापरायमः ।
पत्नीभ्यां सह धर्मात्मा भक्तियुक्तश्चिरं तदा ॥
2.51.m: And he dwelled there joyfully, devoted to his service, / together with his two wives, righteous and full of devotion for a long time.

2.51.s:
rājapatnyau ca te tasya sarvakālamatandrite /
muneratanutāṃ prītiṃ vinayācārabhaktibhiḥ //
2.51.d:
राजपत्न्यौ च ते तस्य सर्वकालमतन्द्रिते ।
मुनेरतनुतां प्रीतिं विनयाचारभक्तिभिः ॥
2.51.m: The two royal wives, ever unwearied, / extended delight to the sage through modesty, good conduct, and devotion.

2.51.s:
bhaktyā śuśrūṣayā caiva tayostuṣṭo mahāmuniḥ /
rājapatnyau samāhūya idaṃ vacanama bravīt //
2.51.d:
भक्त्या शुश्रूषया चैव तयोस्तुष्टो महामुनिः ।
राजपत्न्यौ समाहूय इदं वचनम ब्रवीत् ॥
2.51.m: Pleased by their devotion and service, the great sage / summoned the two royal wives and spoke these words:

2.51.s:
bhavatyau varamasmatto vriyatāṃ kāmamīpsitam /
dāsyāmi taṃ na saṃdeho yadyapi syātsudurllabham //
2.51.d:
भवत्यौ वरमस्मत्तो व्रियतां काममीप्सितम् ।
दास्यामि तं न संदेहो यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुर्ल्लभम् ॥
2.51.m: "May you two choose a desired boon from me at your wish; / I will grant it, there is no doubt, even if it should be very difficult to obtain."

2.51.s:
tataḥ praṇamyaśirasā te 'pyubhe taṃ mahāmunim /
ūcaturbhagavānputrānkāmayāveti sādaram //
2.51.d:
ततः प्रणम्यशिरसा ते ऽप्युभे तं महामुनिम् ।
ऊचतुर्भगवान्पुत्रान्कामयावेति सादरम् ॥
2.51.m: Then, bowing with their heads to that great sage, / both respectfully said: "Lord, we desire sons."

2.51.s:
tataste bhagavānāha bhavatībhyāṃ mayā punaḥ /
rājñaścapriyakāmena varo datto 'yamīpsitaḥ //
2.51.d:
ततस्ते भगवानाह भवतीभ्यां मया पुनः ।
राज्ञश्चप्रियकामेन वरो दत्तो ऽयमीप्सितः ॥
2.51.m: Then the venerable one said to them: "By me, desiring what is pleasing to you / and to the king, this sought-after boon is granted.

2.51.s:
putravatyau mahābhāge bhavatyau matprasādataḥ /
bhavetāṃ dhruvamanyacca śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama //
2.51.d:
पुत्रवत्यौ महाभागे भवत्यौ मत्प्रसादतः ।
भवेतां ध्रुवमन्यच्च श्रूयतां वचनं मम ॥
2.51.m: O fortunate women, by my grace you two shall surely have sons; / and hear another word of mine:

2.51.s:
putro bhaviṣyatyekasyāmekaḥ so 'natidhārmikaḥ /
tathāpi tasya kalpāntaṃ saṃbhūtiśca bhaviṣyati //
2.51.d:
पुत्रो भविष्यत्येकस्यामेकः सो ऽनतिधार्मिकः ।
तथापि तस्य कल्पान्तं संभूतिश्च भविष्यति ॥
2.51.m: To one there will be a single son, not exceedingly righteous, / yet his lineage will continue until the end of the kalpa.

2.51.s:
ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇāmaparasyāṃ ca jāyate /
akṛtārthāśca te sarve vinaṅkṣyantyacirādiva //
2.51.d:
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणामपरस्यां च जायते ।
अकृतार्थाश्च ते सर्वे विनङ्क्ष्यन्त्यचिरादिव ॥
2.51.m: And sixty thousand sons shall be born to the other; / they will all perish before long, without fulfilling their aims.

2.51.s:
evaṃvidhaguṇepeto varau dattau mayā yuvām /
abhīpsitaṃ tu yadyasyāḥ svecchayā tatprakīrtyatām //
2.51.d:
एवंविधगुणेपेतो वरौ दत्तौ मया युवाम् ।
अभीप्सितं तु यद्यस्याः स्वेच्छया तत्प्रकीर्त्यताम् ॥
2.51.m: Endowed with such qualities, two boons have been granted by me to you two; / whatever is desired by either, let that be declared according to your own wish."

2.51.s:
evamukte tu muninā vaidarbhyānvayavarddhanam /
varayāmāsa tanayaṃ putrānanyāstathā parā //
2.51.d:
एवमुक्ते तु मुनिना वैदर्भ्यान्वयवर्द्धनम् ।
वरयामास तनयं पुत्रानन्यास्तथा परा ॥
2.51.m: When this was spoken by the sage, the Vidarbha princess chose the single son / who would continue the lineage, and the other chose the [many] sons.

2.51.s:
iti dattvā varaṃ rājñe sagarāya mahāmuniḥ /
sabhāryāmanumānyainaṃ visasarja purīṃ prati //
2.51.d:
इति दत्त्वा वरं राज्ञे सगराय महामुनिः ।
सभार्यामनुमान्यैनं विससर्ज पुरीं प्रति ॥
2.51.m: Having thus granted the boon to King Sagara, the great sage / gave him and his wives permission and sent them back to the city.

2.51.s:
muninā samanujñātaḥ kṛta kṛtyo mahīpatiḥ /
rathamāruhya vegena sapriyaḥ prayayau purīm //
2.51.d:
मुनिना समनुज्ञातः कृत कृत्यो महीपतिः ।
रथमारुह्य वेगेन सप्रियः प्रययौ पुरीम् ॥
2.51.m: Permitted by the sage, having achieved his purpose, the lord of the earth / mounted his chariot and swiftly returned to the city with his beloved wives.

2.51.s:
sa praviśya purīṃ ramyāṃ tdṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛtām /
ānanditaḥ paurajanai reme paramayā mudā //
2.51.d:
स प्रविश्य पुरीं रम्यां त्दृष्टपुष्टजनावृताम् ।
आनन्दितः पौरजनै रेमे परमया मुदा ॥
2.51.m: Entering the lovely city filled with prosperous and well-fed people, / he, welcomed joyfully by the citizens, delighted with supreme happiness.

2.51.s:
etasminneva kāle tu rājapatnyāvubhe nṛpa /
rājñe prāvocatāṃ garbhaṃ mudā paramayā yute //
2.51.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु राजपत्न्यावुभे नृप ।
राज्ञे प्रावोचतां गर्भं मुदा परमया युते ॥
2.51.m: At that very time, O king, both royal wives, / filled with supreme joy, reported pregnancy to the king.

2.51.s:
vavṛdhe ca tayorgarbhaḥ śuklapakṣe yathoḍurāṭ /
saha saṃtoṣasaṃpattyā pitroḥ paurajanasya ca //
2.51.d:
ववृधे च तयोर्गर्भः शुक्लपक्षे यथोडुराट् ।
सह संतोषसंपत्त्या पित्रोः पौरजनस्य च ॥
2.51.m: And the embryo in the two grew like the moon in the bright fortnight, / along with the abundance of delight of both parents and of the citizens.

2.51.s:
saṃpūrṇe tu tataḥ kāle muhūrte keśinīśubhe /
asūyatāgnigarbhābhaṃ kumāramamitadyutim //
2.51.d:
संपूर्णे तु ततः काले मुहूर्ते केशिनीशुभे ।
असूयताग्निगर्भाभं कुमारममितद्युतिम् ॥
2.51.m: Then, when the time was complete, at an auspicious moment Keśinī / gave birth to an immensely radiant prince, resembling the womb of fire.

2.51.s:
jātakarmādikaṃ tasya kṛtvā caiva yathāvidhi /
asamañcasa ityeva nāma tasyā karonnṛpaḥ //
2.51.d:
जातकर्मादिकं तस्य कृत्वा चैव यथाविधि ।
असमञ्चस इत्येव नाम तस्या करोन्नृपः ॥
2.51.m: Having duly performed the birth rites and other ceremonies for him, / the king gave him the name Asamañjasa.

2.51.s:
sumatiścāpi tatkāle garbhālābamasūyata /
saṃprasūtaṃ tu taṃ tyaktaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājākaronmanaḥ //
2.51.d:
सुमतिश्चापि तत्काले गर्भालाबमसूयत ।
संप्रसूतं तु तं त्यक्तं दृष्ट्वा राजाकरोन्मनः ॥
2.51.m: Sumati also, at that time, gave birth to a womb-gourd; / seeing what was born, the king made up his mind to discard it.

2.51.s:
tajjñātvā bhagavānaurvastatrāgacchadyadṛcchayā /
samyak saṃbhāvito rājñā tamuvāca tvarānvitaḥ //
2.51.d:
तज्ज्ञात्वा भगवानौर्वस्तत्रागच्छद्यदृच्छया ।
सम्यक् संभावितो राज्ञा तमुवाच त्वरान्वितः ॥
2.51.m: Knowing that, the venerable Aurva arrived there as if by chance; / duly honoured by the king, he said to him in haste:

2.51.s:
garbhālāburayaṃ rājanna tyaktuṃ bhavatārhati /
putrāṇāṃ ṣaṣṭisāhasrabījabhūto yatastava //
2.51.d:
गर्भालाबुरयं राजन्न त्यक्तुं भवतार्हति ।
पुत्राणां षष्टिसाहस्रबीजभूतो यतस्तव ॥
2.51.m: "O king, you ought not to abandon this womb-gourd, / because it is the seed of your sixty thousand sons.

2.51.s:
tasmāttatsakalīkṛtya ghṛtakuṃbheṣu yatnataḥ /
niḥkṣipya sapidhāneṣu rakṣaṇīyaṃ pṛthakpṛthak //
2.51.d:
तस्मात्तत्सकलीकृत्य घृतकुंभेषु यत्नतः ।
निःक्षिप्य सपिधानेषु रक्षणीयं पृथक्पृथक् ॥
2.51.m: Therefore, having divided it into parts, placing them carefully / into jars of clarified butter with lids, each should be preserved separately.

2.51.s:
samyagevaṃ kṛte rājanbhavato matprasādataḥ /
yathoktasaṃkhyā patrāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ //
2.51.d:
सम्यगेवं कृते राजन्भवतो मत्प्रसादतः ।
यथोक्तसंख्या पत्राणां भविष्यति न संशयः ॥
2.51.m: When this is done properly, O king, by my grace / the stated number of sons will come to be—there is no doubt.

2.51.s:
kāle pūrṇe tataḥ kumbhānbhittvā niryānti te pṛthak /
evaṃ te ṣaṣṭisāhasraṃ putrāṇāṃ jāyate nṛpa //
2.51.d:
काले पूर्णे ततः कुम्भान्भित्त्वा निर्यान्ति ते पृथक् ।
एवं ते षष्टिसाहस्रं पुत्राणां जायते नृप ॥
2.51.m: Then, when the time is complete, having broken the jars they will emerge separately; / thus, O king, sixty thousand sons will be born to you."

2.51.s:
ityuktvā bhagavānaurvastatraivāntaradhādvibhuḥ /
rājā ca tattathā cakre yathaurveṇa samīritam //
2.51.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवानौर्वस्तत्रैवान्तरधाद्विभुः ।
राजा च तत्तथा चक्रे यथौर्वेण समीरितम् ॥
2.51.m: Having spoken thus, the venerable lord Aurva vanished right there; / and the king did precisely as had been stated by Aurva.

2.51.s:
tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe ghṛtakuṃbhātkrameṇa te /
bhittvābhittvā punarjajñuḥ sahasaivānuvāsaram //
2.51.d:
ततः संवत्सरे पूर्णे घृतकुंभात्क्रमेण ते ।
भित्त्वाभित्त्वा पुनर्जज्ञुः सहसैवानुवासरम् ॥
2.51.m: Then, when a full year had passed, from the jars of clarified butter, in due course, / having burst them, they were born day after day in rapid succession.

2.51.s:
evaṃ krameṇa saṃjātāstanayāste mahīpate /
vavṛdhuḥ saṃghaśo rājanṣaṣṭisāhasrasaṃkhyāyā //
2.51.d:
एवं क्रमेण संजातास्तनयास्ते महीपते ।
ववृधुः संघशो राजन्षष्टिसाहस्रसंख्याया ॥
2.51.m: Thus, in due course, those sons of the earth's lord were born; / they grew up in crowds, O king, to the number of sixty thousand.

2.51.s:
apṛthagdharmacaraṇā mahābalaparākramāḥ /
babhūvuste durādharṣāḥ krūrātmāno viśeṣataḥ //
2.51.d:
अपृथग्धर्मचरणा महाबलपराक्रमाः ।
बभूवुस्ते दुराधर्षाः क्रूरात्मानो विशेषतः ॥
2.51.m: Not practicing separate duties, possessing great strength and prowess, / they became unassailable and particularly cruel by nature.

2.51.s:
sa nātiprītimāṃsteṣu rājā matimatāṃ varaḥ /
keśinītanayaṃ tvekaṃ bahumāna sutaṃ priyam //
2.51.d:
स नातिप्रीतिमांस्तेषु राजा मतिमतां वरः ।
केशिनीतनयं त्वेकं बहुमान सुतं प्रियम् ॥
2.51.m: The king, the best among the wise, had no great fondness for them; / but he held in high esteem the one beloved son, the child of Keśinī.

2.51.s:
vivāhaṃ vidhivattasmai kārayāmāsa pārthivaḥ /
sacāpyānandayāmāsa svaguṇaiḥ suhṛdo 'khilān //
2.51.d:
विवाहं विधिवत्तस्मै कारयामास पार्थिवः ।
सचाप्यानन्दयामास स्वगुणैः सुहृदो ऽखिलान् ॥
2.51.m: The king had a marriage duly performed for him; / and he too delighted all his friends with his good qualities.

2.51.s:
evaṃ pravarta mānasya keśinītanayasya tu /
ajāyata sutaḥ śrīmānaṃśumāniti viśrutaḥ //
2.51.d:
एवं प्रवर्त मानस्य केशिनीतनयस्य तु ।
अजायत सुतः श्रीमानंशुमानिति विश्रुतः ॥
2.51.m: To that son of Keśinī, who conducted himself thus, / was born a glorious son renowned as Aṃśumat.

2.51.s:
sa bālya eva matimānudāraiḥ svaguṇairbhṛśam /
prīṇayāmāsa sutdṛdaḥ svapitāmahameva ca //
2.51.d:
स बाल्य एव मतिमानुदारैः स्वगुणैर्भृशम् ।
प्रीणयामास सुत्दृदः स्वपितामहमेव च ॥
2.51.m: Even in childhood, that wise boy greatly delighted his friends / and his own grandfather with his noble qualities.

2.51.s:
etasminnantare rājñastasya putro 'samañjasaḥ /
āviṣṭo naṣṭaceṣṭo 'bhūtsa piśācena kena cit //
2.51.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राज्ञस्तस्य पुत्रो ऽसमञ्जसः ।
आविष्टो नष्टचेष्टो ऽभूत्स पिशाचेन केन चित् ॥
2.51.m: In the meantime, that king's son, Asamañjasa, / became possessed by a certain piśāca and lost his self-control.

2.51.s:
sa tu kaścidabhūdvaiśyaḥ pūrvajanmani dharmavit /
kasyācidviṣaye rājñaḥ prabhūtadhanadhānyavān //
2.51.d:
स तु कश्चिदभूद्वैश्यः पूर्वजन्मनि धर्मवित् ।
कस्याचिद्विषये राज्ञः प्रभूतधनधान्यवान् ॥
2.51.m: In a previous birth, he had been a certain vaiśya who knew righteousness, / possessed of abundant wealth and grain, living in the territory of some king.

2.51.s:
sa kadācidaraṇyeṣu vicarannidhimuttamam /
dṛṣṭvā grahītumārebhe vaṇiglobhavariplutaḥ //
2.51.d:
स कदाचिदरण्येषु विचरन्निधिमुत्तमम् ।
दृष्ट्वा ग्रहीतुमारेभे वणिग्लोभवरिप्लुतः ॥
2.51.m: Once, wandering in the forests, he saw an excellent treasure / and, overcome with greed, that merchant began to take it.

2.51.s:
tatastadrakṣako 'bhyetya piśācaḥ prāha taṃ tadā /
kṣudhito 'haṃ cirādasminnivasannidhipālakaḥ //
2.51.d:
ततस्तद्रक्षको ऽभ्येत्य पिशाचः प्राह तं तदा ।
क्षुधितो ऽहं चिरादस्मिन्निवसन्निधिपालकः ॥
2.51.m: Then its guardian, a piśāca, approached and said to him at that time: / 'I am hungry, dwelling here as the guardian of this treasure for a long time.

2.51.s:
tasmāttatparihārāya mama dattvā gavāmiṣam /
kāmataḥ pratigṛhṇīṣva nidhimenaṃ mamājñayā //
2.51.d:
तस्मात्तत्परिहाराय मम दत्त्वा गवामिषम् ।
कामतः प्रतिगृह्णीष्व निधिमेनं ममाज्ञया ॥
2.51.m: Therefore, to dispel that [hunger], give me beef, / and freely take this treasure by my command.'

2.51.s:
satasmai tatpariśrutya dāsyāmīti gavāmiṣam /
ādatta ca nidhiṃ taṃ tu piśācenānumoditaḥ //
2.51.d:
सतस्मै तत्परिश्रुत्य दास्यामीति गवामिषम् ।
आदत्त च निधिं तं तु पिशाचेनानुमोदितः ॥
2.51.m: Having promised him, 'I will give beef,' / he took that treasure, permitted by the piśāca.

2.51.s:
na prādācca tato mauḍhyāttasmai yattatpratiśrutam /
pratiśrutāpradānottharoṣaṃ na śraddadhe nṛpa //
2.51.d:
न प्रादाच्च ततो मौढ्यात्तस्मै यत्तत्प्रतिश्रुतम् ।
प्रतिश्रुताप्रदानोत्थरोषं न श्रद्दधे नृप ॥
2.51.m: Then, out of foolishness, he did not give him what he had promised; / he did not heed the wrath that arose from not giving what was promised, O king.

2.51.s:
tamevaṃ suciraṃ kālaṃ pratīkṣyāśanakāṅkṣayā /
apanītadhanaḥ so 'pi mamāra vyathitaḥ kṣudhā //
2.51.d:
तमेवं सुचिरं कालं प्रतीक्ष्याशनकाङ्क्षया ।
अपनीतधनः सो ऽपि ममार व्यथितः क्षुधा ॥
2.51.m: Having waited for him thus for a very long time in desire for food, / deprived of his treasure, [the piśāca] too died, tormented by hunger.

2.51.s:
vaiśyo 'pi bālo maraṇaṃ saṃprāpya sagarasya tu /
babhūva kāle keśinyāṃ tanayo 'nvayavarddhanaḥ //
2.51.d:
वैश्यो ऽपि बालो मरणं संप्राप्य सगरस्य तु ।
बभूव काले केशिन्यां तनयो ऽन्वयवर्द्धनः ॥
2.51.m: The vaiśya boy also died, / and in time became the son of Sagara by Keśinī, increaser of the lineage.

2.51.s:
aśarīraḥ piśāce 'pi pūrvavairamanusmaran /
vāyubhūto 'viśaddehaṃ rājaputrasya bhūpate //
2.51.d:
अशरीरः पिशाचे ऽपि पूर्ववैरमनुस्मरन् ।
वायुभूतो ऽविशद्देहं राजपुत्रस्य भूपते ॥
2.51.m: Even though bodiless, the piśāca, remembering the ancient enmity, / entered the body of the prince as wind, O ruler of the earth.

2.51.s:
tenāviṣṭastataḥ so 'pi krūracitto 'bhavattadā /
mativibhraṃśamāsādya muhustena balātkṛtaḥ //
2.51.d:
तेनाविष्टस्ततः सो ऽपि क्रूरचित्तो ऽभवत्तदा ।
मतिविभ्रंशमासाद्य मुहुस्तेन बलात्कृतः ॥
2.51.m: Possessed by him, he then became cruel-minded; / falling into delusion of mind, he was constantly overpowered by him.

2.51.s:
asamañjasatvaṃ nagare cakre so 'pi nṛśaṃsavat /
bālāṃśca yūnaḥ sthavirānyoṣitaśca sadā khalaḥ //
2.51.d:
असमञ्जसत्वं नगरे चक्रे सो ऽपि नृशंसवत् ।
बालांश्च यूनः स्थविरान्योषितश्च सदा खलः ॥
2.51.m: He caused impropriety in the city like a villain; / the wicked one constantly [seized] boys, young men, old men, and women,

2.51.s:
hatvāhatvā pracikṣepa sarayvāmatinirdayaḥ /
tataḥ paurajanāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā tasya kadaryatām //
2.51.d:
हत्वाहत्वा प्रचिक्षेप सरय्वामतिनिर्दयः ।
ततः पौरजनाः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा तस्य कदर्यताम् ॥
2.51.m: and repeatedly striking them, he ruthlessly hurled them into the Sarayū. / Then all the citizens, having seen his vile conduct,

2.51.s:
bahuśo nikṛtāstena gatvā rājñe vyajijñāpan /
rājā ca tadupaśrutya tamāhūya prayatnataḥ //
2.51.d:
बहुशो निकृतास्तेन गत्वा राज्ञे व्यजिज्ञापन् ।
राजा च तदुपश्रुत्य तमाहूय प्रयत्नतः ॥
2.51.m: and having been mistreated by him many times, went and reported [it] to the king. / And the king, having heard of that, summoned him with diligence

2.51.s:
vārayāmāsa bahudhā duḥkhena mahatānvitaḥ /
bahuśaḥ pratiṣiddho 'pi pitrā tena mahātmanā //
2.51.d:
वारयामास बहुधा दुःखेन महतान्वितः ।
बहुशः प्रतिषिद्धो ऽपि पित्रा तेन महात्मना ॥
2.51.m: and restrained him in many ways, overcome with great sorrow. / Although repeatedly forbidden by that high-souled father,

2.51.s:
jale tapte ca saṃtaptāḥ saṃbabhūvuryathā yavāḥ /
nāśakattaṃ yadā pāpādvinivarttayituṃ nṛpaḥ //
2.51.d:
जले तप्ते च संतप्ताः संबभूवुर्यथा यवाः ।
नाशकत्तं यदा पापाद्विनिवर्त्तयितुं नृपः ॥
2.51.m: just as barley grains roasted in hot water become [parched], / when the king was unable to turn him back from evil,

2.51.s:
lokāpavādabhīrutvādviṣayānatyajattadā //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyamabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde sagaracarite 'samañjasatyāgo nāmaikapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ // 51//
2.51.d:
लोकापवादभीरुत्वाद्विषयानत्यजत्तदा ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यमभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे सगरचरिते ऽसमञ्जसत्यागो नामैकपञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ 51॥
2.51.m:
he then banished him from his territories out of fear of public reproach.

Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, named 'The Banishing of Asamañjasa,' in the story of Sagara, in the third [part], the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle section of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, spoken by Vāyu.

2.52.s:
jaiminiruvāca
tyaktvā putraṃ sa dharmātmā sagaraḥ prema tadgatam /
dharmaśīle tadā vāle cakārāṃśumati prabhuḥ //
2.52.d:
जैमिनिरुवाच
त्यक्त्वा पुत्रं स धर्मात्मा सगरः प्रेम तद्गतम् ।
धर्मशीले तदा वाले चकारांशुमति प्रभुः ॥
2.52.m: Jaimini said: / Having cast out his son, the righteous lord Sagara / directed that love toward the boy Aṃśumān, who was devoted to righteousness.

2.52.s:
etasminneva kāle tu sumatyāstanayā nṛpa /
vavṛdhuḥ saghaśaḥ sarve parasparamanuvratāḥ //
2.52.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सुमत्यास्तनया नृप ।
ववृधुः सघशः सर्वे परस्परमनुव्रताः ॥
2.52.m: At that very time, O king, the sons of Sumatī / all grew up in crowds, devoted to one another.

2.52.s:
vajrasaṃhananāḥ krūrā nirdayā nirapatrapāḥ /
adharmaśīlā nitarāmekagharmāṇa eva ca //
2.52.d:
वज्रसंहननाः क्रूरा निर्दया निरपत्रपाः ।
अधर्मशीला नितरामेकघर्माण एव च ॥
2.52.m: They had bodies like adamantine bolts; they were cruel, ruthless, shameless, / exceedingly unrighteous, and of a single disposition.

2.52.s:
ekakāryābhiniratāḥ krodhanā mūḍhacetasaḥ /
adhṛṣyāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ janopadravakāriṇaḥ //
2.52.d:
एककार्याभिनिरताः क्रोधना मूढचेतसः ।
अधृष्याः सर्वभूतानां जनोपद्रवकारिणः ॥
2.52.m: United in a single purpose, wrathful, dull-witted, / invincible to all beings, they caused distress to the people.

2.52.s:
vinayācā rasanmārganirapekṣāḥ samantataḥ /
babādhire jagatsarvamasurā iva kāmataḥ //
2.52.d:
विनयाचा रसन्मार्गनिरपेक्षाः समन्ततः ।
बबाधिरे जगत्सर्वमसुरा इव कामतः ॥
2.52.m: Disregarding discipline, proper conduct, and the good path on every side, / they harassed the entire world at their will, like asuras.

2.52.s:
vidhvastayajñasanmārgaṃ bhuvanaṃ tairupadrutam /
niḥsvādhyāya vaṣaṭkāraṃ babhūvārtaṃ viśeṣataḥ //
2.52.d:
विध्वस्तयज्ञसन्मार्गं भुवनं तैरुपद्रुतम् ।
निःस्वाध्याय वषट्कारं बभूवार्तं विशेषतः ॥
2.52.m: The world was afflicted by them, its sacrifices and good paths destroyed; / lacking private Vedic recitation and the vaṣaṭ-call, it was especially distressed.

2.52.s:
vidhvasyamāne subhṛśaṃ sāgarairvaradarpitaiḥ /
prakṣobhaṃ paramaṃ jagmurdevāsuramahoragāḥ //
2.52.d:
विध्वस्यमाने सुभृशं सागरैर्वरदर्पितैः ।
प्रक्षोभं परमं जग्मुर्देवासुरमहोरगाः ॥
2.52.m: As it was being violently devastated by the sons of Sagara haughty with boons, / the gods, asuras, and great serpents fell into the greatest agitation.

2.52.s:
dharāsā sāgarākrāntā na calāpi tadā calā /
tapaḥ samādhibhaṅgaśca prababhūva tapasvinām //
2.52.d:
धरासा सागराक्रान्ता न चलापि तदा चला ।
तपः समाधिभङ्गश्च प्रबभूव तपस्विनाम् ॥
2.52.m: The earth, overwhelmed by the sons of Sagara, became shaken though previously immovable; / and the break of ascetic practice and contemplation occurred for the ascetics.

2.52.s:
havyakavyaparibhraṣṭāstridaśāḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha /
duḥśena mahātāviṣṭā viriñjabhavanaṃ yayuḥ //
2.52.d:
हव्यकव्यपरिभ्रष्टास्त्रिदशाः पितृभिः सह ।
दुःशेन महाताविष्टा विरिञ्जभवनं ययुः ॥
2.52.m: Deprived of offerings to the gods and ancestors, the thirty [gods], along with the ancestors, / overcome with great sorrow, went to the abode of Viriñci.

2.52.s:
tatra gatvā yathānyāyaṃ devāḥ śarvapurogamāḥ /
śaśaṃsuḥ sakalaṃ tasmai sāgarāṇāṃ viceṣṭitam //
2.52.d:
तत्र गत्वा यथान्यायं देवाः शर्वपुरोगमाः ।
शशंसुः सकलं तस्मै सागराणां विचेष्टितम् ॥
2.52.m: Having gone there according to custom, the gods, with Śarva at their head, / related all the conduct of the sons of Sagara to him.

2.52.s:
tacchratvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ /
kṣaṇamantarmanā bhūtvā jagāda surasattamaḥ //
2.52.d:
तच्छ्रत्वा वचनं तेषां ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
क्षणमन्तर्मना भूत्वा जगाद सुरसत्तमः ॥
2.52.m: Having heard their words, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / became introspective for a moment and said to the best of the gods:

2.52.s:
